53: /// Run the unified hybrid search and hydrate results into full chunks.
54: ///
55: /// Always runs BM25; adds the `entity`/`vector` tiers according to `tier`.
56: /// When the query is a multi-word natural-language question that returns
57: /// nothing, a second OR-based BM25 pass recovers relevant chunks.
58: async fn hybrid_search(
59:     state: &AppState,
60:     buffer_id: i64,
61:     fts_query: &str,
62:     tier: HybridTier,
63:     top_k: usize,
64: ) -> anyhow::Result<Vec<arlm_search::SearchResult>> {
65:     let storage = state.storage.clone();

67:     let entity = EntitySearch::new(storage.clone()).ok();

69:         .vector_store

71:         .map(|v| SemanticSearch::new(v.clone()));

75:     // async worker, so run it on a blocking task. Falls back to BM25-only when

78:     let embedder = state.embedder.clone();

80:         .await
81:         .ok()
82:         .and_then(Result::ok);
83:     let query_vector = query_vector.as_deref();
84:     let options = SearchOptions {
85:         tier,

87:     };

124: /// Min-max normalise RRF fusion scores to `[0, 1]` (higher = better) so that
125: /// `--min-score` thresholds and downstream ranking remain meaningful.
126: fn normalize_scores(results: &mut [arlm_search::SearchResult]) {
127:     if results.is_empty() {
128:         return;
129:     }
130:     let min = results
131:         .iter()
132:         .map(|r| r.score)
133:         .fold(f32::INFINITY, f32::min);
134:     let max = results
135:         .iter()
136:         .map(|r| r.score)
137:         .fold(f32::NEG_INFINITY, f32::max);
138: 
139:     if (max - min).abs() < f32::EPSILON {
140:         for r in results.iter_mut() {
141:             r.score = 1.0;
142:         }
143:         return;
144:     }
145:     for r in results.iter_mut() {
146:         r.score = (r.score - min) / (max - min);
147:     }
148: }
149: 
150: /// Map hydrated `arlm_search` results into the gRPC `SearchResult` shape.
151: fn to_proto_results(results: &[arlm_search::SearchResult]) -> Vec<SearchResult> {
152:     results
153:         .iter()
154:         .map(|r| SearchResult {
155:             chunk_id: r.chunk_id,
156:             text: r.content.clone(),
157:             score: r.score,
158:             file_path: r.file_path.clone(),
159:             start_line: r.line_start as i32,
160:             end_line: r.line_end as i32,
161:             is_summary: r.is_summary,
162:             summary: None,
163:         })
164:         .collect()
165: }

167: /// Render hydrated chunks into the markdown-style LLM context with a token
168: /// budget. Returns the body and the number of tokens consumed.
169: fn render_context(candidates: &[SearchResult], max_tokens: u32) -> (String, u32) {
170:     let mut body = String::from("# Project Context\n\n");
171:     let mut budget: u32 = 0;
172:     for r in candidates {
173:         let tokens = (r.text.len() as u32).saturating_div(4);
174:         if tokens > 0 && budget + tokens > max_tokens {
175:             continue;
176:         }
177:         budget += tokens;
178:         let _ = write!(
179:             body,
180:             "## {} (score {:.2})\n```\n{}\n```\n\n",
181:             r.file_path, r.score, r.text
182:         );
183:     }
184:     (body, budget)
185: }

/// Scoped timing helper.
///
/// Logs the elapsed time of a code region on drop, with a structured
/// `timer` field so it can be filtered/aggregated in logs.
pub(crate) struct Timer {
    name: &'static str,
    start: std::time::Instant,
}

impl Timer {
    #[must_use]
    pub(crate) fn new(name: &'static str) -> Self {
        Self {
            name,
            start: std::time::Instant::now(),
        }
    }
}

impl Drop for Timer {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        let elapsed_ms = self.start.elapsed().as_millis();
        tracing::info!(timer = %self.name, elapsed_ms = elapsed_ms, "timing");
    }
}

pub struct ClientConfig {
    /// Server address (e.g., "127.0.0.1:50051" or "https://host:443").
    pub addr: String,

impl ClientConfig {
    /// Load client configuration from default locations.
    ///
    /// Resolution order:
    /// 1. .arlm/config.toml (local) — `server.addr`
    /// 2. ~/.arlm/config.toml (global) — `server.addr`
    /// 3. `ARLM_SERVER_ADDR` env var
    /// 4. Fallback: 127.0.0.1:50051
    #[must_use]
    pub fn load() -> Self {
        if let Some(addr) = read_server_addr_from_config() {
            return Self { addr };
        }

        // Try env var
        if let Ok(addr) = std::env::var("ARLM_SERVER_ADDR") {
            return Self { addr };
        }

        // Fallback
        Self {
            addr: "127.0.0.1:50051".to_string(),
        }
    }
}

/// Read the `[server] addr` value from the local/global config files.
#[must_use]
fn read_server_addr_from_config() -> Option<String> {
    // Try local config
    if let Ok(cwd) = std::env::current_dir() {
        let local_config = cwd.join(".arlm/config.toml");
        if let Some(addr) = read_addr_from_file(&local_config) {
            return Some(addr);
        }
    }

    // Try global config
    if let Some(home) = dirs() {
        let global_config = home.join(".arlm/config.toml");
        if let Some(addr) = read_addr_from_file(&global_config) {
            return Some(addr);
        }

{

  "content": "//! Question-vector index for the semantic query-answer cache (plan 017).\n//!\n//! This is a **dedicated** `usearch` index (`question_vectors`) in its own\n//! vector space, separate from the chunk vector store (`vector.usearch`). It\n//! holds the embedding of each cached *question* under the `cos` metric so that\n//! cache lookup by question similarity never mixes with chunk retrieval.\n//!\n//! Keys are the `qa_cache.id` rowids (`u64`), keeping a 1:1 logical mapping to\n//! `qa_cache`. The index is persisted next to the SQLite database and saved on\n//! every mutation.\n\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\n\nuse anyhow::{Context, Result};\nuse usearch::{Index, IndexOptions, MetricKind, ScalarKind};\n\nuse crate::sqlite::conn::Storage;\n\nconst DEFAULT_QUESTION_DIMS: usize = 1024;\nconst INDEX_FILE: &str = \"question_vectors.usearch\";\n\n/// A nearest neighbour of a question query, with cosine similarity in `[0, 1]`.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct QuestionNeighbor {\n    /// `qa_cache.id` of the matching cached question.\n    pub id: u64,\n    /// Cosine similarity to the query (clamped to `[0, 1]`).\n    pub similarity: f32,\n}\n\n/// `usearch` index of question embeddings (cosine metric).\npub struct QuestionVectorStore {\n    index: Index,\n    index_path: PathBuf,\n}\n\nimpl QuestionVectorStore {\n    /// Open (or create) the question index at `storage_path/question_vectors.usearch`.\n    ///\n    /// # Errors\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if the index file cannot be created or restored.\n    pub fn open(storage_path: &Path, dims: usize) -> Result<Self> {\n        let dims = if dims == 0 { DEFAULT_QUESTION_DIMS } else { dims };\n        std::fs::create_dir_all(storage_path).context(\"failed to create storage dir\")?;\n        let index_path = storage_path.join(INDEX_FILE);\n\n        let index = if index_path.exists() {\n            let path_str = index_path.to_str().context(\"non-utf8 index path\")?;\n            Index::restore(path_str)\n                .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"failed to restore question index: {e}\"))?\n        } else {\n            let opts = IndexOptions {\n                dimensions: dims,\n                metric: MetricKind::Cos,\n                quantization: ScalarKind::F32,\n                connectivity: 0,\n                expansion_add: 0,\n                expansion_search: 0,\n                ..Default::default()\n            };\n            Index::new(&opts).map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"failed to create question index: {e}\"))?\n        };\n\n        Ok(Self { index, index_path })\n    }\n\n    /// Build a store rooted alongside the given `Storage`'s directory.\n    ///\n    /// # Errors\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if the index cannot be opened.\n    pub fn open_for_storage(storage: &Storage, dims: usize) -> Result<Self> {\n        Self::open(storage.path(), dims)\n    }\n\n    /// The embedding dimensionality.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn dimensions(&self) -> usize {\n        self.index.dimensions()\n    }\n\n    /// Number of indexed questions.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn len(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.index.size()\n    }\n\n    /// Whether the index is empty.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.index.size() == 0\n    }\n\n    /// Insert or replace a question vector keyed by `qa_cache.id`.\n    ///\n    /// # Errors\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if the vector has the wrong dimensionality or the\n    /// insertion fails.\n    pub fn insert(&self, id: u64, vector: &[f32]) -> Result<()> {\n        let dims = self.index.dimensions();\n        if vector.len() != dims {\n            anyhow::bail!(\n                \"question vector dimension mismatch: expected {dims}, got {}\",\n                vector.len()\n            );\n        }\n        // usearch does not upsert; remove any prior key first.\n        let _ = self.index.remove(id);\n        self.index\n            .reserve(self.index.size() + 1)\n            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"failed to reserve question index capacity: {e}\"))?;\n        self.index\n            .add(id, vector)\n            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"failed to add question vector {id}: {e}\"))?;\n        self.save()\n    }\n\n    /// Remove a question vector by `qa_cache.id`.\n    ///\n    /// # Errors\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if the deletion or save fails.\n    pub fn delete(&self, id: u64) -> Result<()> {\n        let _ = self.index.remove(id);\n        self.save()\n    }\n\n    /// Search for the `limit` nearest questions, returning cosine similarity.\n    ///\n    /// # Errors\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if the search fails.\n    pub fn search(&self, query: &[f32], limit: usize) -> Result<Vec<QuestionNeighbor>> {\n        if self.is_empty() {\n            return Ok(Vec::new());\n        }\n        let matches = self\n            .index\n            .search(query, limit)\n            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"question vector search failed: {e}\"))?;\n        let out = matches\n            .keys\n            .iter()\n            .copied()\n            .zip(matches.distances.iter().copied())\n            .map(|(id, dist)| QuestionNeighbor {\n                id,\n                // `cos` metric returns cosine distance (1 - cos); clamp to [0, 1].\n                similarity: (1.0_f32 - dist).clamp(0.0, 1.0),\n            })\n            .collect();\n        Ok(out)\n    }\n\n    /// Drop the entire index (used by `prune-tokens`-style emergency wipes and\n    /// full-project cache invalidation).\n    ///\n    /// # Errors\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if the index cannot be reset.\n    pub fn clear(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        // Recreate an empty index at the same path.\n        let opts = IndexOptions {\n            dimensions: self.index.dimensions(),\n            metric: MetricKind::Cos,\n            quantization: ScalarKind::F32,\n            connectivity: 0,\n            expansion_add: 0,\n            expansion_search: 0,\n            ..Default::default()\n        };\n        let fresh = Index::new(&opts)\n            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"failed to reset question index: {e}\"))?;\n        self.index = fresh;\n        self.save()\n    }\n\n    fn save(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        let path_str = self.index_path.to_str().context(\"non-utf8 index path\")?;\n        self.index\n            .save(path_str)\n            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"failed to save question index: {e}\"))?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n"

  "content": "//! Similarity math for the semantic query-answer cache (plan 017).\n//!\n//! Cache lookup decides hit/miss/tier by question cosine similarity **plus** a\n//! secondary check that defeats false positives (e.g. \"login\" vs \"logout\" have\n//! nearby question vectors but disjoint provenance). These helpers are pure so\n//! they can be unit-tested without storage or an embedder.\n\n/// Cosine similarity of two vectors, clamped to `[-1, 1]`.\n///\n/// Returns `0.0` for zero vectors or mismatched lengths.\n#[must_use]\npub fn cosine_similarity(a: &[f32], b: &[f32]) -> f32 {\n    if a.len() != b.len() || a.is_empty() {\n        return 0.0;\n    }\n    let dot: f32 = a.iter().zip(b).map(|(x, y)| x * y).sum();\n    let na: f32 = a.iter().map(|x| x * x).sum::<f32>().sqrt();\n    let nb: f32 = b.iter().map(|x| x * x).sum::<f32>().sqrt();\n    if na == 0.0 || nb == 0.0 {\n        return 0.0;\n    }\n    (dot / (na * nb)).clamp(-1.0, 1.0)\n}\n\n/// Jaccard similarity of two string multisets, in `[0, 1]`:\n/// `|a ∩ b| / |a ∪ b|`. Used as the secondary check on provenance chunk ids.\n#[must_use]\npub fn jaccard_similarity(a: &[String], b: &[String]) -> f32 {\n    if a.is_empty() && b.is_empty() {\n        return 0.0;\n    }\n    let set_a: std::collections::HashSet<&str> = a.iter().map(String::as_str).collect();\n    let set_b: std::collections::HashSet<&str> = b.iter().map(String::as_str).collect();\n    let inter = set_a.intersection(&set_b).count();\n    let union = set_a.union(&set_b).count();\n    if union == 0 {\n        return 0.0;\n    }\n    inter as f32 / union as f32\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn cosine_identical_is_one() {\n        let v = vec![0.1, 0.2, -0.3, 0.4];\n        assert!((cosine_similarity(&v, &v) - 1.0).abs() < 1e-5);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn cosine_orthogonal_is_zero() {\n        assert!((cosine_similarity(&[1.0, 0.0], &[0.0, 1.0])).abs() < 1e-5);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn jaccard_half_overlap() {\n        let a = vec![\"c1\".into(), \"c2\".into(), \"c3\".into()];\n        let b = vec![\"c1\".into(), \"c2\".into(), \"c4\".into()];\n        assert!((jaccard_similarity(&a, &b) - 0.5).abs() < 1e-6);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn jaccard_disjoint_is_zero() {\n        let a = vec![\"c1\".into()];\n        let b = vec![\"c9\".into()];\n        assert_eq!(jaccard_similarity(&a, &b), 0.0);\n    }\n}\n"
}

This module is pure (no storage, no embedder) so it can be unit-tested and\n//! reused by both the server (lookup) and the client (digest-once).\n\nuse serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};\n\n/// Configurable thresholds for cache lookup and widening.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct QaThresholds {\n    /// Chunks digested on a brand-new question (client). Upper bound.\n    pub novel_k: usize,\n    /// Provenance chunks returned alongside a cached answer.\n    pub provenance_k: usize,\n    /// At/above this similarity a hit is a high-confidence near-exact match.\n    pub sim_high: f32,\n    /// Below this similarity the query is treated as brand new (full digest).\n    pub sim_floor: f32,\n    /// Descending similarity boundaries for widening tiers.\n    pub tier_steps: Vec<f32>,\n    /// Minimum provenance Jaccard for a hit to pass the secondary check.\n    pub jaccard_min: f32,\n}\n\nimpl Default for QaThresholds {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            novel_k: 20,\n            provenance_k: 5,\n            sim_high: 0.90,\n            sim_floor: 0.40,\n            tier_steps: vec![0.90, 0.80, 0.70, 0.60, 0.50],\n            jaccard_min: 0.5,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// A digest plan produced by [`resolve_plan`].\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct QaPlan {\n    /// Chunks the client should digest (`≤ novel_k`).\n    pub digest_k: usize,\n    /// Provenance chunks to return with the answer (`≤ digest_k`).\n    pub provenance_k: usize,\n    /// Whether this is a MISS (full fresh digest + new cache entry).\n    pub is_miss: bool,\n    /// Tier index: `-1` for miss, `0..=tier_steps.len()-1` for hits.\n    pub tier: i32,\n}\n\nimpl QaPlan {\n    /// Whether this is a high-confidence near-exact hit (top tier).\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn is_top_tier(&self) -> bool {\n        self.tier == 0\n    }\n}\n\n// Per-tier digest/provenance schedule (index aligns with `tier_steps`).\nconst DIGEST_SCHEDULE: [usize; 5] = [10, 12, 13, 15, 18];\nconst PROV_SCHEDULE: [usize; 5] = [5, 6, 7, 8, 10];\n\n/// Resolve a similarity + secondary-check Jaccard into a digest plan.\n///\n/// # Panics\n///\n/// Never panics; clamps gracefully when `tier_steps` is shorter than the\n/// schedule arrays.\n#[must_use]\npub fn resolve_plan(similarity: f32, jaccard: f32, t: &QaThresholds) -> QaPlan {\n    // Below the floor → brand new question.\n    if similarity < t.sim_floor {\n        return QaPlan {\n            digest_k: t.novel_k,\n            provenance_k: t.provenance_k,\n            is_miss: true,\n            tier: -1,\n        };\n    }\n\n    // Find the highest descending tier step the similarity still meets.\n    let tier_idx = t\n        .tier_steps\n        .iter()\n        .position(|&step| similarity >= step);\n\n    let tier_idx = match tier_idx {\n        Some(i) => i,\n        // Similarity is above the floor but below the lowest tier step:\n        // treat as a near-miss (full fresh digest).\n        None => {\n            return QaPlan {\n                digest_k: t.novel_k,\n                provenance_k: t.provenance_k,\n                is_miss: true,\n                tier: -1,\n            };\n        }\n    };\n\n    // Secondary check defeats false positives (e.g. \"login\" vs \"logout\").\n    if jaccard < t.jaccard_min {\n        return QaPlan {\n            digest_k: t.novel_k,\n            provenance_k: t.provenance_k,\n            is_miss: true,\n            tier: -1,\n        };\n    }\n\n    let digest_k = DIGEST_SCHEDULE\n        .get(tier_idx)\n        .copied()\n        .unwrap_or(t.novel_k)\n        .min(t.novel_k);\n    let provenance_k = PROV_SCHEDULE\n        .get(tier_idx)\n        .copied()\n        .unwrap_or(t.provenance_k)\n        .min(digest_k)\n        .max(1);\n\n    QaPlan {\n        digest_k,\n        provenance_k,\n        is_miss: false,\n        tier: i32::try_from(tier_idx).unwrap_or(-1),\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn miss_below_floor() {\n        let t = QaThresholds::default();\n        let p = resolve_plan(0.2, 0.0, &t);\n        assert!(p.is_miss);\n        assert_eq!(p.digest_k, t.novel_k);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn false_positive_blocked_by_jaccard() {\n        let t = QaThresholds::default();\n        // \"login\" vs \"logout\" can be cos-similar but disjoint provenance.\n        let p = resolve_plan(0.92, 0.1, &t);\n        assert!(p.is_miss);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn top_tier_hit() {\n        let t = QaThresholds::default();\n        let p = resolve_plan(0.95, 0.8, &t);\n        assert!(!p.is_miss);\n        assert!(p.is_top_tier());\n        assert_eq!(p.digest_k, 10);\n        assert_eq!(p.provenance_k, 5);\n        assert!(p.provenance_k <= p.digest_k);\n        assert!(p.digest_k <= t.novel_k);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn widening_lower_tier() {\n        let t = QaThresholds::default();\n        let p = resolve_plan(0.65, 0.6, &t);\n        assert!(!p.is_miss);\n        assert!(p.digest_k >= 10);\n        assert!(p.provenance_k <= p.digest_k);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn invariant_holds_at_every_tier() {\n        let t = QaThresholds::default();\n        for s in [0.50, 0.55, 0.62, 0.71, 0.83, 0.91, 0.99] {\n            let p = resolve_plan(s, 0.9, &t);\n            if !p.is_miss {\n                assert!(p.provenance_k <= p.digest_k);\n                assert!(p.digest_k <= t.novel_k);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n"
}

Empty = use `project` path.\n  string cache_id = 2;\n  // Invalidation mode for the `qa_cache` path.\n  InvalidateMode mode = 3;\n  // If set, also invalidate `qa_cache` entries whose question is within this\n  // cosine radius of the target (error-chain invalidation).\n  float similarity_radius = 4;\n}\n\nmessage InvalidateCacheResponse {\n  // Number of cache entries removed (qa_cache rows + question vectors).\n  int64 invalidated = 1;\n  // Username of the admin who triggered the invalidation (audit).\n  string invalidated_by = 2;\n}\n\n// Query the semantic cache. The server is deterministic: it embeds, searches\n// and decides hit/miss — it never runs an LLM. The client digests on a MISS.\nmessage QueryWithCacheRequest {\n  string project = 1;\n  string question = 2;\n  // Optional explicit buffer id (scoping). use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::Arc;

use anyhow::{Context, Result};
use arlm_proto::proto::arlm_service_client::ArlmServiceClient;
use arlm_proto::proto::arlm_service_server::ArlmServiceServer;
use arlm_storage::{Storage, VectorStore};
use tonic::transport::{Identity, Server, ServerTlsConfig};
use tracing::{info, warn};

use crate::config::ServerConfig;
use crate::grpc::ArlmGrpcService;
use crate::state::AppState;
use crate::timing::Timer;

/// Load config, open storage, wire the service and run the gRPC server.
///
/// Blocks until a shutdown signal is received.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// Returns an error if configuration, storage, the LLM backend or the server
/// setup fails.
pub async fn run() -> Result<()> {
    let _timer = Timer::new("server_startup");

    let config = ServerConfig::load().context("failed to load server config")?;

    info!(addr = %config.listen_addr, backend = %config.llm.backend, model = %config.llm.model, "starting arlm-server");

    // Single-mode storage: `arlm-storage`'s read paths (`get_chunk`,
    // `get_summary`, `search_summaries`, …) currently assume a single
    // connection via `Storage::conn()`. Opening single-mode keeps both the
    // `conn()`-based read helpers and the `connection()`-based pooled writes
    // (used by indexing) valid. Concurrent handlers serialize on the shared
    // connection mutex, which is acceptable for a local dev server.
    let storage = Storage::open(&config.data_dir).context("failed to open storage")?;

    let llm = AppState::build_llm(&config).context("failed to configure LLM backend")?;

    let vector_store = match VectorStore::open_with_dims(
        &config.data_dir,
        crate::state::embedder_dimension(),
    )
    .await
    {
        Ok(store) => Some(Arc::new(store)),
        Err(e) => {
            tracing::warn!(error = %e, "vector store unavailable, continuing without semantic search");
            None
        }
    };

    run_server(config, storage, llm, vector_store).await
}

/// Run the gRPC server with graceful shutdown.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// Returns an error if the server cannot be started or terminates uncleanly.
pub async fn run_server(
    config: ServerConfig,
    storage: Storage,
    llm: Arc<dyn arlm_llm::LlmBackend + Send + Sync>,
    vector_store: Option<Arc<VectorStore>>,
) -> Result<()> {
    let state = AppState::new(storage.clone(), config.clone(), llm, vector_store)?;

    let grpc_service = ArlmServiceServer::new(ArlmGrpcService::new(state));
    let addr = config
        .listen_addr
        .parse()
        .context("failed to parse listen address")?;

    let mut builder = Server::builder();

    if let (Some(cert), Some(key)) = (config.tls_cert(), config.tls_key()) {
        let identity = Identity::from_pem(&load_file(&cert)?, &load_file(&key)?);
        builder = builder.tls_config(ServerTlsConfig::new().identity(identity))?;
        info!(cert = %cert.display(), "gRPC server TLS enabled");
    } else {
        info!("gRPC server running without TLS (dev mode)");
    }

    info!(addr = %addr, "arlm-server listening");

    builder
        .add_service(grpc_service)
        .serve_with_shutdown(addr, shutdown_signal())
        .await?;

    info!("arlm-server shut down gracefully");
    Ok(())
}

fn load_file(path: &PathBuf) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
    std::fs::read(path).with_context(|| format!("failed to read TLS file {}", path.display()))
}

/// Query a running server's health over gRPC and print a summary.
///
/// Used by the `arlm-server status` subcommand (and the Docker HEALTHCHECK).
///
/// # Errors
///
/// Returns an error if the config cannot be loaded or the server is unreachable.
pub async fn status_check() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let config = ServerConfig::load().context("failed to load server config")?;
    let endpoint = format!("http://{}", config.listen_addr);

    let mut client = ArlmServiceClient::connect(endpoint)
        .await
        .context("failed to connect to arlm-server (is it running?)")?;

    let status = client
        .get_server_status(())
        .await
        .context("GetServerStatus RPC failed")?
        .into_inner();

    println!(
        "OK version={} uptime_s={} active_runs={} total_projects={} total_chunks={} total_summaries={}",
        status.version,
        status.uptime_seconds,
        status.active_runs,
        status.total_projects,
        status.total_chunks,
        status.total_summaries,
    );
    Ok(())
}

  "newString": "/// Fetch provenance chunks for a cached answer (top `k` by stored order).\nasync fn provenance_chunks(state: &AppState, ids: &[String], k: usize) -> Vec<SearchResult> {\n    let ids: Vec<i64> = ids.iter().filter_map(|s| s.parse::<i64>().ok()).collect();\n    if ids.is_empty() {\n        return Vec::new();\n    }\n    let taken: Vec<i64> = ids.iter().copied().take(k.max(1)).collect();\n    let chunks = store::blocking(move || {\n        let storage = state.storage.clone();\n        move || storage.get_chunks_with_content(&taken)\n    })\n    .await\n    .ok()\n    .unwrap_or_default();\n    chunks\n        .into_iter()\n        .map(|(c, content)| SearchResult {\n            chunk_id: c.id as u64,\n            text: content.unwrap_or_default(),\n            score: 1.0,\n            file_path: c.file_path,\n            start_line: c.line_start as i32,\n            end_line: c.line_end as i32,\n            is_summary: false,\n            summary: None,\n        })\n        .collect()\n}\n\n/// Top-K chunk ids from a hybrid search (for the secondary Jaccard check).\nasync fn top_chunk_ids(state: &AppState, _project: &str, question: &str, k: usize) -> Vec<String> {\n    // Best-effort; if search fails, an empty list yields a failing Jaccard and\n    // forces a MISS (safe default).\n    match hybrid_search(state, 0, &sanitize(question), arlm_search::SearchTier::Vector, k).await {\n        Ok(results) => results\n            .iter()\n            .map(|r| r.chunk_id.to_string())\n            .collect::<Vec<_>>(),\n        Err(_) => Vec::new(),\n    }\n}"

Errors\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if the queries fail.\n    pub fn invalidate_stale_cache_for_buffer(&self, buffer_id: i64) -> Result<usize> {\n        let current = self\n            .chunk_hashes_for_buffer(buffer_id)\n            .unwrap_or_default();\n        if current.is_empty() {\n            return Ok(0);\n        }\n        let rows = self.list_qa_hashes_for_buffer(buffer_id)?;\n        let mut n = 0;\n        for (id, hashes) in rows {\n            let missing = hashes.iter().any(|h| !current.contains(h));\n            if missing && self.mark_qa_stale(id, \"system\", \"chunk changed\")? {\n                n += 1;\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(n)\n    }\n}"

//! Client-side auth (plan 018).
//!
//! Wraps the generated gRPC client so every call automatically carries a
//! `Bearer` session token. The session token is obtained once from
//! `AuthRefresh` and proactively renewed on a background task (the refresh
//! token lives only in `config.toml`); the CLI user never manages it manually.

use std::str::FromStr;
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::time::Duration;

use anyhow::{Context, Result};
use parking_lot::Mutex;
use tokio::runtime::Runtime;
use tonic::metadata::MetadataValue;
use tonic::service::Interceptor;
use tonic::service::interceptor::InterceptedService;
use tonic::transport::Channel;
use tonic::{Request, Status};

use arlm_proto::proto::arlm_service_client::ArlmServiceClient;
use arlm_proto::proto::{AuthRefreshRequest, AuthRefreshResponse};

use crate::client::{self, ClientConfig};

/// Authenticated gRPC client type returned by [`connect`].
pub type ArlmClient = ArlmServiceClient<InterceptedService<Channel, BearerInterceptor>>;

/// Interceptor that attaches the current session token as a `Bearer` header.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct BearerInterceptor {
    token: Arc<Mutex<String>>,
}

impl Interceptor for BearerInterceptor {
    fn call(&mut self, mut req: Request<()>) -> Result<Request<()>, Status> {
        let token = self.token.lock().clone();
        if token.is_empty() {
            return Ok(req);
        }
        let value = MetadataValue::from_str(&format!("Bearer {token}"))
            .map_err(|_| Status::internal("invalid session token"))?;
        req.metadata_mut().insert("authorization", value);
        Ok(req)
    }
}

/// Connect to the server, performing `AuthRefresh` (if a refresh token is
/// configured) and returning a client that auto-attaches and renews the
/// session token.
///
/// When no `refresh_token` is configured the returned client sends no auth
/// header (the server will reject privileged RPCs with `UNAUTHENTICATED`).
///
/// # Errors
///
/// Returns an error if the channel cannot be established or the initial
/// `AuthRefresh` fails.
pub fn connect(
    rt: &Runtime,
    client_config: &ClientConfig,
    auth: &crate::config::AuthConfig,
) -> Result<ArlmClient> {
    let channel = rt
        .block_on(client::connect_channel(client_config))
        .context("failed to connect to arlm-server")?;

    let token = Arc::new(Mutex::new(String::new()));

    if let Some(refresh) = &auth.refresh_token {
        let refresh = refresh.clone();

        let mut refresh_client = ArlmServiceClient::new(channel.clone());
        let session: AuthRefreshResponse = rt
            .block_on(refresh_client.auth_refresh(AuthRefreshRequest {
                refresh_token: refresh.clone(),
            }))
            .context("AuthRefresh failed")?
            .into_inner();
        *token.lock() = session.session_token;

```

use std::path::PathBuf;

use clap::Parser;

use super::commands::Commands;

/// Output format selected on the command line.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, clap::ValueEnum)]
pub enum OutputFormatArg {
    #[value(name = "full_json")]
    FullJson,
    #[value(name = "path")]
    Path,
    #[value(name = "markdown")]
    Markdown,
    /// `text` is the agent-facing prompt context format (formerly `prompt`).
    #[value(name = "text")]
    Text,
    #[value(name = "jsonl")]
    Jsonl,
}

/// arlm command-line interface.
#[derive(Parser, Debug)]
#[command(
    name = "arlm",
    about = "Agnostic RLM — Recursive Language Model CLI",
    version
)]
pub struct Cli {
    #[command(subcommand)]
    pub command: Commands,

    /// Enable verbose output with structured logging
    #[arg(short, long, global = true)]
    pub verbose: bool,

    /// Output format: full_json, path, markdown, text, jsonl
    ///
    /// `path` prints the relative file path (human tree for search). `text`
    /// renders the agent-facing prompt context. `jsonl` (default for
    /// search/context/query) emits a single `{"query":..,"results":[{"file","text"}]}`
    /// object so an AI can consume only the needed content.
    #[arg(short, long, global = true)]
    pub format: Option<OutputFormatArg>,

    /// Project path
    #[arg(short, long, global = true)]
    pub project: Option<PathBuf>,

    /// Config file path (default: ~/.arlm/config.toml)
    #[arg(long, global = true)]
    pub config: Option<PathBuf>,

    /// LLM backend (overrides config)
    #[arg(long, global = true)]
    pub backend: Option<String>,

    /// Model name (overrides config)
    #[arg(long, global = true)]
    pub model: Option<String>,

    /// Agent name (overrides config)
    #[arg(long, global = true)]
    pub agent: Option<String>,

    /// Connect to a running arlm-server instead of running locally
    #[arg(long, global = true)]
    pub server: Option<String>,
}

/// Parse a `--tool` argument in format "name:description" or
/// "name:param1,param2:description".
#[must_use]
pub fn parse_tool_arg(arg: &str) -> Option<arlm_core::CustomTool> {
    let (name_part, description) = arg.split_once(':')?;
    let name = name_part.trim().to_string();
    let description = description.trim().to_string();
    if name.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    Some(arlm_core::CustomTool::function(&name, &description))
}

## Objective
- Implement plan 017 (`plan/017-query-answer-cache.md` — Semantic Query-Answer Cache, digest-once on client) using `sd` for task tracking, reviewing carefully with the precondition that plan 018 (`plan/018-auth-token-management.md`) is already fully implemented (auth/admin-gating confirmed present in code).

## Important Details
- Plan 018 is implemented: `arlm-server/src/auth/mod.rs` (`authenticate`, `require_admin`, `Role`), `arlm-storage/src/sqlite/tokens.rs` (tables `auth_tokens`/`auth_sessions`), `arlm-server/src/grpc/query_cache.rs` already had `handle_invalidate_cache` gated by admin but operating on legacy `result_cache` via `arlm_storage::cache::invalidate_cache`.
- **Reconciliation decision:** 018 `InvalidateCache` kept backward-compatible. When `cache_id` empty → legacy `result_cache` purge (018 path). When `cache_id` set → `qa_cache` (017 path) with `mode` (Stale/Delete) + `similarity_radius` over `question_vectors`. This preserves 018's existing tests.
- Question vectors use `usearch` **Cos** metric in a dedicated index (`qa_vectors.rs`), keyed by `qa_cache.id` (u64), separate from chunk `VectorStore` (L2). Opened with `crate::state::embedder_dimension()` (not `qa_config.question_vector_dims`) to match the chunk embedder.
- `chunk_content_hash` is sha256 hex (matches `indexing.rs` `hash_text`) — clients send `source_hashes` computed this way so the server staleness hook can compare against stored chunk hashes.
- Reserve lock implemented as idempotent upsert in `store_answer` (same `project`+`question_hash` reuses `cache_id`).
- Question prefix `QUESTION_PREFIX = "search_query: "` applied by server when embedding questions (both at store and query time).
- `QaThresholds` defaults: `novel_k=20, provenance_k=5, sim_high=0.90, sim_floor=0.40, tier_steps=[0.90,0.80,0.70,0.60,0.50], jaccard_min=0.5`. `DIGEST_SCHEDULE=[10,12,13,15,18]`, `PROV_SCHEDULE=[5,6,7,8,10]`.
- `AppState::new` signature changed to 5 args (added `question_vector_store: Option<Arc<QuestionVectorStore>>`). All call sites updated (lifecycle.rs, query_cache.rs test).

1: # Plan 017: Semantic Query-Answer Cache (Digestão sob Demanda, no Client)
2: 
3: ## Context
4: 
5: O summarizer hierárquico atual (`file → module → project`) é uma **agregação pré-computada e estática** que não faz sentido para desenvolvimento iterativo:
6: 
7: - `Summarizer::summarize` (`crates/arlm-server/src/summarizer/engine.rs:53`) recarrega **todos** os chunks do buffer e re-sumariza **todo** o projeto a cada rodada de `summarize`, incondicionalmente.
8: - `insert_summary` (`crates/arlm-server/src/store/summaries.rs:90`) é um `INSERT` puro, sem `ON CONFLICT` → rodar duas vezes **duplica** linhas.
9: - `estimate_incremental_cost` (`crates/arlm-server/src/summarizer/cost.rs:55`) existe mas **nunca é chamado** → o caminho incremental foi planejado e não conectado.
10: - O servidor carrega `LlmBackend` **só** para sumarizar (`engine.rs:243`), duplicando o LLM que o agente consumidor (Continue/Aider/Cline) já possui.
11: 
12: Este plano substitui a hierarquia estática por um **cache semântico de respostas digeridas na hora da query**, com duas decisões de arquitetura:
13: 
14: 1. **A digestão (síntese por LLM) roda no CLIENT**, usando o LLM do próprio usuário (configurado em `~/.arlm/config.toml` via `arlm-llm`). O servidor **não aciona nenhum LLM** — ele apenas armazena e processa **deterministicamente** (embedding, FTS, hashes, RRF).
15: 2. **O armazenamento vetorial usa `usearch`** (HNSW single-file, mais enxuto e plenamente capaz para o escopo; o projeto migrou do LanceDB para o usearch).
16: 
17: Isso descentraliza custo/modelo, mantém o servidor enxuto e é coerente com o princípio "agent-agnostic" do projeto. A digestão sob demanda é a materialização do padrão do `rlm_guide` (Sub-LLM digere chunks *pela necessidade de informação*), agora no client.
18: 
19: Este plano **já incorpora as correções** discutidas:
20: 
21: 1. **Versionamento / invalidação** por mudança de código (senão o cache mente após refatorações).
22: 2. **Resolução do cosseno** (similaridade de pergunta é proxy fraco; evitar falso-positivo tipo "login" vs "logout").
23: 3. **Thresholds flexíveis/configuráveis**.
24: 4. **Eviction razoável**.
25: 5. **Provenance** obrigatória (chunk_ids que geraram a resposta).
26: 6. **5 pontos de atenção** do design client-side (ver seção dedicada).
27: 
28: ---
29: 
30: ## Goals
31: 
32: - Servidor **sem LLM**: só embedding + SQLite + `usearch` + ops determinísticas.
33: - Pagar 1 digestão por **pergunta nova**, no client do usuário; amortizar nas repetidas/próximas.
34: - Redução de contexto **monótona e limitada** (`trechos_na_resposta ≤ trechos_novelos`).
35: - Respostas em cache **nunca stale** após mudança de código (invalidação por hash de chunk).
36: - Falso-positivo de cache minimizado (checagem secundária além do cosseno de pergunta).
37: - Tudo configurável (limiares, dimensões, política de eviction) sem rebuild.
38: 
39: ## Non-goals
40: 
41: - Não elimina a busca híbrida (BM25 + semântica) — o cache **consome** o resultado dela.
42: - Não roda LLM no servidor (removido o `LlmBackend` de summarization do server).
43: - Não substitui embeddings de chunk; usa um **espaço vetorial separado** (`usearch`) para perguntas.
44: 
45: ---
46: 
47: ## Architecture Overview
48: 
49: ```
50: ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
51: │  Client (arlm-cli) — USA O LLM DO USUÁRIO (config.toml)        │
52: │                                                                │
53: │  1. QueryWithCache(pergunta, project)  ──gRPC──►  Server       │
54: │  6. ◄── HIT: answer+provenance  (0 LLM no client)              │
55: │       ◄── MISS: top-K chunks crus                             │
56: │  4. [MISS] 1 chamada LLM sintetiza top-K → answer             │
57: │  5. exibe answer ao usuário (UX imediata)                      │
58: │  7. StoreAnswer(answer, provenance, source_hashes) fire-forget│
59: └───────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┘
60:                             │
61:                             ▼  (server = DETERMINÍSTICO, sem LLM)
62: ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
63: │  arlm-server                                                   │
64: │  • embed(query) + HybridSearch (BM25+entity+vector) → top-K    │
65: │  • embed(pergunta) espaço B (usearch question_vectors)         │
66: │  • lookup cache (cosseno + checagem secundária) → tier         │
67: │  • StoreAnswer: FTS do answer + grava qa_cache + marca stale   │
68: │  • RRF funde cache + chunks                                    │
69: └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
70: ```
71: 
72: ---
73: 
74: ## Data Model
75: 
76: ### Tabela `qa_cache` (SQLite, `arlm-storage`)
77: 
78: | Coluna | Tipo | Papel |
79: |---|---|---|
80: | `id` | INTEGER PK | |
81: | `cache_id` | TEXT (UUIDv7, unique) | **ID estável da resposta**, propagável p/ sub-agentes (anti-drift) |
82: | `buffer_id` | INTEGER | scoping por projeto/buffer |
83: | `project` | TEXT | redundância p/ lookup rápido |
84: | `question_text` | TEXT | texto original da pergunta |
85: | `question_hash` | TEXT | hit exato (mesma pergunta, mesmo buffer) |
86: | `answer_text` | TEXT | resposta digerida (cache, vinda do client) |
87: | `source_chunk_ids` | TEXT (JSON) | **provenance**: chunk_ids usados |
88: | `source_hashes` | TEXT (JSON) | **invalidation**: hashes dos chunks |
89: | `model` | TEXT | **metadado** do LLM que sintetizou (não bloqueia reuso) |
90: | `confidence` | REAL | decai se algum chunk ficar stale |
91: | `tier_snapshot` | TEXT (JSON) | limiares usados (reprodutibilidade) |
92: | `token_count` | INTEGER | custo da resposta |
93: | `access_count` | INTEGER | p/ eviction ponderado |
94: | `created_at` | INTEGER | epoch ms |
95: | `last_accessed_at` | INTEGER | epoch ms (LRU) |
96: | `stale` | INTEGER (bool) | marcado por invalidação |
97: | `invalidated_at` | INTEGER | epoch ms da invalidação manual (audit) |
98: | `invalidated_by` | TEXT | quem invalidou (audit) |
99: | `invalidated_reason` | TEXT | motivo (ex: alucinação) |
100: 
101: FTS5 opcional sobre `question_text` (e/ou `answer_text`) para busca lexical de cache.
102: 
103: ### Espaço vetorial separado (perguntas) — `usearch`
104: 
105: - **Novo** índice `question_vectors` (`usearch`, HNSW single-file), **distinto** do `chunk_vectors`.
106: - Dimensões configuráveis (`question_vector_dims`), reusando o embedder do servidor com prefixo de task (`search_query: `) — mas **nunca** misturado ao espaço de chunk.
107: - Chave estrangeira lógica `question_vectors.id → qa_cache.id`.
108: 
109: ## Query Flow (client-centric, com thresholds configuráveis)
110: 
111: Parâmetros default (todos sobrescrevíveis em config):
112: 
113: | Parâmetro | Default | Significado |
114: |---|---|---|
115: | `novel_k` | 20 | trechos digeridos numa pergunta nova (client) |
116: | `provenance_k` | 5 | trechos devolvidos junto da resposta em cache |
117: | `sim_high` | 0.90 | acima disso → reaproveita resposta + re-digest leve |
118: | `sim_floor` | 0.40 | abaixo disso → trata como nova (digest completo) |
119: | `tier_steps` | [0.90, 0.80, 0.70, 0.60, 0.50] | fronteiras de widen |
120: 
121: Fluxo no client:
122: 
123: 1. Cliente chama `QueryWithCache(pergunta, project)` no server.
124: 2. Server (determinístico): embed(query) + HybridSearch → top-K; embed(pergunta) espaço B; lookup cache → decide `s` (similaridade) e tier.
125: 3. Server responde:
126:    - **HIT exato / tier alto**: `answer_text` + top `provenance_k` trechos de provenance. Cliente **não chama LLM** (0 custo).
127:    - **MISS / tier baixo**: top-K chunks crus. Cliente faz **1 chamada LLM** sintetizando → `answer`, exibe ao usuário, e dispara `StoreAnswer` (fire-and-forget).
128: 4. Comportamento por tier (`s` após checagem secundária):
129:    - `s ≥ sim_high`: re-digere 10 trechos, devolve `answer + 5`, atualiza cache.
130:    - `0.80 ≥ s > sim_high`… descendo: digere 10→15, devolve 5→10 conforme `tier_steps`.
131:    - `s < sim_floor`: MISS → digest completo (`novel_k`=20), persiste nova entrada.
132: 5. **Invariante de redução:** `trechos_na_resposta ≤ trechos_novelos (20)` em todos os tiers.
133: 
134: ---
135: 
136: ## Escopo por projeto e reserve lock (multi-dev / multi-projeto)
137: 
138: Cenário alvo: vários devs no **mesmo** projeto; 1 dev em **vários** projetos. Regras:
139: 
140: - **Conhecimento é escopado no PROJETO** (`buffer_id`/`project`). Não há compartilhamento de cache entre projetos diferentes.
141: - **Mesma pergunta, mesmo projeto, devs diferentes → preserva-se o 1º.** O primeiro digest vence; os demais reutilizam a entrada (hit). A chave de cache é `(project, question_hash)`.
142: - **Mesma pergunta, projetos diferentes → regra independente.** Cada projeto tem sua própria entrada (próprio `cache_id`); sem cross-contaminação.
143: - **Reserve lock:** no MISS, o server reserva `(project, question_hash)` *antes* de disparar a digestão no client, para que requisições concorrentes idênticas (mesmo projeto) não geram digests duplicados — elas aguardam/retornam o mesmo `cache_id`. O lock é por projeto, então não bloqueia perguntas em outros projetos.
144: - `GetAnswerById` também é escopado por projeto (`cache_id` + `project`/`buffer_id`).
145: 
146: ---
147: 
148: ## Similarity Resolution (correção do cosseno)
149: 
150: Cosseno de pergunta é necessário mas **insuficiente** (falso-positivo: "onde é login?" ≈ "onde é logout?"). Pipeline (lado server, determinístico exceto a comparação de vetores):
151: 
152: 1. `embed(pergunta)` no espaço B (`usearch`) → busca k candidatos (`sim ≥ sim_floor`).
153: 2. **Checagem secundária** para o melhor candidato:
154:    - **Overlap de snippet-set:** Jaccard entre os `top-K` chunks da nova query e os `source_chunk_ids` do cache. Se `J ≥ 0.5` → mesmo *information need* confirmado.
155:    - **Ou** re-embed da `answer_text` do cache vs embed da nova pergunta; se cosseno alto, confirma.
156: 3. Só se (1) **e** (2) passarem é que conta como HIT/tier. Caso contrário → MISS (digest novo no client).
157: 
158: ---
159: 
160: ## Invalidation (correção de staleness)
161: 
162: Cada entrada guarda `source_hashes` (hash de conteúdo de cada chunk usado).
163: 
164: - No `reindex`/`lifecycle` (`crates/arlm-server/src/lifecycle.rs`), após atualizar chunks, computa-se o diff de hashes por buffer (determinístico, server-side).
165: - Toda entrada de `qa_cache` cujo `source_hashes` contiver **qualquer** chunk que mudou/sumiu → marcada `stale=1` e `confidence=0`.
166: - Hit em entrada stale força **re-digest completo** no client (trata como MISS), regenerando a resposta com chunks frescos.
167: - Garante que, após refatoração de 5k linhas, respostas afetadas são automaticamente invalidadas.
168: 
169: ---
170: 
171: ## Eviction (política razoável)
172: 
173: - **LRU ponderado**: `score = access_count / (1 + (now - last_accessed_at)/λ)`; remove os piores quando `count > max_entries_per_project`.
174: - **TTL opcional**: entradas com `last_accessed_at` mais antigo que `cache_ttl_ms` expiram.
175: - Roda em background (worker) ou no acesso, com batch `DELETE`.
176: 
177: ---
178: 
179: ## Provenance
180: 
181: - `source_chunk_ids` + `file_path` devolvidos junto da resposta para o agente consumidor poder (a) fundamentar e (b) permitir invalidação.
182: - No `build_context`/`build_search_results` (`crates/arlm-search/src/context.rs`), entradas de cache são resolvidas como `is_cache_answer` para montar o prompt.
183: 
184: ---
185: 
186: ## Resposta com ID estável e lookup direto (anti-drift)
187: 
188: Toda resposta servida recebe um **`cache_id` (UUIDv7)** no momento da criação (no `StoreAnswer`, server-side, via `uuid::Uuid::now_v7()` — padrão do projeto, ver `crates/arlm-server/src/grpc/summarize.rs:27`). O `cache_id` é **distinto do `id` (rowid)** e é o identificador estável da resposta.
189: 
190: ### Por quê
191: 
192: Um agente orquestrador (Root LLM) faz a consulta, recebe a resposta **+ `cache_id`**, e pode repassar esse ID a um **sub-agente**. O sub-agente aciona o lookup direto e recebe **exatamente o mesmo contexto (answer + provenance)**, sem re-digestão e sem deriva semântica (drift) causada por nova busca híbrida ou nova síntese LLM.
193: 
194: ### Regras
195: 
196: 1. **Todo served response inclui `cache_id`**, independente do formato de output (Prompt/Json/Markdown) e independente de ser HIT ou MISS (no MISS, o `StoreAnswer` retorna o `cache_id` recém-criado ao client).
197: 2. **Lookup direto (`GetAnswerById`)**: RPC que recebe `cache_id` (+ `buffer_id`/`project` p/ escopo) e devolve `answer_text` + `source_chunk_ids` + `cache_id` **1:1**, **sem** tocar em indexação, embedding, busca híbrida ou LLM. É o caminho de "contexto determinístico e reproduzível".
198: 3. O CLI expõe esse lookup direto (ex: `arlm query --cache-id <uuidv7>`), que **não passa** pelo sistema de index/retrieval — apenas retorna a resposta salva.
199: 4. `GetAnswerById` também serve para o orquestrador re-obter sua própria resposta sem custo.
200: 
201: ---
202: 
203: ## Invalidação manual (reset de resposta e cadeia de erros)
204: 
205: Cenário: um dev alucina ao sumarizar "como proteger senhas?"; a resposta vira bug conceitual. Por ser recente/relevante, vários devs fazem perguntas próximas e o fluxo leva ao mesmo bug. Um sênior deve poder **forçar o reset** daquela resposta e das próximas a ela, invalidando a cadeia de erros.
206: 
207: ### Mecanismo
208: 
209: - RPC `InvalidateCache`:
210:   - `cache_id` (alvo).
211:   - `mode`: `Stale` (soft — marca `stale=1`, `confidence=0`, preenche `invalidated_at/by/reason`) ou `Delete` (hard — remove a linha de `qa_cache` + o vetor em `question_vectors`).
212:   - `similarity_radius`: `Option<f32>`. Se presente, além do alvo, **invalida também as entradas cuja pergunta está dentro do raio de similaridade** no espaço `question_vectors` (reusa o próprio índice `usearch` para achar vizinhos — a "cadeia de erros"). Default sugerido `0.85`.
213: - Após `Stale`, a próxima query que der hit naquela (ou vizinha) entrada **força re-digest** (tratada como MISS) → resposta fresca, corrigindo o bug sem apagar o histórico (auditável).
214: - `Delete` remove de vez (sem trilha, exceto log do server).
215: 
216: ### CLI
217: 
218: `arlm cache invalidate --cache-id <uuidv7> [--radius 0.85] [--delete] [--reason "alucinacao"]`
219: 
220: ### Privilégio
221: 
222: Em time fechado, qualquer client pode invalidar. Em multi-user restrito (plan 015), deve ser **opção privilegiada** (role sênior) — conecta com o ponto de atenção 3 (trust/poisoning).
223: 
224: ---
225: 
226: ## Resolução dos 5 pontos de atenção (design client-side)
227: 
228: | # | Ponto | Resolução planejada |
229: |---|-------|---------------------|
230: | 1 | **Provenance no store RPC** | `StoreAnswer` (server) recebe `source_chunk_ids` + `source_hashes` do client e persiste em `qa_cache`; sem isso a invalidação (item 3) quebra. Implementado em `grpc/query_cache.rs` + `store/qa_cache.rs`. |
231: | 2 | **Race de digest duplicado** | Resolvido por **reserve lock** no server, chave `(project, question_hash)`: no MISS o server reserva antes de disparar a digestão, e requisições concorrentes idênticas (mesmo projeto) reutilizam o mesmo `cache_id`. O lock é por projeto → não bloqueia outros projetos. Cross-project a pergunta é independente (regra própria). |
232: | 3 | **Trust / poisoning em multi-user** | Server armazena cegamente o que o client manda → risco de envenenamento em multi-user. Single-user local: OK. Multi-user (roadmap plan 015): exige auth + validação/quotas. Fora de escopo deste plano; referenciado. |
233: | 4 | **Model-specific** | **Removido como bloqueador.** `qa_cache.model` guarda metadado do LLM que sintetizou, mas **não impede** reuso da informação entre os modelos da equipe — a resposta é servida a qualquer client independente do modelo. |
234: | 5 | **Fire-and-forget no envio ao server** | Cliente exibe a resposta imediatamente; o `StoreAnswer` roda em background/`spawn_blocking` sem bloquear a UX do usuário. |
235: 
236: ---
237: 
238: ## Where to Implement
239: 
240: | Componente | Crate | Arquivo(s) |
241: |---|---|---|
242: | Schema `qa_cache` + FTS + `usearch` `question_vectors` + `evict()` | `arlm-storage` | `src/store/qa_cache.rs` (novo) + migração |
243: | Embed de pergunta (prefixo task, espaço B) | `arlm-embedding` | `embedder/mod.rs` (`embed_query`) |
244: | Lookup + checagem secundária | `arlm-search` | `src/qa_cache.rs` (novo) |
245: | Engine de widening adaptativo | `arlm-core` | `src/qa_cache/mod.rs` (novo) |
246: | **Digest-once (LLM) — CLIENT** | `arlm-cli` (via `arlm-llm` + `config.toml`) | `src/commands/query_cache.rs` (novo) |
247: | Invalidation no reindex (determinístico) | `arlm-server` | `lifecycle.rs` + hook pós-index |
248: | Eviction | `arlm-storage` | `src/store/qa_cache.rs` (`evict`) |
249: | `StoreAnswer` RPC (server, determinístico) | `arlm-proto`, `arlm-server` | `proto/arlm.proto`, `grpc/query_cache.rs` |
250: | Config (thresholds/dims/eviction) | `arlm-server` + `arlm-cli` | `config.rs` (`QaCacheConfig`) + user LLM config |
251: | `GetAnswerById` (lookup direto 1:1, anti-drift) | `arlm-proto`, `arlm-server`, `arlm-cli` | `proto/arlm.proto`, `grpc/query_cache.rs`, `cli/commands.rs` (`--cache-id`) |
252: | `InvalidateCache` (reset manual: single + cluster por raio) | `arlm-proto`, `arlm-server`, `arlm-cli` | `proto/arlm.proto`, `grpc/query_cache.rs` (Stale/Delete + `similarity_radius` via `usearch`), `cli/commands.rs` (`cache invalidate`) |
253: | Testes/bench | `tests/`, `benches/` | `qa_cache_test.rs`, `qa_cache_bench.rs` |
254: 
255: > Nota: o servidor **não** precisa de `LlmBackend` para este fluxo. O `arlm-server/src/summarizer/` torna-se obsoleto para o cache (pode ser mantido como legado ou removido).
256: 
257: ---
258: 
259: ## Implementation Steps (milestones)
260: 
261: 1. **Storage**: `qa_cache` + `usearch question_vectors` + migração + `evict()`.
262: 2. **Embedding**: `embed_query` com prefixo de task no espaço B.
263: 3. **Lookup**: busca por cosseno + checagem secundária (Jaccard/overlap).
264: 4. **Adaptive engine**: mapear `s` → tier → `(digest_k, provenance_k)`.
265: 5. **Digest-once (CLIENT)**: síntese LLM de top-K (usa `arlm-llm` + config.toml) → `answer` + provenance + hashes; exibe e dispara `StoreAnswer` fire-and-forget.
266: 6. **Invalidation**: hook em `lifecycle` pós-reindex marcando `stale`.
267: 7. **Eviction**: LRU ponderado em background.
268: 8. **Config**: `QaCacheConfig` + LLM do usuário no client.
269: 9. **Wiring**: RPC `QueryWithCache` + `StoreAnswer` (server) + cliente CLI orquestrando.
270: 10. **Tests/Bench**: corretude de hit/miss/tier, invalidação, eviction, redução de contexto.
271: 
272: ---
273: 
274: ## Testing & Benchmarks
275: 
276: - `test_qa_cache_exact_hit_zero_llm_calls` (client não chama LLM).
277: - `test_qa_cache_near_hit_widens_context` (verifica tier → k).
278: - `test_qa_cache_false_positive_login_vs_logout` (checagem secundária bloqueia).
279: - `test_qa_cache_invalidated_after_chunk_hash_change` (stale → re-digest no client).
280: - `test_qa_cache_eviction_lru` (cap respeitado).
281: - `test_qa_cache_store_fire_and_forget` (resposta exibida antes do save completar).
282: - `test_qa_cache_id_emitted_in_all_formats` (Prompt/Json/Markdown incluem `cache_id`).
283: - `test_qa_cache_get_by_id_returns_identical_1to1` (lookup direto ignora index/busca/LLM e devolve exatamente a mesma resposta+provenance).
284: - `test_qa_cache_scoped_per_project` (mesma pergunta em projetos A e B gera entradas independentes, `cache_id` distintos, sem cross-contaminação).
285: - `test_qa_cache_reserve_lock_dedupes_same_project` (MISS concorrente idêntico no mesmo projeto → 1 digest, mesmo `cache_id` p/ todos; lock não afeta outros projetos).
286: - `test_qa_cache_invalidate_single_marks_stale_forces_redigest` (Stale faz re-digest na próxima query).
287: - `test_qa_cache_invalidate_cluster_by_radius` (raio invalida perguntas vizinhas no espaço `question_vectors`).
288: - `test_qa_cache_invalidate_delete_removes_entry_and_vector`.
289: - Bench: latência de cache hit vs digest novo; redução de tokens na resposta.
290: 
291: ---
292: 
293: ## Risks
294: 
295: | Risco | Mitigação |
296: |---|---|
297: | Embed de pergunta com prefixo errado polui retrieval | usar espaço B dedicado + prefixo `search_query:` validado |
298: | Checagem secundária cara | só roda sobre k candidatos (≤10) |
299: | Eviction agressiva apaga cache útil | peso por `access_count` + TTL generoso default |
300: | Resposta cacheada grande em tokens | `token_count` no budget do contexto |
301: | Drift do embedder (troca de modelo) | versionar `embedding_model` na entrada; invalidar em troca |
302: | Poisoning em multi-user | auth/validação (plan 015); single-user local OK |
303: | Race de digest duplicado | custo client-side aceitável; reserve lock opcional |
304:

#![allow(
    clippy::unwrap_used,
    clippy::expect_used,
    clippy::panic,
    clippy::pedantic

//! Integration tests for the typed store layer (`arlm_server::store`).
//!
//! Storage is opened in single-connection mode (SQLite in a temp dir) so the
//! tests are fast and hermetic; the same functions are used by the server's
//! pooled mode.

use arlm_server::store;
use arlm_storage::Storage;
use tempfile::TempDir;

fn setup() -> (Storage, TempDir) {
    let dir = TempDir::new().expect("tempdir");
    // Single-header DB at a fixed path.
    let storage = Storage::open(dir.path()).expect("open storage");
    (storage, dir)
}

// ── Projects ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

#[test]
fn test_insert_and_get_project_by_name() {
    let (storage, _dir) = setup();
    let id = store::insert_project(&storage, "my-project", "/path/to/project").unwrap();
    assert!(id > 0);

    let row = store::get_project_by_name(&storage, "my-project")
        .unwrap()
        .expect("project exists");
    assert_eq!(row.id, id);
    assert_eq!(row.path, "/path/to/project");
    assert!(row.uuid.is_some());
}

#[test]
fn test_get_project_by_uuid() {
    let (storage, _dir) = setup();
    store::insert_project(&storage, "p1", "/p1").unwrap();

    let by_name = store::get_project_by_name(&storage, "p1").unwrap().unwrap();
    let by_uuid = store::get_project_by_uuid(&storage, by_name.uuid.as_deref().unwrap())
        .unwrap()
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(by_uuid.id, by_name.id);
}

#[test]
fn test_list_projects() {
    let (storage, _dir) = setup();
    for i in 0..3 {
        store::insert_project(&storage, &format!("proj-{i}"), &format!("/p{i}")).unwrap();
    }
    let projects = store::list_projects(&storage).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(projects.len(), 3);

```

//! Semantic query-answer cache persistence (plan 017).
//!
//! The server stores *digested* answers here (synthesized client-side). Lookup
//! by `(project, question_hash)` gives exact hits; similarity hits are resolved
//! by the caller against the dedicated `question_vectors` index
//! (`crate::qa_vectors`). `source_hashes` drive staleness: when a source chunk
//! changes, the lifecycle hook marks the row `stale` so the next query forces a
//! re-digest.
//!
//! All queries go through [`super::conn::Storage::connection`], which is safe in
//! both single (CLI) and pooled (server) modes.

use anyhow::{Context, Result};
use rusqlite::OptionalExtension;
use rusqlite::params;

use super::conn::Storage;
use super::tokens::now_ms;

/// A stored query-answer cache row.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct QaCacheRow {
    /// Numeric rowid (also the `question_vectors` key).
    pub id: i64,
    /// Stable UUIDv7 answer id (anti-drift, propagated to sub-agents).
    pub cache_id: String,
    /// Scoping buffer id (project).
    pub buffer_id: Option<i64>,
    /// Project name (redundant for fast lookup).
    pub project: String,
    /// Original question text.
    pub question_text: String,
    /// Exact-hit hash of the question.
    pub question_hash: String,
    /// Digested answer text.
    pub answer_text: String,
    /// Provenance: chunk ids that produced the answer.
    pub source_chunk_ids: Vec<String>,
    /// Invalidation: content hashes of source chunks.
    pub source_hashes: Vec<String>,
    /// LLM model that synthesized (metadata).
    pub model: Option<String>,
    /// Confidence (decays to 0 when stale).
    pub confidence: f64,
    /// Thresholds snapshot (JSON, for reproducibility).
    pub tier_snapshot: Option<String>,
    /// Token cost of the answer.
    pub token_count: i64,
    /// Access count (for weighted LRU eviction).
    pub access_count: i64,
    /// Created epoch ms.
    pub created_at: i64,
    /// Last accessed epoch ms.
    pub last_accessed_at: i64,
    /// Whether the entry is stale.
    pub stale: bool,
    /// Epoch ms of manual invalidation (audit).
    pub invalidated_at: Option<i64>,
    /// Who invalidated (audit).
    pub invalidated_by: Option<String>,
    /// Why invalidated (audit).
    pub invalidated_reason: Option<String>,
}

/// Input for [`Storage::store_answer`].
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct StoreAnswerInput {
    /// Scoping buffer id.
    pub buffer_id: Option<i64>,
    /// Project name.
    pub project: String,
    /// Original question text.
    pub question_text: String,
    /// Exact-hit hash of the question.
    pub question_hash: String,
    /// Digested answer text.
    pub answer_text: String,
    /// Provenance: chunk ids.
    pub source_chunk_ids: Vec<String>,
    /// Invalidation: chunk content hashes.
    pub source_hashes: Vec<String>,
    /// LLM model (metadata).
    pub model: Option<String>,
    /// Thresholds snapshot (JSON).
    pub tier_snapshot: Option<String>,
    /// Token cost.
    pub token_count: i64,
}

/// Result of storing an answer.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct StoredAnswer {
    /// Stable answer id.
    pub cache_id: String,
    /// Numeric rowid (question_vectors key).
    pub id: i64,
    /// Whether this was a brand-new entry (vs. an idempotent reuse).
    pub created: bool,
}

/// Compute the exact-hit hash for a question (normalized, lowercased).
#[must_use]
pub fn question_hash(question: &str) -> String {
    use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};
    let normalized: String = question
        .chars()
        .filter(|c| !c.is_whitespace())
        .collect::<String>()
        .to_lowercase();
    let mut hasher = Sha256::new();
    hasher.update(normalized.as_bytes());
    hex::encode(hasher.finalize())
}

/// Canonical content hash for a chunk (sha256 hex). Clients must use this exact
/// function when computing `source_hashes` so the server's staleness hook can
/// compare against stored chunk hashes.
#[must_use]
pub fn chunk_content_hash(content: &str) -> String {
    use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};
    let mut hasher = Sha256::new();
    hasher.update(content.as_bytes());
    hex::encode(hasher.finalize())
}

/// Parse a JSON array column into a `Vec<String>`.
fn parse_json_array(text: Option<String>) -> Vec<String> {
    match text {
        Some(s) if !s.is_empty() => serde_json::from_str::<Vec<String>>(&s).unwrap_or_default(),
        _ => Vec::new(),
    }
}

fn row_mapper(r: &rusqlite::Row<'_>) -> rusqlite::Result<QaCacheRow> {
    Ok(QaCacheRow {
        id: r.get(0)?,

        buffer_id: r.get(2)?,
        project: r.get(3)?,

        invalidated_at: r.get(17)?,
        invalidated_by: r.get(18)?,
        invalidated_reason: r.get(19)?,
    })
}

1: //! Adaptive widening engine for the semantic query-answer cache (plan 017).
2: //!
3: //! Maps a query's resolved similarity (question cosine) **and** secondary
4: //! check (provenance Jaccard) onto a digest plan: how many chunks to re-digest
5: //! on the client and how many provenance chunks to return with the cached
6: //! answer. Lower similarity → wider context (more chunks), never exceeding
7: //! `novel_k`. The invariant `provenance_k ≤ digest_k ≤ novel_k` always holds.
8: //!
9: //! This module is pure (no storage, no embedder) so it can be unit-tested and
10: //! reused by both the server (lookup) and the client (digest-once).
11: 
12: use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
13: 
14: /// Configurable thresholds for cache lookup and widening.
15: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
16: pub struct QaThresholds {
17:     /// Chunks digested on a brand-new question (client). Upper bound.
18:     pub novel_k: usize,
19:     /// Provenance chunks returned alongside a cached answer.
20:     pub provenance_k: usize,
21:     /// At/above this similarity a hit is a high-confidence near-exact match.
22:     pub sim_high: f32,
23:     /// Below this similarity the query is treated as brand new (full digest).
24:     pub sim_floor: f32,
25:     /// Descending similarity boundaries for widening tiers.
26:     pub tier_steps: Vec<f32>,
27:     /// Minimum provenance Jaccard for a hit to pass the secondary check.
28:     pub jaccard_min: f32,
29: }
30: 
31: impl Default for QaThresholds {
32:     fn default() -> Self {
33:         Self {
34:             novel_k: 20,

36:             sim_high: 0.90,
37:             sim_floor: 0.40,
38:             tier_steps: vec![0.90, 0.80, 0.70, 0.60, 0.50],
39:             jaccard_min: 0.5,
40:         }
41:     }
42: }
43: 
44: /// A digest plan produced by [`resolve_plan`].
45: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
46: pub struct QaPlan {
47:     /// Chunks the client should digest (`≤ novel_k`).
48:     pub digest_k: usize,
49:     /// Provenance chunks to return with the answer (`≤ digest_k`).
50:     pub provenance_k: usize,
51:     /// Whether this is a MISS (full fresh digest + new cache entry).
52:     pub is_miss: bool,
53:     /// Tier index: `-1` for miss, `0..=tier_steps.len()-1` for hits.
54:     pub tier: i32,
55: }
56: 
57: impl QaPlan {
58:     /// Whether this is a high-confidence near-exact hit (top tier).
59:     #[must_use]
60:     pub fn is_top_tier(&self) -> bool {
61:         self.tier == 0
62:     }
63: }

65: // Per-tier digest/provenance schedule (index aligns with `tier_steps`).
66: const DIGEST_SCHEDULE: [usize; 5] = [10, 12, 13, 15, 18];
67: const PROV_SCHEDULE: [usize; 5] = [5, 6, 7, 8, 10];
68: 
69: /// Resolve a similarity + secondary-check Jaccard into a digest plan.
70: ///
71: /// # Panics
72: ///
73: /// Never panics; clamps gracefully when `tier_steps` is shorter than the
74: /// schedule arrays.
75: #[must_use]
76: pub fn resolve_plan(similarity: f32, jaccard: f32, t: &QaThresholds) -> QaPlan {
77:     // Below the floor → brand new question.
78:     if similarity < t.sim_floor {
79:         return QaPlan {
80:             digest_k: t.novel_k,
81:             provenance_k: t.provenance_k,
82:             is_miss: true,
83:             tier: -1,
84:         };
85:     }
86: 
87:     // Find the highest descending tier step the similarity still meets.
88:     let tier_idx = t.tier_steps.iter().position(|&step| similarity >= step);
89: 
90:     // Similarity is above the floor but below the lowest tier step:
91:     // treat as a near-miss (full fresh digest).
92:     let Some(tier_idx) = tier_idx else {
93:         return QaPlan {
94:             digest_k: t.novel_k,
95:             provenance_k: t.provenance_k,
96:             is_miss: true,
97:             tier: -1,
98:         };
99:     };
100: 
101:     // Secondary check defeats false positives (e.g. "login" vs "logout").
102:     if jaccard < t.jaccard_min {
103:         return QaPlan {
104:             digest_k: t.novel_k,
105:             provenance_k: t.provenance_k,
106:             is_miss: true,
107:             tier: -1,
108:         };
109:     }
110: 
111:     let digest_k = DIGEST_SCHEDULE
112:         .get(tier_idx)
113:         .copied()
114:         .unwrap_or(t.novel_k)
115:         .min(t.novel_k);
116:     let provenance_k = PROV_SCHEDULE
117:         .get(tier_idx)
118:         .copied()
119:         .unwrap_or(t.provenance_k)
120:         .min(digest_k)
121:         .max(1);
122: 
123:     QaPlan {
124:         digest_k,
125:         provenance_k,
126:         is_miss: false,
127:         tier: i32::try_from(tier_idx).unwrap_or(-1),
128:     }
129: }

1: //! Similarity math for the semantic query-answer cache (plan 017).
2: //!
3: //! Cache lookup decides hit/miss/tier by question cosine similarity **plus** a
4: //! secondary check that defeats false positives (e.g. "login" vs "logout" have
5: //! nearby question vectors but disjoint provenance). These helpers are pure so
6: //! they can be unit-tested without storage or an embedder.
7: 
8: /// Cosine similarity of two vectors, clamped to `[-1, 1]`.
9: ///
10: /// Returns `0.0` for zero vectors or mismatched lengths.
11: #[must_use]
12: pub fn cosine_similarity(a: &[f32], b: &[f32]) -> f32 {
13:     if a.len() != b.len() || a.is_empty() {
14:         return 0.0;
15:     }
16:     let dot: f32 = a.iter().zip(b).map(|(x, y)| x * y).sum();
17:     let na: f32 = a.iter().map(|x| x * x).sum::<f32>().sqrt();
18:     let nb: f32 = b.iter().map(|x| x * x).sum::<f32>().sqrt();
19:     if na == 0.0 || nb == 0.0 {
20:         return 0.0;
21:     }
22:     (dot / (na * nb)).clamp(-1.0, 1.0)
23: }
24: 
25: /// Jaccard similarity of two string multisets, in `[0, 1]`:
26: /// `|a ∩ b| / |a ∪ b|`. Used as the secondary check on provenance chunk ids.
27: #[must_use]
28: #[allow(clippy::cast_precision_loss)]
29: pub fn jaccard_similarity(a: &[String], b: &[String]) -> f32 {
30:     if a.is_empty() && b.is_empty() {
31:         return 0.0;
32:     }
33:     let set_a: std::collections::HashSet<&str> = a.iter().map(String::as_str).collect();
34:     let set_b: std::collections::HashSet<&str> = b.iter().map(String::as_str).collect();
35:     let inter = set_a.intersection(&set_b).count();
36:     let union = set_a.union(&set_b).count();
37:     if union == 0 {
38:         return 0.0;
39:     }
40:     inter as f32 / union as f32
41: }

    pub fn evict_qa(&self, project: &str, max_entries: usize, lambda_ms: i64) -> Result<usize> {
        if max_entries == 0 {
            // Keep at least one slot; 0 would purge everything.
            return Ok(0);
        }
        let conn = self.connection().context("failed to acquire connection")?;
        let now = now_ms();
        let lambda = if lambda_ms <= 0 { 1 } else { lambda_ms };
        conn.execute(|c| {
            let count: i64 = c.query_row(
                "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM qa_cache WHERE project = ?1",
                params![project],
                |r| r.get(0),
            )?;
            if count <= i64::try_from(max_entries).unwrap_or(i64::MAX) {
                return Ok(0);
            }
            // Score ascending; delete the excess lowest-scoring rows.
            let excess = count - i64::try_from(max_entries).unwrap_or(i64::MAX);
            let mut stmt = c.prepare(
                "SELECT id FROM qa_cache WHERE project = ?1 \
                 ORDER BY (access_count * 1.0) / (1.0 + ((?2 - last_accessed_at) * 1.0 / ?3)) ASC \
                 LIMIT ?4",
            )?;
            let ids: Vec<i64> = stmt
                .query_map(params![project, now, lambda, excess], |r| r.get(0))?
                .filter_map(std::result::Result::ok)
                .collect();
            let n = ids.len();
            for id in ids {
                c.execute("DELETE FROM qa_cache WHERE id = ?1", params![id])?;
            }
            Ok(n)
        })
        .context("failed to evict qa_cache entries")
    }

    pub fn store_answer(&self, input: &StoreAnswerInput) -> Result<StoredAnswer> {
        let conn = self.connection().context("failed to acquire connection")?;

        // Reserve-lock: reuse an existing non-stale entry for this question.
        if let Some(existing) = conn.execute(|c| {
            c.query_row(
                "SELECT id, cache_id FROM qa_cache \
                 WHERE project = ?1 AND question_hash = ?2 AND stale = 0 \
                 LIMIT 1",
                params![input.project, input.question_hash],
                |r| Ok((r.get::<_, i64>(0)?, r.get::<_, String>(1)?)),
            )
            .optional()
            .context("failed to probe existing qa_cache entry")
        })? {
            return Ok(StoredAnswer {
                cache_id: existing.1,
                id: existing.0,
                created: false,
            });
        }

        let now = now_ms();
        let cache_id = uuid::Uuid::now_v7().to_string();
        let chunk_ids_json = serde_json::to_string(&input.source_chunk_ids)
            .context("failed to serialize source_chunk_ids")?;
        let hashes_json = serde_json::to_string(&input.source_hashes)
            .context("failed to serialize source_hashes")?;
        let snapshot = input
            .tier_snapshot
            .clone()
            .unwrap_or_else(|| "{}".to_string());

        let id: i64 = conn.execute(|c| {
            c.query_row(
                "INSERT INTO qa_cache \
                 (cache_id, buffer_id, project, question_text, question_hash, answer_text, \
                  source_chunk_ids, source_hashes, model, confidence, tier_snapshot, \
                  token_count, access_count, created_at, last_accessed_at, stale) \
                 VALUES (?1, ?2, ?3, ?4, ?5, ?6, ?7, ?8, ?9, 1.0, ?10, ?11, 0, ?12, ?12, 0) \
                 RETURNING id",
                params![
                    cache_id,
                    input.buffer_id,
                    input.project,
                    input.question_text,
                    input.question_hash,
                    input.answer_text,
                    chunk_ids_json,
                    hashes_json,
                    input.model,
                    snapshot,
                    input.token_count,
                    now,
                ],
                |r| r.get::<_, i64>(0),
            )
            .context("failed to insert qa_cache entry")
        })?;

        Ok(StoredAnswer {
            cache_id,
            id,
            created: true,
        })
    }

===== ROOT README (head) =====
# arlm — Agnostic RLM

Recursive Language Model CLI/HTTP para processamento massivo de codebases. Indexa arquivos, armazena embeddings e realiza busca híbrida (BM25 + semântica) para fornecer contexto a agentes LLM.

**Agent-agnostic:** qualquer agente (OPencode, Cursor, Aider, Pi) pode consumir sua saída.

## Arquitetura (server-first)

O `arlm` é **server-first** (ver `plan/016-server-first-architecture.md`): o
`arlm-server` é o processo primário e de longa duração, e o `arlm-cli` é um
cliente gRPC fino que se comunica com ele.

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                  arlm-server  (long-running)           │
│  SQLite (pool r2d2) + LanceDB (vetorial) + summarizer  │
│  expõe API gRPC (tonic + prost, via arlm-proto)       │
└───────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────┘
                              │ gRPC (protobuf, TLS opcional)
┌───────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────┐
│  arlm-cli  (thin gRPC client)  ── index/search/run…   │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

- **9 crates**: `arlm-cli`, `arlm-core`, `arlm-storage`, `arlm-search`,
  `arlm-embedding`, `arlm-memory`, `arlm-llm`, `arlm-proto`, `arlm-server`.
- Conexão tipada por `arlm-proto` (trait `ArlmService`, 19 RPCs).
- **Sem LLM para index/search/context/query** (embeddings usam
  *fallback hash* determinístico e offline por padrão; BGE-M3 via `candle`
  é opcional). LLM é *opt-in* (`--llm`) apenas para `run`/summarize.
- O CLI também roda **localmente** (sem `--server`), operando diretamente
  sobre `~/.arlm` (retrocompatibilidade).

## Instalação

```bash
# Binários (server + client)
cargo build --release            # → ./target/release/arlm e ./target/release/arlm-server

# Ou via script de instalação
./install.sh                     # instala arlm e cria ~/.arlm/config.toml
```

### Requisitos

- Rust 1.85+ (edition 2024)
- `protoc` (protobuf-compiler) para gRPC/`arlm-proto`
- `protobuf-devel` para includes do protobuf

## Uso Rápido

```bash
# Indexar um projeto
arlm index ./meu-projeto

# Indexar com ignore patterns
arlm index ./meu-projeto --ignore "dist/" --ignore "*.log"

# Indexar com watch mode (reindexa automaticamente)
arlm index ./meu-projeto --watch
===== arlm-server/README =====
# arlm-server

Long-running **gRPC server** para a plataforma [arlm](https://github.com/anomalyco/arlm)
(Agnostic RLM). Armazena, indexa, sumariza e executa RLM (Recursive Language Model)
para times, expondo uma API gRPC (tonic) consumível por qualquer agente de IA.

## Visão geral

O servidor gerencia **projetos (buffers)**, **sessões**, **runs de RLM**, **indexação**
(chunking + embeddings + LanceDB) e **sumarização hierárquica**, com streaming de
eventos em tempo real para clientes.

## Build & Run

```bash
# Desenvolvimento
cargo run -p arlm-server -- up

# Release
cargo build --release -p arlm-server
./target/release/arlm-server up

# Checagem e testes (otimizado, 12 threads)
cargo check -p arlm-server
cargo test   -p arlm-server
cargo clippy -p arlm-server --all-targets
```

### Subcomandos

| Comando | Descrição |
|----------|-----------|
| `up`     | (padrão) Carrega config, abre storage, sobe o servidor gRPC. |
| `status` | Consulta a saúde de um servidor em execução via `GetServerStatus` (usado pelo Docker HEALTHCHECK). |

### Docker

```bash
# Build + run via compose (porta 50051, comando `up`)
docker compose -f docker-compose.server.yml up --build
```

O `Dockerfile.server` expõe a porta `50051` e roda `HEALTHCHECK CMD arlm-server status`.

## Configuração

Carregada de `.arlm/config.toml` (local → global) ou env `ARLM_SERVER_ADDR`.
Exemplo:

```toml
listen_addr = "127.0.0.1:50051"
data_dir    = "/var/lib/arlm"
pool_size   = 4

[llm]
backend = "ollama"        # openai | anthropic | ollama | gemini | deepseek | mimo
model   = "qwen2.5-coder:7b"
# api_key = "..."         # opcional; cai no env da backend se ausente
# base_url = "..."        # opcional

# tls_cert / tls_key     # opcionais → habilita TLS
```

## Arquitetura

Fluxo unidirecional: `arlm-cli` → `arlm-server` (gRPC) → `arlm-core` (engine RLM) /
`arlm-storage` (SQLite + LanceDB) / `arlm-embedding` / `arlm-llm`.

- **Handlers gRPC** (`src/grpc/*`): um arquivo por grupo de RPCs.
- **`store`** (`src/store/*`): camada de acesso a dados tipada e segura para o pool.
- **`summarizer`** (`src/summarizer/*`): engine de sumarização hierárquica em worker
  em background, com streaming de progresso.
- **`events`**: `EventHub` (broadcast) que faz a ponte engine → streams gRPC.
- **`state`**: `AppState` compartilhado (storage, llm, event hub, vector store,
  abort signals de runs).
- **`timing`**: `Timer` que emite `elapsed_ms`/`elapsed_us` estruturados via `tracing`.

## Testes

Os testes de integração vivem em `tests/` (fora de `src/`):

- `tests/indexing_tests.rs` — chunking, linguagem, hashing.
- `tests/store_tests.rs` — CRUD de projetos/sessões/runs.
- `tests/summarizer_tests.rs` — custo, progresso, estratégia de prompt.

## Licença

Idêntica ao workspace (MIT/Apache-2.0).
