32: /// Build the embedder: Ollama when configured, else BGE-M3 (quantized) when
33: /// weights are available, else a hash fallback.
34: fn load_embedder() -> Arc<dyn Embedder + Send + Sync> {
35:     const DIMS: usize = 1024;
36: 
37:     // Ollama backend (laptop-friendly): enabled via ARLM_OLLAMA_MODEL.
38:     if let Ok(model) = std::env::var("ARLM_OLLAMA_MODEL") {
39:         let url = std::env::var("ARLM_OLLAMA_URL")
40:             .unwrap_or_else(|_| "http://localhost:11434".to_string());
41:         let dims = std::env::var("ARLM_OLLAMA_DIMS")
42:             .ok()
43:             .and_then(|d| d.parse::<usize>().ok())
44:             .unwrap_or(768);
45:         let prefix =
46:             std::env::var("ARLM_OLLAMA_PREFIX").unwrap_or_else(|_| "search_document: ".to_string());
47:         let cfg = arlm_embedding::embedder::config::EmbeddingConfig {
48:             model: arlm_embedding::embedder::config::EmbeddingModel::Ollama,
49:             quantization: arlm_embedding::embedder::config::Quantization::None,
50:             matryoshka_dims: None,
51:             model_dir: None,
52:             dims,
53:             ollama_url: Some(url.clone()),
54:             ollama_model: Some(model.clone()),
55:             ollama_prefix: Some(prefix),
56:         };
57:         match arlm_embedding::embedder::config::build_embedder(&cfg) {
58:             Ok(embedder) => {
59:                 tracing::info!(model = "ollama", ollama_model = %model, "loaded Ollama embedder");
60:                 return embedder;
61:             }
62:             Err(err) => {
63:                 tracing::warn!(error = %err, "Ollama embedder failed; falling back");
64:             }
65:         }
66:     }
67: 
68:     match std::env::var("ARLM_MODEL_DIR").ok().map(PathBuf::from) {
69:         Some(dir) if dir.join("model.safetensors").exists() => {
70:             // Quantize to INT8 at load time: runs real BGE-M3 semantics via
71:             // `QMatMul` at ~3-4x less CPU/RAM than FP32 (set ARLM_MODEL_QUANT
72:             // to override). FP32 ("none") is far too slow for CPU indexing.
73:             let quant = match std::env::var("ARLM_MODEL_QUANT").as_deref() {
74:                 Ok("none") => arlm_embedding::embedder::config::Quantization::None,
75:                 Ok("int4") => arlm_embedding::embedder::config::Quantization::Int4,
76:                 _ => arlm_embedding::embedder::config::Quantization::Int8,
77:             };
78:             let cfg = arlm_embedding::embedder::config::EmbeddingConfig {
79:                 model: arlm_embedding::embedder::config::EmbeddingModel::BgeM3,
80:                 quantization: quant,
81:                 matryoshka_dims: Some(DIMS),
82:                 model_dir: Some(dir.clone()),
83:                 dims: DIMS,
84:                 ollama_url: None,
85:                 ollama_model: None,
86:                 ollama_prefix: None,
87:             };
88:             match bge_m3::BgeM3Embedder::new_with_config(&dir, &cfg) {
89:                 Ok(embedder) => {
90:                     tracing::info!(
91:                         model_dir = %dir.display(),
92:                         quantization = ?quant,
93:                         "loaded BGE-M3 embedder"
94:                     );
95:                     Arc::new(embedder)
96:                 }
97:                 Err(err) => {
98:                     tracing::warn!(
99:                         error = %err,
100:                         "BGE-M3 load failed, falling back to hash embedder"
101:                     );
102:                     Arc::new(fallback::FallbackEmbedder::new(DIMS))
103:                 }
104:             }
105:         }
106:         Some(dir) => {
107:             tracing::warn!(
108:                 model_dir = %dir.display(),
109:                 "ARLM_MODEL_DIR set but model.safetensors missing; using hash embedder"
110:             );
111:             Arc::new(fallback::FallbackEmbedder::new(DIMS))
112:         }
113:         None => {
114:             tracing::info!("ARLM_MODEL_DIR not set; using fallback hash embedder");
115:             Arc::new(fallback::FallbackEmbedder::new(DIMS))
116:         }
117:     }
118: }

1: //! Auth core for the gRPC server (plan 018).
2: //!
3: //! - [`Role`] is re-exported from `arlm-storage` (single source of truth).
4: //! - [`AuthContext`] is the caller identity resolved from a session token.
5: //! - [`authenticate`] enforces a valid session on a request's `Authorization`
6: //!   metadata; call it at the top of every RPC handler except `AuthRefresh`
7: //!   (the login RPC) and the health RPCs.
8: //! - [`require_admin`] enforces the admin gate used by privileged RPCs.
9: //!
10: //! Note: tonic 0.13's `Interceptor` cannot see the RPC path, so per-RPC
11: //! exemption (notably `AuthRefresh`) is done at the handler level rather than
12: //! via a global interceptor.
13: 
14: pub use arlm_storage::Role;
15: 
16: use arlm_storage::Storage;
17: use tonic::metadata::MetadataMap;
18: use tonic::{Request, Status};
19: 
20: /// Identity of the caller, resolved from a valid session token.
21: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
22: pub struct AuthContext {
23:     /// Auditing username (from the refresh token).
24:     pub username: String,
25:     /// Authorization role.
26:     pub role: Role,
27: }
28: 
29: impl AuthContext {
30:     /// Whether this context carries the `admin` role.
31:     #[must_use]
32:     pub fn is_admin(&self) -> bool {
33:         self.role == Role::Admin
34:     }
35: }
36: 
37: /// Authenticate a request from its `Authorization: Bearer` metadata.
38: ///
39: /// Returns the caller's identity, or `UNAUTHENTICATED` / `internal`.
40: ///
41: /// # Errors
42: ///
43: /// Returns a `Status` when the session is missing, invalid, expired, or when
44: /// validation fails.
45: pub fn authenticate(md: &MetadataMap, storage: &Storage) -> Result<AuthContext, Status> {
46:     let token = bearer(md)?;
47:     match arlm_storage::tokens::validate_session(storage, &token) {
48:         Ok(Some((username, role))) => Ok(AuthContext { username, role }),
49:         Ok(None) => Err(Status::unauthenticated("invalid or expired session")),
50:         Err(e) => {
51:             tracing::error!(error = %e, "session validation failed");
52:             Err(Status::internal("session validation failed"))
53:         }
54:     }
55: }
56: 
57: /// Enforce the `admin` role, returning `PERMISSION_DENIED` otherwise.
58: ///
59: /// # Errors
60: ///
61: /// Returns a `Status` when the caller is not an admin.
62: pub fn require_admin(ctx: &AuthContext) -> Result<(), Status> {
63:     if ctx.is_admin() {
64:         Ok(())
65:     } else {
66:         Err(Status::permission_denied(
67:             "admin role required for this operation",
68:         ))
69:     }
70: }
71: 
72: fn bearer(md: &MetadataMap) -> Result<String, Status> {
73:     let value = md
74:         .get("authorization")
75:         .ok_or_else(|| Status::unauthenticated("missing authorization header"))?
76:         .to_str()
77:         .map_err(|_| Status::unauthenticated("authorization header is not valid UTF-8"))?;
78:     let token = value
79:         .strip_prefix("Bearer ")
80:         .or_else(|| value.strip_prefix("bearer "))
81:         .ok_or_else(|| Status::unauthenticated("authorization must be a Bearer token"))?;
82:     if token.is_empty() {
83:         return Err(Status::unauthenticated("empty bearer token"));
84:     }
85:     Ok(token.to_string())
86: }
87: 
88: /// Helper to authenticate a typed request (carries `metadata()`).
89: ///
90: /// # Errors
91: ///
92: /// See [`authenticate`].
93: pub fn authenticate_request<T>(req: &Request<T>, storage: &Storage) -> Result<AuthContext, Status> {
94:     authenticate(req.metadata(), storage)
95: }

1: //! Query-Answer Cache RPCs (plan 017) + admin-gated `InvalidateCache`.
2: //!
3: //! The server is **deterministic**: it embeds, searches (BM25 + vector) and
4: //! stores — it never runs an LLM. Digestion happens client-side (plan 017
5: //! "digest-once"). `InvalidateCache` is admin-gated by plan 018: non-admins
6: //! receive `PERMISSION_DENIED`.
7: //!
8: //! `InvalidateCache` is backward-compatible with plan 018: when `cache_id` is
9: //! empty it purges the legacy `result_cache` by project (empty = all). When
10: //! `cache_id` is set it invalidates the semantic `qa_cache` (Stale/Delete, with
11: //! an optional similarity radius over `question_vectors`).
12: 
13: use arlm_core::qa_cache::{QaThresholds, resolve_plan};
14: use arlm_proto::proto::*;
15: use arlm_search::qa_cache::jaccard_similarity;
16: use arlm_storage::qa_cache as qa_store;
17: use arlm_storage::qa_cache::StoreAnswerInput;
18: use tonic::{Request, Response, Status};
19: 
20: use crate::grpc::error::{internal, invalid_arg};
21: use crate::grpc::search::{buffer_id_for, hybrid_search};
22: use crate::state::AppState;
23: use crate::store;
24: 
25: /// Task prefix applied to question embeddings (separate vector space B).
26: const QUESTION_PREFIX: &str = "search_query: ";
27: 
28: /// Embed a question in the dedicated question space (blocking).
29: async fn embed_query(state: &AppState, question: &str) -> Option<Vec<f32>> {
30:     let embedder = state.embedder.clone();
31:     let text = format!("{QUESTION_PREFIX}{question}");
32:     tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || embedder.embed(&text))
33:         .await
34:         .ok()
35:         .and_then(Result::ok)
36: }
37: 
38: /// Map hydrated `arlm_search::SearchResult` into the gRPC `SearchResult` shape.
39: fn to_proto_results(results: &[arlm_search::SearchResult]) -> Vec<SearchResult> {
40:     results
41:         .iter()
42:         .map(|r| SearchResult {
43:             chunk_id: r.chunk_id,
44:             text: r.content.clone(),
45:             score: r.score,
46:             file_path: r.file_path.clone(),
47:             start_line: r.line_start as i32,
48:             end_line: r.line_end as i32,
49:             is_summary: r.is_summary,
50:             summary: None,
51:         })
52:         .collect()
53: }
54: 
55: /// Build the adaptive thresholds from server config.
56: fn thresholds(state: &AppState) -> QaThresholds {
57:     let c = &state.qa_config;
58:     QaThresholds {
59:         novel_k: c.novel_k,
60:         provenance_k: c.provenance_k,
61:         sim_high: c.sim_high,
62:         sim_floor: c.sim_floor,
63:         tier_steps: c.tier_steps.clone(),
64:         jaccard_min: c.jaccard_min,
65:     }
66: }
67: 
68: /// Resolve a project to its buffer id (explicit or by name).
69: async fn resolve_buffer(state: &AppState, project: &str, explicit: i64) -> Option<i64> {
70:     if explicit > 0 {
71:         return Some(explicit);
72:     }
73:     buffer_id_for(state, project).await.ok().flatten()
74: }
75: 
76: /// Query the semantic cache; decides hit/miss/tier deterministically.
77: ///
78: /// # Errors
79: ///
80: /// Returns `UNAUTHENTICATED` without a session, or `internal` on storage failure.
81: pub async fn handle_query_with_cache(
82:     state: &AppState,
83:     request: Request<QueryWithCacheRequest>,
84: ) -> Result<Response<QueryWithCacheResponse>, Status> {
85:     let _timer = crate::timing::Timer::new("handler.query_with_cache");
86:     crate::auth::authenticate(request.metadata(), &state.storage)?;
87:     let req = request.into_inner();
88: 
89:     let project = req.project;
90:     if project.trim().is_empty() {
91:         return Err(invalid_arg("project is required"));
92:     }
93:     if req.question.trim().is_empty() {
94:         return Err(invalid_arg("question is required"));
95:     }
96: 
97:     let buffer_id = resolve_buffer(state, &project, req.buffer_id).await;
98:     let qh = qa_store::question_hash(&req.question);
99:     let th = thresholds(state);
100: 
101:     // 1) Exact hit (same question, same project).
102:     let qh_owned = qh.clone();
103:     let project_owned = project.clone();
104:     if let Some(row) = store::blocking({
105:         let storage = state.storage.clone();
106:         move || storage.get_cached_answer(&project_owned, &qh_owned)
107:     })
108:     .await
109:     .map_err(internal)?
110:     {
111:         let id = row.id;
112:         let cache_id = row.cache_id.clone();
113:         // Touch for eviction weighting.
114:         let storage = state.storage.clone();
115:         let _ = store::blocking(move || storage.touch_qa(id)).await;
116:         let provenance = provenance_chunks(&state, &row.source_chunk_ids, th.provenance_k).await;
117:         return Ok(Response::new(QueryWithCacheResponse {
118:             cache_id,
119:             hit: true,
120:             tier: 0,
121:             similarity: 1.0,
122:             answer_text: row.answer_text,
123:             provenance,
124:             candidates: Vec::new(),
125:             digest_k: 0,
126:             provenance_k: th.provenance_k as i32,
127:         }));
128:     }
129: 
130:     // 2) Near hit: embed question, search question vectors, secondary check.
131:     let query_vec = embed_query(state, &req.question).await;
132:     let mut best_sim = 0.0_f32;
133:     if let (Some(vec), Some(qv_store)) = (&query_vec, state.question_vector_store.as_ref()) {
134:         if let Ok(neighbors) = qv_store.search(vec, 10) {
135:             if let Some(best) = neighbors.first() {
136:                 best_sim = best.similarity;
137:                 if best.similarity >= th.sim_floor {
138:                     if let Ok(Some(cand)) = store::blocking({
139:                         let storage = state.storage.clone();
140:                         let id = best.id;
141:                         move || storage.get_qa_by_rowid(id as i64)
142:                     })
143:                     .await
144:                     {
145:                         // New query's top-K chunk ids for the Jaccard check.
146:                         let new_ids =
147:                             top_chunk_ids(state, &project, &req.question, th.novel_k).await;
148:                         let jac = jaccard_similarity(&new_ids, &cand.source_chunk_ids);
149:                         let plan = resolve_plan(best.similarity, jac, &th);
150:                         if !plan.is_miss {
151:                             let cid = cand.cache_id.clone();
152:                             let storage = state.storage.clone();
153:                             let _ = store::blocking(move || storage.touch_qa(cand.id)).await;
154:                             let provenance =
155:                                 provenance_chunks(state, &cand.source_chunk_ids, th.provenance_k)
156:                                     .await;
157:                             return Ok(Response::new(QueryWithCacheResponse {
158:                                 cache_id: cid,
159:                                 hit: true,
160:                                 tier: plan.tier,
161:                                 similarity: best.similarity,
162:                                 answer_text: cand.answer_text,
163:                                 provenance,
164:                                 candidates: Vec::new(),
165:                                 digest_k: plan.digest_k as i32,
166:                                 provenance_k: plan.provenance_k as i32,
167:                             }));
168:                         }
169:                     }
170:                 }
171:             }
172:         }
173:     }
174: 
175:     // 3) Miss: return top-K raw chunks to digest client-side.
176:     let candidates = hybrid_search(
177:         state,
178:         buffer_id.unwrap_or(0),
179:         &sanitize(&req.question),
180:         arlm_search::SearchTier::Vector,
181:         th.novel_k,
182:     )
183:     .await
184:     .map_err(internal)?;
185: 
186:     Ok(Response::new(QueryWithCacheResponse {
187:         cache_id: String::new(),
188:         hit: false,
189:         tier: -1,
190:         similarity: best_sim,
191:         answer_text: String::new(),
192:         provenance: Vec::new(),
193:         candidates: to_proto_results(&candidates),
194:         digest_k: th.novel_k as i32,
195:         provenance_k: th.provenance_k as i32,
196:     }))
197: }
198: 
199: /// Store a client-digested answer (idempotent per project+question_hash).
200: ///
201: /// # Errors
202: ///
203: /// Returns `UNAUTHENTICATED` without a session, or `internal` on failure.
204: pub async fn handle_store_answer(
205:     state: &AppState,
206:     request: Request<StoreAnswerRequest>,
207: ) -> Result<Response<StoreAnswerResponse>, Status> {
208:     let _timer = crate::timing::Timer::new("handler.store_answer");
209:     crate::auth::authenticate(request.metadata(), &state.storage)?;
210:     let req = request.into_inner();
211: 
212:     let project = req.project;
213:     if project.trim().is_empty() {
214:         return Err(invalid_arg("project is required"));
215:     }
216:     if req.question.trim().is_empty() {
217:         return Err(invalid_arg("question is required"));
218:     }
219:     if req.answer.trim().is_empty() {
220:         return Err(invalid_arg("answer is required"));
221:     }
222: 
223:     let buffer_id = resolve_buffer(state, &project, req.buffer_id).await;
224:     let qh = qa_store::question_hash(&req.question);
225: 
226:     let input = StoreAnswerInput {
227:         buffer_id,
228:         project: project.clone(),
229:         question_text: req.question.clone(),
230:         question_hash: qh,
231:         answer_text: req.answer,
232:         source_chunk_ids: req.source_chunk_ids,
233:         source_hashes: req.source_hashes,
234:         model: if req.model.is_empty() {
235:             None
236:         } else {
237:             Some(req.model)
238:         },
239:         tier_snapshot: Some(
240:             serde_json::to_string(&state.qa_config).unwrap_or_else(|_| "{}".into()),
241:         ),
242:         token_count: req.token_count,
243:     };
244: 
245:     let stored = store::blocking({
246:         let storage = state.storage.clone();
247:         move || storage.store_answer(&input)
248:     })
249:     .await
250:     .map_err(internal)?;
251: 
252:     // Embed the question and persist it in the dedicated question space.
253:     if let Some(vec) = embed_query(state, &req.question).await {
254:         if let Some(qv_store) = state.question_vector_store.as_ref() {
255:             if let Err(e) = qv_store.insert(stored.id as u64, &vec) {
256:                 tracing::warn!(error = %e, "failed to persist question vector");
257:             }
258:         }
259:     }
260: 
261:     Ok(Response::new(StoreAnswerResponse {
262:         cache_id: stored.cache_id,
263:     }))
264: }

266: /// Direct, deterministic lookup of a served answer by stable id (anti-drift).
267: ///
268: /// # Errors
269: ///
270: /// Returns `UNAUTHENTICATED` without a session, or `internal` on failure.
271: pub async fn handle_get_answer_by_id(
272:     state: &AppState,
273:     request: Request<GetAnswerByIdRequest>,
274: ) -> Result<Response<GetAnswerByIdResponse>, Status> {
275:     let _timer = crate::timing::Timer::new("handler.get_answer_by_id");
276:     crate::auth::authenticate(request.metadata(), &state.storage)?;
277:     let req = request.into_inner();
278: 
279:     if req.cache_id.trim().is_empty() {
280:         return Err(invalid_arg("cache_id is required"));
281:     }
282: 
283:     let storage = state.storage.clone();
284:     let cache_id = req.cache_id.clone();
285:     let project = req.project.clone();
286:     let row = store::blocking(move || storage.get_qa_by_id(&cache_id, &project))
287:         .await
288:         .map_err(internal)?;
289: 
290:     match row {
291:         Some(r) => Ok(Response::new(GetAnswerByIdResponse {
292:             found: true,
293:             cache_id: r.cache_id,
294:             project: r.project,
295:             answer_text: r.answer_text,
296:             source_chunk_ids: r.source_chunk_ids,
297:             source_hashes: r.source_hashes,
298:         })),
299:         None => Ok(Response::new(GetAnswerByIdResponse {
300:             found: false,
301:             cache_id: req.cache_id,
302:             project: req.project,
303:             answer_text: String::new(),
304:             source_chunk_ids: Vec::new(),
305:             source_hashes: Vec::new(),
306:         })),
307:     }
308: }

310: /// Admin-gated invalidation of cached answers (plan 018 + plan 017).
311: ///
312: /// # Errors
313: ///
314: /// Returns `UNAUTHENTICATED` with no session, `PERMISSION_DENIED` for
315: /// non-admins, or `internal` on storage failure.
316: pub async fn handle_invalidate_cache(
317:     state: &AppState,
318:     request: Request<InvalidateCacheRequest>,
319: ) -> Result<Response<InvalidateCacheResponse>, Status> {
320:     let _timer = crate::timing::Timer::new("handler.invalidate_cache");
321:     let ctx = crate::auth::authenticate(request.metadata(), &state.storage)?;
322:     crate::auth::require_admin(&ctx)?;
323: 
324:     let req = request.into_inner();
325: 
326:     // Plan 017 path: invalidate a specific semantic cache entry (and radius).
327:     if !req.cache_id.is_empty() {
328:         return invalidate_qa_entry(state, &req, &ctx.username).await;
329:     }
330: 
331:     // Legacy plan 018 path: purge the `result_cache` by project.
332:     let project = req.project;
333:     let project_opt = if project.is_empty() {
334:         None
335:     } else {
336:         Some(project)
337:     };
338:     let invalidated = store::blocking({
339:         let storage = state.storage.clone();
340:         let p = project_opt.clone();
341:         move || arlm_storage::cache::invalidate_cache(&storage, p.as_deref())
342:     })
343:     .await
344:     .map_err(internal)?;
345: 
346:     Ok(Response::new(InvalidateCacheResponse {
347:         invalidated: invalidated as i64,
348:         invalidated_by: ctx.username,
349:     }))
350: }
351: 
352: /// Invalidate a single `qa_cache` entry, optionally with a similarity radius
353: /// over `question_vectors` (error-chain invalidation).
354: async fn invalidate_qa_entry(
355:     state: &AppState,
356:     req: &InvalidateCacheRequest,
357:     username: &str,
358: ) -> Result<Response<InvalidateCacheResponse>, Status> {
359:     let cache_id = req.cache_id.clone();
360:     let row = store::blocking({
361:         let storage = state.storage.clone();
362:         move || storage.get_qa_by_cache_id(&cache_id)
363:     })
364:     .await
365:     .map_err(internal)?;
366: 
367:     let Some(row) = row else {
368:         return Ok(Response::new(InvalidateCacheResponse {
369:             invalidated: 0,
370:             invalidated_by: username.to_string(),
371:         }));
372:     };
373: 
374:     let delete = req.mode == InvalidateMode::Delete as i32;
375:     let mut count: u64 = 0;
376: 
377:     // Radius neighbors first (they reference the target's question vector).
378:     if req.similarity_radius > 0.0 {
379:         if let Some(vec) = embed_query(state, &row.question_text).await {
380:             if let Some(qv_store) = state.question_vector_store.as_ref() {
381:                 if let Ok(neighbors) = qv_store.search(&vec, 1000) {
382:                     for n in neighbors {
383:                         if n.id as i64 == row.id {
384:                             continue;
385:                         }
386:                         if n.similarity < req.similarity_radius {
387:                             continue;
388:                         }
389:                         let nid = n.id as i64;
390:                         if delete {
391:                             if store::blocking({
392:                                 let storage = state.storage.clone();
393:                                 move || storage.delete_qa(nid)
394:                             })
395:                             .await
396:                             .map_err(internal)?
397:                                 > 0
398:                             {
399:                                 let _ = qv_store.delete(n.id);
400:                                 count += 1;
401:                             }
402:                         } else if store::blocking({
403:                             let storage = state.storage.clone();
404:                             let u = username.to_string();
405:                             move || storage.mark_qa_stale(nid, &u, "radius")
406:                         })
407:                         .await
408:                         .map_err(internal)?
409:                         {
410:                             count += 1;
411:                         }
412:                     }
413:                 }
414:             }
415:         }
416:     }
417: 
418:     // The target entry itself.
419:     if delete {
420:         if store::blocking({
421:             let storage = state.storage.clone();
422:             move || storage.delete_qa(row.id)
423:         })
424:         .await
425:         .map_err(internal)?
426:             > 0
427:         {
428:             if let Some(qv_store) = state.question_vector_store.as_ref() {
429:                 let _ = qv_store.delete(row.id as u64);
430:             }
431:             count += 1;
432:         }
433:     } else if store::blocking({
434:         let storage = state.storage.clone();
435:         let u = username.to_string();
436:         let id = row.id;
437:         move || storage.mark_qa_stale(id, &u, "admin")
438:     })
439:     .await
440:     .map_err(internal)?
441:     {
442:         count += 1;
443:     }
444: 
445:     Ok(Response::new(InvalidateCacheResponse {
446:         invalidated: count as i64,
447:         invalidated_by: username.to_string(),
448:     }))
449: }

451: /// Fetch provenance chunks for a cached answer (top `k` by stored order).
452: async fn provenance_chunks(state: &AppState, ids: &[String], k: usize) -> Vec<SearchResult> {
453:     let ids: Vec<i64> = ids.iter().filter_map(|s| s.parse::<i64>().ok()).collect();
454:     if ids.is_empty() {
455:         return Vec::new();
456:     }
457:     let taken: Vec<i64> = ids.iter().copied().take(k.max(1)).collect();
458:     let storage = state.storage.clone();
459:     let chunks = store::blocking(move || storage.get_chunks_with_content(&taken))
460:         .await
461:         .ok()
462:         .unwrap_or_default();
463:     chunks
464:         .into_iter()
465:         .map(|(c, content)| SearchResult {
466:             chunk_id: c.id,
467:             text: content.unwrap_or_default(),
468:             score: 1.0,
469:             file_path: c.file_path,
470:             start_line: c.line_start as i32,
471:             end_line: c.line_end as i32,
472:             is_summary: false,
473:             summary: None,
474:         })
475:         .collect()
476: }
477: 
478: /// Top-K chunk ids from a hybrid search (for the secondary Jaccard check).
479: async fn top_chunk_ids(state: &AppState, _project: &str, question: &str, k: usize) -> Vec<String> {
480:     // Best-effort; if search fails, an empty list yields a failing Jaccard and
481:     // forces a MISS (safe default).
482:     match hybrid_search(
483:         state,
484:         0,
485:         &sanitize(question),
486:         arlm_search::SearchTier::Vector,
487:         k,
488:     )
489:     .await
490:     {
491:         Ok(results) => results
492:             .iter()
493:             .map(|r| r.chunk_id.to_string())
494:             .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
495:         Err(_) => Vec::new(),
496:     }
497: }
498: 
499: /// Sanitise a query for FTS5 `MATCH` (kept in sync with `grpc::search`).
500: fn sanitize(query: &str) -> String {
501:     query
502:         .chars()
503:         .map(|c| {
504:             if c.is_alphanumeric() || c.is_whitespace() {
505:                 c
506:             } else {
507:                 ' '
508:             }
509:         })
510:         .collect()
511: }

7: /// Options for consolidation.
8: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
9: pub struct ConsolidateOptions {
10:     /// Remove chunks with duplicate hashes.
11:     pub deduplicate: bool,
12:     /// Remove patterns with confidence below this threshold.
13:     pub min_pattern_confidence: f64,
14: }
15: 
16: impl Default for ConsolidateOptions {
17:     fn default() -> Self {
18:         Self {
19:             deduplicate: true,
20:             min_pattern_confidence: 0.3,
21:         }
22:     }
23: }
24: 
25: /// Result of a consolidation operation.
26: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
27: pub struct ConsolidateResult {
28:     pub duplicate_chunks_removed: u64,
29:     pub low_confidence_patterns_removed: u64,
30: }
31: 
32: /// Handles memory consolidation: deduplication, cleanup, aggregation.
33: pub struct ConsolidationEngine {
34:     storage: Storage,
35: }
36: 
37: impl ConsolidationEngine {
38:     /// Create a new `ConsolidationEngine`.
39:     #[must_use]
40:     pub fn new(storage: Storage) -> Self {
41:         Self { storage }
42:     }
43: 
44:     /// Consolidate memory for a project.
45:     ///
46:     /// Removes duplicate chunks and low-confidence patterns.
47:     ///
48:     /// # Errors
49:     ///
50:     /// Returns an error if database operations fail.
51:     pub fn consolidate(
52:         &self,
53:         buffer_id: i64,
54:         options: &ConsolidateOptions,
55:     ) -> Result<ConsolidateResult> {
56:         let _timer = ScopedTimer::new("consolidation");
57: 
58:         let mut result = ConsolidateResult {
59:             duplicate_chunks_removed: 0,
60:             low_confidence_patterns_removed: 0,
61:         };
62: 
63:         if options.deduplicate {
64:             result.duplicate_chunks_removed = self.remove_duplicate_chunks(buffer_id)?;
65:         }
66: 
67:         result.low_confidence_patterns_removed =
68:             self.remove_low_confidence_patterns(buffer_id, options.min_pattern_confidence)?;
69: 
70:         tracing::info!(
71:             buffer_id,
72:             duplicates_removed = result.duplicate_chunks_removed,
73:             patterns_removed = result.low_confidence_patterns_removed,
74:             "consolidation completed"
75:         );
76: 
77:         Ok(result)
78:     }
79: 
80:     fn remove_duplicate_chunks(&self, buffer_id: i64) -> Result<u64> {
81:         let conn = self.storage.conn();
82:         let conn = conn.lock();
83: 
84:         // Find duplicate hashes within the same buffer
85:         let mut stmt = conn
86:             .prepare(
87:                 "SELECT hash, COUNT(*) as cnt FROM chunks WHERE buffer_id = ?1 GROUP BY hash HAVING cnt > 1",
88:             )
89:             .context("failed to prepare duplicate query")?;
90: 
91:         let duplicate_hashes: Vec<Vec<u8>> = stmt
92:             .query_map([buffer_id], |row| row.get(0))?
93:             .filter_map(std::result::Result::ok)
94:             .collect();
95: 
96:         let mut removed: u64 = 0;
97: 
98:         for hash in &duplicate_hashes {
99:             // Keep the first chunk, remove the rest
100:             let mut del_stmt = conn
101:                 .prepare(
102:                     "DELETE FROM chunks WHERE id IN (
103:                         SELECT id FROM chunks WHERE buffer_id = ?1 AND hash = ?2
104:                         ORDER BY id DESC
105:                         LIMIT -1 OFFSET 1
106:                     )",
107:                 )
108:                 .context("failed to prepare delete duplicates")?;
109: 
110:             let deleted = del_stmt
111:                 .execute(rusqlite::params![buffer_id, hash])
112:                 .context("failed to delete duplicates")?;
113: 
114:             removed += u64::try_from(deleted).unwrap_or(0);
115:         }
116: 
117:         Ok(removed)
118:     }
119: 
120:     fn remove_low_confidence_patterns(&self, buffer_id: i64, min_confidence: f64) -> Result<u64> {
121:         let conn = self.storage.conn();
122:         let conn = conn.lock();
123: 
124:         let deleted = conn
125:             .execute(
126:                 "DELETE FROM patterns WHERE buffer_id = ?1 AND confidence < ?2 AND confidence IS NOT NULL",
127:                 rusqlite::params![buffer_id, min_confidence],
128:             )
129:             .context("failed to remove low confidence patterns")?;
130: 
131:         Ok(u64::try_from(deleted).unwrap_or(0))
132:     }
133: }

1: //! Salience / decay scoring for memory entries.
2: //!
3: //! Pure, self-contained heuristics used to rank and evict wiki pages and chunks.
4: //! Salience is a value in `[0.0, 1.0]` derived from three signals:
5: //!
6: //! - **recency** — how recently the entry was last accessed (exponential decay),
7: //! - **frequency** — how often the entry has been accessed (diminishing returns),
8: //! - **age** — how old the entry is (gentle penalty).
9: //!
10: //! This module intentionally has no dependency on `arlm-search` so it can be reused
11: //! by any memory backend.
12: 
13: use std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};
14: 
15: /// Configuration for the salience computation.
16: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
17: pub struct DecayConfig {
18:     /// Milliseconds after which recency score halves.
19:     pub recency_half_life_ms: f64,
20:     /// Weight of the recency component (0.0–1.0).
21:     pub recency_weight: f64,
22:     /// Weight of the frequency component (0.0–1.0).
23:     pub frequency_weight: f64,
24:     /// Weight of the age component (0.0–1.0).
25:     pub age_weight: f64,
26: }
27: 
28: impl Default for DecayConfig {
29:     fn default() -> Self {
30:         Self {
31:             recency_half_life_ms: 30.0 * 24.0 * 3_600.0 * 1_000.0,
32:             recency_weight: 0.6,
33:             frequency_weight: 0.3,
34:             age_weight: 0.1,
35:         }
36:     }
37: }
38: 
39: /// Input signals for a single memory entry.
40: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
41: pub struct SalienceInput {
42:     /// Creation timestamp in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.
43:     pub created_at_ms: u64,
44:     /// Last-access timestamp in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.
45:     pub last_accessed_at_ms: u64,
46:     /// Number of times the entry has been accessed.
47:     pub access_count: u64,
48:     /// Current time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.
49:     pub now_ms: u64,
50: }
51: 
52: /// Return the current time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.
53: #[must_use]
54: #[allow(clippy::cast_possible_truncation)]
55: pub fn now_ms() -> u64 {
56:     SystemTime::now()
57:         .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
58:         .map_or(0, |d| d.as_millis() as u64)
59: }
60: 
61: /// Clamp a value into `[min, max]`.
62: #[must_use]
63: pub fn clamp(value: f64, min: f64, max: f64) -> f64 {
64:     if value < min {
65:         min
66:     } else if value > max {
67:         max
68:     } else {
69:         value
70:     }
71: }
72: 
73: /// Compute the recency component in `(0.0, 1.0]`.
74: ///
75: /// Newer accesses score closer to `1.0`; older accesses decay exponentially.
76: #[must_use]
77: pub fn recency_score(age_ms: u64, half_life_ms: f64) -> f64 {
78:     if half_life_ms <= 0.0 {
79:         return 0.0;
80:     }
81:     let exponent = f64::from(u32::try_from(age_ms).unwrap_or(u32::MAX)) / half_life_ms;
82:     0.5f64.powf(exponent)
83: }
84: 
85: /// Compute the frequency component in `[0.0, 1.0)` with diminishing returns.
86: ///
87: /// Uses `1 - 1/(1 + n)` so the first few accesses matter most.
88: #[must_use]
89: pub fn frequency_score(access_count: u64) -> f64 {
90:     let n = f64::from(u32::try_from(access_count).unwrap_or(u32::MAX));
91:     1.0 - (1.0 / (1.0 + n))
92: }
93: 
94: /// Compute the age penalty in `[0.0, 1.0]`.
95: ///
96: /// Older entries receive a larger penalty (closer to `1.0`).
97: #[must_use]
98: pub fn age_penalty(age_ms: u64, half_life_ms: f64) -> f64 {
99:     if half_life_ms <= 0.0 {
100:         return 1.0;
101:     }
102:     let exponent = f64::from(u32::try_from(age_ms).unwrap_or(u32::MAX)) / half_life_ms;
103:     1.0 - 0.5f64.powf(exponent)
104: }
105: 
106: /// Compute the combined salience score in `[0.0, 1.0]`.
107: ///
108: /// The three weighted components (recency, frequency, age) are normalized by the
109: /// sum of their weights. A non-positive total weight is treated as a degenerate
110: /// configuration and yields a salience of `0.0` instead of panicking.
111: #[must_use]
112: pub fn compute_salience(input: &SalienceInput, config: &DecayConfig) -> f64 {
113:     let total = config.recency_weight + config.frequency_weight + config.age_weight;
114:     if total <= 0.0 {
115:         return 0.0;
116:     }
117: 
118:     let recency_age = input.now_ms.saturating_sub(input.last_accessed_at_ms);
119:     let creation_age = input.now_ms.saturating_sub(input.created_at_ms);
120: 
121:     let recency = recency_score(recency_age, config.recency_half_life_ms);
122:     let frequency = frequency_score(input.access_count);
123:     let age = age_penalty(creation_age, config.recency_half_life_ms);
124: 
125:     let raw = config.recency_weight * recency
126:         + config.frequency_weight * frequency
127:         + config.age_weight * (1.0 - age);
128: 
129:     clamp(raw / total, 0.0, 1.0)
130: }
131: 
132: /// Decide whether an entry should be evicted given a minimum salience threshold.
133: #[must_use]
134: pub fn should_evict(salience: f64, min_salience: f64) -> bool {
135:     salience < min_salience
136: }

50: pub(crate) async fn handle_index_project(

120:     if let Some(vector_store) = &state.vector_store {

142: 
143:         let results = stream::iter(batches)
144:             .map(|batch| {
145:                 let emb = embedder.clone();
146:                 tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
147:                     let texts: Vec<&str> = batch.iter().map(|(_, c)| c.as_str()).collect();
148:                     emb.embed_batch(&texts).map(|vectors| {

165: 
166:         let mut entries: Vec<VectorEntry> = Vec::with_capacity(persisted.len());
167:         for r in results {

183:     let embedding_dims = state.embedder.dimensions() as i64;

1: //! Deterministic indexing primitives for `IndexProject`.
2: //!
3: //! Kept dependency-light so indexing works offline with no model weights:
4: //! files are discovered, chunked deterministically, hashed, and stored with
5: //! their extracted entities. All functions are pure where possible so they can
6: //! be unit-tested independently of storage.
7: 
8: use std::path::Path;
9: 
10: use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};
11: 
12: /// A chunk produced by the deterministic chunker.
13: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
14: pub struct IndexedChunk {
15:     pub file_path: String,
16:     /// 1-based start line (inclusive).
17:     pub line_start: i32,
18:     /// 1-based start line (inclusive).
19:     pub line_end: i32,
20:     pub content: String,
21:     /// SHA-256 hex digest of the content.
22:     pub hash: String,
23:     /// Language hint inferred from the file extension.
24:     pub language: Option<String>,
25:     /// Simple chunk type tag ("code", "markdown", "text").
26:     pub chunk_type: String,
27: }
28: 
29: const DEFAULT_MAX_LINES: usize = 80;
30: const DEFAULT_OVERLAP_LINES: usize = 8;
31: 
32: /// Infer a language hint from a file path extension.
33: #[must_use]
34: pub fn infer_language(path: &Path) -> Option<&'static str> {
35:     let ext = path.extension()?.to_str()?.to_ascii_lowercase();
36:     match ext.as_str() {
37:         "rs" => Some("rust"),
38:         "py" => Some("python"),
39:         "js" | "jsx" | "ts" | "tsx" => Some("javascript"),
40:         "go" => Some("go"),
41:         "java" => Some("java"),
42:         "c" | "h" => Some("c"),
43:         "cpp" | "cc" | "cxx" | "hpp" => Some("cpp"),
44:         "rb" => Some("ruby"),
45:         "php" => Some("php"),
46:         "md" | "markdown" => Some("markdown"),
47:         _ => None,
48:     }
49: }
50: 
51: /// Classify a file as code, markdown or plain text for chunking purposes.
52: #[must_use]
53: pub fn classify(path: &Path) -> &'static str {
54:     match infer_language(path).map(str::to_ascii_lowercase) {
55:         Some(lang) if lang == "markdown" => "markdown",
56:         Some(_) => "code",
57:         None => "text",
58:     }
59: }
60: 
61: /// Split text into chunks of at most `max_lines` lines with `overlap` lines of
62: /// context shared between adjacent chunks.
63: #[must_use]
64: pub fn chunk_lines(content: &str, max_lines: usize, overlap: usize) -> Vec<(i32, i32, String)> {
65:     if content.is_empty() {
66:         return Vec::new();
67:     }
68: 
69:     let lines: Vec<&str> = content.lines().collect();
70:     let max_lines = max_lines.max(1);
71:     let overlap = overlap.min(max_lines.saturating_sub(1));
72: 
73:     let mut chunks = Vec::with_capacity(lines.len() / max_lines + 1);
74:     let mut start = 0usize;
75: 
76:     while start < lines.len() {
77:         let end = (start + max_lines).min(lines.len());
78:         let text = lines[start..end].join("\n");
79:         // 1-based line numbers.
80:         chunks.push((start as i32 + 1, end as i32, text));
81:         if end >= lines.len() {
82:             break;
83:         }
84:         start = end.saturating_sub(overlap);
85:     }
86: 
87:     chunks
88: }
89: 
90: /// Chunk a file's content, returning `IndexedChunk`s with language metadata.
91: #[must_use]
92: pub fn index_file(path: &Path, content: &str) -> Vec<IndexedChunk> {
93:     let language = infer_language(path).map(str::to_string);
94:     let chunk_type = classify(path);
95:     let file_path = path.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
96: 
97:     chunk_lines(content, DEFAULT_MAX_LINES, DEFAULT_OVERLAP_LINES)
98:         .into_iter()
99:         .map(|(line_start, line_end, text)| {
100:             let hash = hash_text(&text);
101:             IndexedChunk {
102:                 file_path: file_path.clone(),
103:                 line_start,
104:                 line_end,
105:                 content: text,
106:                 hash,
107:                 language: language.clone(),
108:                 chunk_type: chunk_type.to_string(),
109:             }
110:         })
111:         .collect()
112: }
113: 
114: /// SHA-256 hex digest of arbitrary text.
115: #[must_use]
116: pub fn hash_text(text: &str) -> String {
117:     let mut hasher = Sha256::new();
118:     hasher.update(text.as_bytes());
119:     hex::encode(hasher.finalize())
120: }

3: /// Configuration for salience decay scoring.

5: /// Uses exponential decay: `score * exp(-lambda * age_hours)`.

12:     pub enabled: bool,

30:             enabled: true,
31:         }

43:     /// Apply decay to a base score given the age in hours.
44:     ///
45:     /// Returns `base_score * exp(-lambda * age_hours)`.
46:     /// If decay is disabled, returns `base_score` unchanged.
47:     #[must_use]
48:     pub fn score(&self, base_score: f32, age_hours: f32) -> f32 {
49:         if !self.enabled || age_hours <= 0.0 {
50:             return base_score;
51:         }
52:         #[allow(clippy::cast_lossless, clippy::cast_possible_truncation)]
53:         let factor = (-self.lambda * f64::from(age_hours)).exp() as f32;
54:         base_score * factor

57:     /// Compute age in hours from a `last_accessed_at` unix timestamp (seconds).
58:     ///
59:     /// Returns 0.0 if the timestamp is in the future or if current time cannot be read.
60:     #[must_use]
61:     pub fn age_hours(last_accessed_at: i64) -> f32 {
62:         #[allow(clippy::cast_possible_wrap)]
63:         let now = SystemTime::now()
64:             .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)

71:         }

3: -- `qa_cache` stores digested answers (synthesized client-side) keyed by
4: -- (project, question_hash). The server is deterministic: it embeds, searches,
5: -- and stores — it never runs an LLM. A separate `usearch` index
6: -- (`question_vectors`) holds the question embeddings in their own vector space
7: -- (cosine metric) so cache lookup never mixes with the chunk vector space.
8: --
9: -- Staleness is tracked by `source_hashes` (content hashes of the chunks that
10: -- produced the answer); the lifecycle hook marks rows `stale` when their
11: -- chunks change. Manual invalidation (admin-gated by plan 018) supports a soft
12: -- `Stale` mark and a hard `Delete`, plus a similarity radius over
13: -- `question_vectors` to invalidate a whole error chain at once.
14: 
15: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS qa_cache (
16:     id                INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
17:     cache_id          TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,        -- UUIDv7, stable answer id (anti-drift)
18:     buffer_id         INTEGER,                     -- scoping by project/buffer
19:     project           TEXT NOT NULL,               -- redundant for fast lookup
20:     question_text     TEXT NOT NULL,               -- original question
21:     question_hash     TEXT NOT NULL,               -- exact-hit key (project, question_hash)
22:     answer_text       TEXT NOT NULL,               -- digested answer (from client)
23:     source_chunk_ids  TEXT,                        -- JSON array of chunk ids (provenance)
24:     source_hashes     TEXT,                        -- JSON array of chunk content hashes (invalidation)
25:     model             TEXT,                        -- LLM that synthesized (metadata, not a blocker)
26:     confidence        REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 1.0,   -- decays to 0 when stale
27:     tier_snapshot     TEXT,                        -- JSON of thresholds used (reproducibility)
28:     token_count       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,

30:     created_at        INTEGER NOT NULL,
31:     last_accessed_at  INTEGER NOT NULL,
32:     stale             INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,  -- 0/1
33:     invalidated_at    INTEGER,                     -- epoch ms of manual invalidation (audit)
34:     invalidated_by    TEXT,                        -- username (audit)

1: //! Semantic query-answer cache persistence (plan 017).
2: //!
3: //! The server stores *digested* answers here (synthesized client-side). Lookup
4: //! by `(project, question_hash)` gives exact hits; similarity hits are resolved
5: //! by the caller against the dedicated `question_vectors` index
6: //! (`crate::qa_vectors`). `source_hashes` drive staleness: when a source chunk
7: //! changes, the lifecycle hook marks the row `stale` so the next query forces a
8: //! re-digest.
9: //!
10: //! All queries go through [`super::conn::Storage::connection`], which is safe in
11: //! both single (CLI) and pooled (server) modes.
12: 
13: use anyhow::{Context, Result};
14: use rusqlite::OptionalExtension;
15: use rusqlite::params;
16: 
17: use super::conn::Storage;
18: use super::tokens::now_ms;

20: /// A stored query-answer cache row.
21: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
22: pub struct QaCacheRow {

```rust
use anyhow::Result;
use arlm_memory::consolidation::{ConsolidateOptions, ConsolidationEngine};
use arlm_search::decay::DecayConfig;
use arlm_storage::Storage;
use crate::store;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct MaintenanceReport {
    pub duplicate_chunks_removed: u64,
    pub low_confidence_patterns_removed: u64,
    pub decayed_chunks: u64,
    pub kept: u64,
}

pub async fn list_project_buffer_ids(storage: &Storage) -> Result<Vec<i64>> {
    let projects = store::list_projects(storage)?;
    Ok(projects.into_iter().map(|p| p.id).collect())
}

pub async fn consolidate(project: &str, storage: &Storage) -> Result<MaintenanceReport> {
    let buffer_ids = resolve_buffers(storage, project).await?;
    let engine = ConsolidationEngine::new(storage.clone());
    let mut report = MaintenanceReport::default();
    for bid in buffer_ids {
        let res = engine.consolidate(bid, &ConsolidateOptions::default())?;
        report.duplicate_chunks_removed += res.duplicate_chunks_removed;
        report.low_confidence_patterns_removed += res.low_confidence_patterns_removed;
    }
    Ok(report)
}
```

For decay:
```rust
pub async fn decay(project: &str, storage: &Storage, score_floor: f32) -> Result<MaintenanceReport> {
    let buffer_ids = resolve_buffers(storage, project).await?;
    let decay_cfg = DecayConfig::default();
    let mut report = MaintenanceReport::default();
    for bid in buffer_ids {
        // fetch chunk ids with last_accessed_at
        let rows = storage.conn()... query
        for each chunk:
            let age_hours = DecayConfig::age_hours(last_accessed_at)
            let decayed = decay_cfg.score(1.0, age_hours)
            if decayed < score_floor { delete; report.decayed_chunks+=1 } else { report.kept+=1 }
    }
    Ok(report)
}
```

pub fn load() -> Result<Self> {
    let path = std::env::var("ARLM_SERVER_CONFIG")
        .map(PathBuf::from)
        .unwrap_or_else(|_| PathBuf::from("/etc/arlm/server.toml"));
    if path.exists() {
        let contents = std::fs::read_to_string(&path).with_context(...)?;
        let mut config: ServerConfig = toml::from_str(&contents)...?;
        // env overrides
        if let Ok(addr) = std::env::var("ARLM_SERVER_ADDR") { config.listen_addr = addr; }
        if let Ok(dir) = std::env::var("ARLM_DATA_DIR") { config.data_dir = PathBuf::from(dir); }
        return Ok(config);
    }
    // No file: build defaults with env overrides.
    let mut config = Self::default();
    if let Ok(addr) = std::env::var("ARLM_SERVER_ADDR") { config.listen_addr = addr; }
    if let Ok(dir) = std::env::var("ARLM_DATA_DIR") { config.data_dir = PathBuf::from(dir); }
    Ok(config)
}
```

```rust
fn remove_duplicate_chunks(&self, buffer_id: i64, dry_run: bool) -> Result<u64> {
    // gather duplicate hashes
    let hashes = ...;
    let mut removed = 0;
    for h in hashes {
        if dry_run {
            let cnt: u64 = conn.query_row("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM chunks WHERE buffer_id=?1 AND hash=?2", ...)?;
            // but that counts all including the one we'd keep; we keep first, remove rest => cnt-1
            removed += cnt.saturating_sub(1);
        } else {
            let deleted = conn.execute("DELETE FROM chunks WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM chunks WHERE buffer_id=?1 AND hash=?2 ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT -1 OFFSET 1)")?;
            removed += deleted as u64;
        }
    }
    Ok(removed)
}
```

```rust
use anyhow::Result;
use arlm_memory::consolidation::{ConsolidateOptions, ConsolidationEngine};
use arlm_search::decay::DecayConfig;
use arlm_storage::Storage;
use rusqlite::params;

use crate::store;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct MaintenanceReport {
    pub duplicate_chunks_removed: u64,
    pub low_confidence_patterns_removed: u64,
    pub decayed_chunks: u64,
    pub kept: u64,
}

impl MaintenanceReport {
    fn merge(&mut self, other: &MaintenanceReport) {
        self.duplicate_chunks_removed += other.duplicate_chunks_removed;
        self.low_confidence_patterns_removed += other.low_confidence_patterns_removed;
        self.decayed_chunks += other.decayed_chunks;
        self.kept += other.kept;
    }
}

async fn resolve_buffer_ids(storage: &Storage, project: &str) -> Result<Vec<i64>> {
    if project.is_empty() {
        let projects = store::list_projects(storage)?;
        Ok(projects.into_iter().map(|p| p.id).collect())
    } else {
        match store::buffer_id_for_project(storage, project)? {
            Some(id) => Ok(vec![id]),
            None => Ok(Vec::new()),
        }
    }
}

pub async fn consolidate(project: &str, storage: &Storage, dry_run: bool) -> Result<MaintenanceReport> {
    let buffer_ids = resolve_buffer_ids(storage, project).await?;
    let engine = ConsolidationEngine::new(storage.clone());
    let mut report = MaintenanceReport::default();
    for bid in buffer_ids {
        let res = engine.consolidate(bid, &ConsolidateOptions { dry_run, ..Default::default() })?;
        report.duplicate_chunks_removed += res.duplicate_chunks_removed;
        report.low_confidence_patterns_removed += res.low_confidence_patterns_removed;
    }
    Ok(report)
}

pub async fn decay(project: &str, storage: &Storage, score_floor: f32, dry_run: bool) -> Result<MaintenanceReport> {
    let buffer_ids = resolve_buffer_ids(storage, project).await?;
    let decay_cfg = DecayConfig::default();
    let storage = storage.clone();
    let mut report = MaintenanceReport::default();
    for bid in buffer_ids {
        let removed = crate::store::blocking({
            let storage = storage.clone();
            move || run_decay_for_buffer(&storage, bid, &decay_cfg, score_floor, dry_run)
        }).await?;
        report.decayed_chunks += removed.decayed_chunks;
        report.kept += removed.kept;
    }
    Ok(report)
}

struct DecayCount { decayed_chunks: u64, kept: u64 }

fn run_decay_for_buffer(storage: &Storage, buffer_id: i64, decay_cfg: &DecayConfig, score_floor: f32, dry_run: bool) -> Result<DecayCount> {
    let conn = storage.conn();
    let conn = conn.lock();
    let mut stmt = conn.prepare("SELECT id, last_accessed_at FROM chunks WHERE buffer_id = ?1")?;
    let rows: Vec<(i64, i64)> = stmt.query_map(params![buffer_id], |r| Ok((r.get(0)?, r.get(1)?)))?.filter_map(Result::ok).collect();
    let mut count = DecayCount { decayed_chunks: 0, kept: 0 };
    for (id, last_accessed) in rows {
        let age = DecayConfig::age_hours(last_accessed);
        let decayed = decay_cfg.score(1.0, age);
        if decayed < score_floor {
            count.decayed_chunks += 1;
            if !dry_run {
                crate::store::chunks::delete_chunk(storage, id)?; // careful: storage is &Storage; but we hold conn lock! 
            }
        } else {
            count.kept += 1;
        }
    }
    Ok(count)
}
```

pub async fn handle_trigger_maintenance(state, request) -> Result<Response<MaintenanceReport>, Status> {
    let ctx = authenticate(...)?;
    require_admin(&ctx)?;
    let req = request.into_inner();
    let storage = state.storage.clone();
    let floor = state.config.maintenance.decay_score_floor;
    let cons = maintenance::consolidate(&req.project, &storage, req.dry_run).await.map_err(internal)?;
    let dec = maintenance::decay(&req.project, &storage, floor, req.dry_run).await.map_err(internal)?;
    let mut report = cons; report.merge(&dec);
    Ok(Response::new(MaintenanceReport { duplicate_chunks_removed: report.duplicate_chunks_removed as i64, ... }))
}

pub fn chunk_file_paths(storage: &Storage, ids: &[i64]) -> Result<Vec<String>> {
    if ids.is_empty() { return Ok(vec![]); }
    let conn = storage.connection()?;
    conn.execute(|conn| {
        let placeholders = ...;
        let sql = format!("SELECT DISTINCT file_path FROM chunks WHERE id IN ({})", placeholders);

        Ok(rows)
    })
}

pub async fn handle_list_memory(state: &AppState, request: Request<ListMemoryRequest>) -> Result<Response<ListMemoryResponse>, Status> {
    let ctx = crate::auth::authenticate(request.metadata(), &state.storage)?;
    crate::auth::require_admin(&ctx)?;
    let req = request.into_inner();
    let limit = if req.limit > 0 { req.limit } else { 100 };
    let storage = state.storage.clone();
    let project = req.project.clone();
    let rows = crate::store::blocking(move || list_memory_rows(&storage, &project, limit)).await.map_err(internal)?;
    let entries = rows.into_iter().map(|r| MemoryEntry {
        cache_id: r.cache_id,
        project: r.project,
        question: r.question_text,
        created_at: r.created_at.to_string(),
        score: r.confidence,
        entities: Vec::new(),
    }).collect();
    let stats = format!("project={} entries={} include_entities={}", req.project, rows.len(), req.include_entities);
    Ok(Response::new(ListMemoryResponse { entries, stats }))
}

fn list_memory_rows(storage: &Storage, project: &str, limit: i64) -> anyhow::Result<Vec<QaMemoryRow>> {
    let conn = storage.connection()?;
    conn.execute(|conn| {
        let (sql, params_vec): (String, Vec<Box<dyn rusqlite::types::ToSql>>) = if project.is_empty() {
            ("SELECT cache_id, project, question_text, created_at, confidence FROM qa_cache ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT ?1".to_string(), vec![Box::new(limit)])
        } else {
            ("SELECT cache_id, project, question_text, created_at, confidence FROM qa_cache WHERE project = ?1 ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT ?2".to_string(), vec![Box::new(project), Box::new(limit)])
        };
        let mut stmt = conn.prepare(&sql).context("prepare list_memory")?;
        let refs: Vec<&dyn rusqlite::types::ToSql> = params_vec.iter().map(AsRef::as_ref).collect();
        let rows = stmt.query_map(refs.as_slice(), |r| Ok(QaMemoryRow { cache_id: r.get(0)?, project: r.get(1)?, question_text: r.get(2)?, created_at: r.get(3)?, confidence: r.get(4)? }))?
            .filter_map(Result::ok).collect();
        Ok(rows)
    })
}
```

```rust
pub async fn handle_get_cache(state: &AppState, request: Request<GetCacheRequest>) -> Result<Response<GetCacheResponse>, Status> {
    let ctx = authenticate; require_admin;
    let req = request.into_inner();
    if req.cache_id.trim().is_empty() { return Err(invalid_arg("cache_id is required")); }
    let storage = state.storage.clone();
    let cache_id = req.cache_id.clone();
    let row = crate::store::blocking(move || arlm_storage::qa_cache::get_qa_by_cache_id(&storage, &cache_id)).await.map_err(internal)?;
    match row {
        Some(r) => {
            let ids: Vec<i64> = r.source_chunk_ids.iter().filter_map(|s| s.parse::<i64>().ok()).collect();
            let files = if ids.is_empty() { Vec::new() } else {
                let storage = state.storage.clone();
                crate::store::blocking(move || crate::store::chunks::chunk_file_paths(&storage, &ids)).await.map_err(internal)?
            };
            Ok(Response::new(GetCacheResponse {
                answer: r.answer_text,
                source_chunk_ids: r.source_chunk_ids,
                files,
                project: r.project,
            }))
        }
        None => Ok(Response::new(GetCacheResponse::default())),
    }
}
```

pub async fn handle_trigger_maintenance(state: &AppState, request: Request<TriggerMaintenanceRequest>) -> Result<Response<MaintenanceReport>, Status> {
    let ctx = authenticate; require_admin;
    let req = request.into_inner();
    let storage = state.storage.clone();
    let project = req.project.clone();
    let floor = state.config.maintenance.decay_score_floor;
    let report = crate::maintenance::run_maintenance(&project, &storage, floor, req.dry_run).await.map_err(internal)?;
    Ok(Response::new(MaintenanceReport {
        duplicate_chunks_removed: i64::try_from(report.duplicate_chunks_removed).unwrap_or(i64::MAX),
        low_confidence_patterns_removed: i64::try_from(report.low_confidence_patterns_removed).unwrap_or(i64::MAX),
        decayed_chunks: i64::try_from(report.decayed_chunks).unwrap_or(i64::MAX),
        kept: i64::try_from(report.kept).unwrap_or(i64::MAX),
    }))
}

```rust
pub async fn handle_get_history(state: &AppState, request: Request<GetHistoryRequest>) -> Result<Response<GetHistoryResponse>, Status> {
    let ctx = crate::auth::authenticate(request.metadata(), &state.storage)?; // UNAUTHENTICATED if missing
    let req = request.into_inner();
    // Scope by user: admin may query any user (or all when empty); others are forced to their own.
    let user_filter: Option<String> = if ctx.is_admin() {
        if req.user.trim().is_empty() { None } else { Some(req.user.trim().to_string()) }
    } else {
        Some(ctx.username.clone())
    };
    let limit = if req.limit > 0 { req.limit } else { 50 };
    let storage = state.storage.clone();
    let records = crate::store::blocking(move || {
        let mgr = arlm_memory::HistoryManager::new(storage);
        mgr.recent_opt_user(user_filter.as_deref(), limit)
    }).await.map_err(internal)?;
    let entries = records.into_iter().map(|r| HistoryEntry {
        id: r.id,
        user: r.user.unwrap_or_default(),
        question: r.query,
        created_at: r.created_at.to_string(),
        cache_id: String::new(),
    }).collect();
    Ok(Response::new(GetHistoryResponse { entries }))
}
```

Per-user query history RPC (plan 019, E).\n//!\n//! `GetHistory` is scoped by the authenticated caller: admins may query any\n//! `user` (or all users when `user` is empty); non-admins are forced to their\n//! own `username`. Without a session the call returns `UNAUTHENTICATED`.\n\nuse arlm_proto::proto::*;\nuse tonic::{Request, Response, Status};\n\nuse crate::auth;\nuse crate::grpc::error::internal;\nuse crate::state::AppState;\nuse crate::store;\n\n/// Fetch per-user query history (auth-scoped).\n///\n/// # Errors\n///\n/// Returns `UNAUTHENTICATED` without a session, or `internal` on storage failure.\npub async fn handle_get_history(\n    state: &AppState,\n    request: Request<GetHistoryRequest>,\n) -> Result<Response<GetHistoryResponse>, Status> {\n    // No session → unauthenticated (plan 019, E).\n    let ctx = auth::authenticate(request.metadata(), &state.storage)?;\n\n    let req = request.into_inner();\n\n    // Scope: admin may read any user (or all); others are pinned to themselves.\n    let user_filter: Option<String> = if ctx.is_admin() {\n        if req.user.trim().is_empty() {\n            None\n        } else {\n            Some(req.user.trim().to_string())\n        }\n    } else {\n        Some(ctx.username.clone())\n    };\n\n    let limit = if req.limit > 0 { req.limit } else { 50 };\n\n    let storage = state.storage.clone();\n    let records = store::blocking(move || {\n        let mgr = arlm_memory::HistoryManager::new(storage);\n        mgr.recent_opt_user(user_filter.as_deref(), limit)\n    })\n    .await\n    .map_err(internal)?;\n\n    let entries = records\n        .into_iter()\n        .map(|r| HistoryEntry {\n            id: r.id,\n            user: r.user.unwrap_or_default(),\n            question: r.query,\n            created_at: r.created_at.to_string(),\n            cache_id: String::new(),\n        })\n        .collect();\n\n    Ok(Response::new(GetHistoryResponse { entries }))\n}\n",

3: ## Context
4: 
5: Os planos 017 (QA-Cache, digestão no client) e 018 (auth por refresh token) estabeleceram a
6: filosofia **on-demand, agent-agnostic, sem LLM no servidor**. O projeto acumulou, porém, um

11: - `arlm run` dispara um loop recursivo `planner → solver → synthesizer` que **não existe mais** na
12:   arquitetura sob demanda. A filosofia agora é "processamento sob demanda via `-qa`".

21: conjunto enxuto e coerente (init/index/search/query/memory/persist/history), **remove o legado
22: RLM** de ponta a ponta (core → server → proto → cli → storage), e **repensa** os comandos
23: `persist` e `history` e a gestão de memória (`cache`+`decay`+`entities` → `arlm memory` admin).

84: ## Architecture Overview
85: 
86: ```
87:  CLIENT (arlm-cli)                              SERVER (arlm-server, sem LLM)
88:  ┌────────────────────────────┐                ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
89:  │ init   → scaffold .arlm/ + index            │ gRPC business:                        │
90:  │ index  → ingestão local → gRPC IndexProject │   IndexProject, Search, QueryWithCache │
91:  │ search → gRPC Search                        │   StoreAnswer, GetAnswerById          │
92:  │ query  → -qa digest no client (arlm-llm)    │   InvalidateCache (admin)             │
93:  │         --cache-id lookup 1:1               │   ListMemory / GetCache (admin)       │
94:  │ memory (admin) → List/Get/Invalidate/Cleanup│   TriggerMaintenance (admin)          │
95:  │ persist <id> → resumo via arlm-llm →        │   GetHistory {user} (por usuário)     │
96:  │   wiki/yyyymmddhhmm_title.md                │                                        │
97:  │ history → GetHistory(user)                  │ Maintenance (interno, sem gRPC):       │
98:  │                                            │   consolidate() + decay() a cada tick │
99:  │  auth_client: AuthRefresh → bearer          │   (cron via [maintenance] interval)   │
100:  └────────────────────────────┘                └──────────────────────────────────────┘
101: ```

194: (session); o interceptor exige `role=admin` (reuso do `require_admin`).
195: 
196: | Subcomando | RPC (server) | Ação |
197: |---|---|---|
198: | `list [--project P] [--limit N] [--include-entities]` | `ListMemory` | visualiza entradas `qa_cache` + stats + (opcional) entidades dos chunks |
199: | `get <cache_id>` | `GetCache` | busca resposta por id (admin/debug; usuário comum usa `arlm query --cache-id`) |
200: | `invalidate [--cache-id C] [--project P] [--radius R] [--delete] [--reason S]` | `InvalidateCache` (plan 017/018) | marca `stale` (soft) ou `--delete` (hard); `--radius` invalida vizinhos; sem `--cache-id` purga `result_cache` legado do `--project` |
201: | `cleanup [--dry-run] [--project P]` | `TriggerMaintenance` | limpeza forçada de memória: **decay** (chunks com score < 0.1) + **consolidate** (dedupe + low-confidence) no server |
202: 
203: O `arlm query --cache-id <id>` (consumer/anti-drift do plan 017) **permanece** sob `query`, não
204: sob `memory` — é o caminho determinístico do usuário final.
205: 
206: ### C.1 Manutenção server-side (consolidate + decay)
207: - Novo módulo `arlm-server/src/maintenance.rs`: `consolidate(project)` usa
208:   `arlm_memory::ConsolidationEngine`; `decay(project)` usa `arlm_search::decay::DecayConfig`
209:   (já existe) sobre `arlm_storage`. Ambos retornam um `MaintenanceReport`
210:   (`duplicate_chunks_removed`, `low_confidence_patterns_removed`, `decayed_chunks`, `kept`).
211: - **Admin RPC** `TriggerMaintenance { project, dry_run }` → `MaintenanceReport`.
212: - **CLI interno** `arlm-server admin consolidate [--dry-run] [--project P]` (abre `Storage`
213:   direto, sem gRPC — igual ao `admin create-refresh`).
214: - **Cron**: `arlm-server` config ganha `[maintenance] interval_secs` (default ex.: 3600; `0` =
215:   desliga). Na `lifecycle`, um `tokio::spawn` dispara `consolidate+decay` a cada tick (e também
216:   logo após `index`, para manter a memória fresca).
217: 
218: ---
219: 
220: ## D. `arlm persist` (rework)
221: 
222: - Uso: `arlm persist <response_id> [--title T]`. `<response_id>` é o `cache_id` emitido por
223:   `arlm query -qa` (plan 017 já emite `cache_id` em todos os formatos).
224: - Fluxo:
225:   1. Exibe o `response_id` ao usuário.
226:   2. `GetAnswerById(response_id)` → `answer_text` + `source_chunk_ids` + arquivos (provenance).
227:   3. Executa resumo **via IA real do usuário** (`arlm-llm` + `~/.arlm/arlm.toml`, igual ao `query -qa`)
228:      com prompt de sumarização fixo + os artefatos (trechos fonte), produzindo um documento.
229:   4. Escreve `wiki/<yyyymmddhhmm>_<slug(title)>.md` (pasta `wiki/` relativa ao projeto; sem git).
230: - **Estrutura fixa** do documento:
231:   ```markdown

233: 
234:   - **Response ID:** <cache_id>
235:   - **Generated:** <yyyymmddhhmm>
236:   - **Model:** <model>
237:   - **Project:** <project>
238:   - **Provenance:** <chunk_ids / file_paths>
239: 
240:   ## Summary
241:   <resumo gerado pela IA>
242: 
243:   ## Key Findings / Artifacts
244:   <lista estruturada de arquivos fonte + snippets relevantes>
245: 
246:   ## Related
247:   <refs / queries derivadas>
248:   ```
249: - Remove-se `save_page` (usado por run/context) e o uso de `PersistEngine` solto; `persist`
250:   vira o único dono da pasta `wiki/`.

254: ## E. `arlm history` (por usuário, atrelado ao refresh token)
255: 
256: - Atual `HistoryManager` (cliente, lê SQLite local) → **server-side**: o server registra cada
257:   query em `history` com a coluna `user` (do `AuthContext` do plan 018). Migration adiciona
258:   `user TEXT` a `history`.
259: - RPC `GetHistory { user, limit }`: usuário vê **só suas** queries; `admin` vê todas (ou filtra
260:   por `user`). Sem sessão → `UNAUTHENTICATED`.
261: - `arlm history [--limit N]` (default 20) chama `GetHistory` com o `username` do token; remove a
262:   seção "runs" (morta).
263: - Respeita o princípio "histórico útil a nível do próprio usuário, atrelado ao refresh token".

267: ## F. Justificativas das remoções
268: 
269: - **`session`**: as `sessions` (multi-turn, migration 006) existiam para rastrear contextos/
270:   turnos de um **run RLM de longa duração**. Com on-demand `-qa` não há sessão multi-turno a
271:   rastrear; o `history` por usuário já cobre o que o usuário precisa. Removem-se comando, RPCs e
272:   tabelas `sessions`/`session_contexts`/`session_history`.
273: - **`context`**: `arlm context <task>` monta janela de contexto (busca híbrida) sem LLM — é
274:   **redundante** com `arlm query` quando nenhum `--llm` está configurado (query já devolve o
275:   contexto). Consolidar em `query`.
276: - **`status`/`cost`/`cancel`/`checkpoints`**: 100% atrelados a `runs`/`trajectories` (tabelas
277:   mortas). Sem o engine, não têm objeto.
278: - **`restore-page`**: reconstruía página a partir de busca FTS — desnecessário com o `persist`
279:   estruturado e o `query`.
280: - **`wiki` (comando)**: gestão de repo git de knowledge base **não é responsabilidade do
281:   projeto**. O `persist` apenas escreve arquivos markdown numa pasta `wiki/` (sem git).
282: - **`consolidate`/`decay` (CLI)**: lógica determinística que pertence ao **servidor** (dono do
283:   DB compartilhado) e deve rodar periodicamente (cron), não sob demanda no client de cada dev.
