90: ## Schema: `server.toml` (server-only, arquivo do HOST montado no container)
91: 
92: > É um arquivo **do host**, versionado/provido pelo operador e montado no container
93: > (`docker compose`/`docker -v`: `./server.toml:/etc/arlm/server.toml`). Dentro do container,
94: > lido de `/etc/arlm/server.toml` (ou `ARLM_SERVER_CONFIG`). **Não** é gerado pelo client nem
95: > vive no `~/.arlm` do client.
96: 
97: ```toml
98: # ── Servir / receber ───────────────────────────────────────────────
99: listen_addr = "0.0.0.0:50051"        # (env ARLM_SERVER_ADDR sobrescreve)
100: tls_cert = "/etc/arlm/tls/server.crt"   # optional → habilita TLS
101: tls_key  = "/etc/arlm/tls/server.key"   # optional
102: # mtls_ca = "/etc/arlm/tls/ca.crt"       # optional → exige client cert
103: 
104: # ── Armazenamento / dados ─────────────────────────────────────────
105: data_dir = "/var/lib/arlm"           # (env ARLM_DATA_DIR sobrescreve)
106: pool_size = 4
107: flush_interval_ms = 100
108: max_batch_size = 50
109: 
110: # ── Processamento de dados (chunk + embed) — EXCLUSIVO do server ───
111: [embedder]
112: model = "bge-m3"                     # bge-m3 | ollama | lightweight
113: model_dir = "/models/bge-m3"         # p/ bge-m3
114: ollama_url = "http://localhost:11434"
115: ollama_model = "nomic-embed-text-v2-moe"
116: dims = 1024
117: batch_size = 32
118: max_tokens = 512                     # tamanho do chunk
119: overlap_tokens = 64
120: cache = true
121: 
122: # ── Busca (defaults aplicados pelo server) ────────────────────────
123: [search]
124: tier = "hybrid"
125: top_k = 10
126: max_tokens = 8000
127: 
128: # ── Cache semântico (plan 017) ────────────────────────────────────
129: [qa_cache]
130: novel_k = 20
131: provenance_k = 5
132: sim_high = 0.90
133: sim_floor = 0.40
134: tier_steps = [0.90, 0.80, 0.70, 0.60, 0.50]
135: jaccard_min = 0.5
136: question_vector_dims = 1024
137: max_entries_per_project = 1000
138: eviction_lambda_ms = 604800000
139: eviction_interval_ms = 60000
140: 
141: # ── Manutenção (decay + consolidate, plan 019) ────────────────────
142: [maintenance]
143: interval_secs = 3600                 # 0 = desliga
144: decay_score_floor = 0.1
145: ```
146: 
147: **Removidos do server:** seção `[llm]` (server) — o server fica sem LLM (plan 017/019).
148: 
149: ### Schema: `~/.arlm/arlm.toml` (global, user)
150: 
151: ```toml
152: [auth]
153: username = "dev1"
154: refresh_token = "<token gerado por arlm-server admin create-refresh>"
155: 
156: [llm]
157: backends = [
158:   { name = "default", kind = "openai", model = "gpt-4o-mini",
159:     api_key = "env:OPENAI_API_KEY", base_url = null },
160: ]
161: 
162: [server]
163: addr = "https://arlm.corp.internal:50051"
164: ```
165: 
166: ### Schema: `.arlm.toml` (local, projeto, gitignored)
167: 
168: ```toml
169: [project]
170: name = "meu-repo"
171: ignore = ["target/", "node_modules/", "*.lock"]
172: 
173: # overrides opcionais (granular fallback p/ o global quando ausentes):
174: [server]
175: addr = "http://localhost:50051"      # sobrescreve o global p/ este projeto
176: 
177: [llm]
178: backends = [ { name = "default", kind = "ollama", model = "qwen2.5-coder:7b" } ]
179: ```
180: 
181: **Não** se copia `auth` para o local: identidade é global; com fallback granular, o local herda
182: `auth` do global. `arlm init` gera apenas `[project]` (+ overrides desejados) e **não** grava o
183: `refresh_token` no repo.
184: 
185: ---
186: 
187: ## Merge granular (client)
188: 
189: `EffectiveUserConfig = merge(global ~/.arlm/arlm.toml, local .arlm.toml)`:
190: 
191: - Deserializa ambos na **mesma** struct (todos os campos `Option` ou tabelas aninhadas opcionais).
192: - Para cada campo escalar: `local.field.or(global.field)`.
193: - Para tabelas aninhadas (`[llm]`, `[server]`, `[project]`): merge **recursivo** campo a campo
194:   (granular), não substituição da tabela inteira.
195: - Resultado efetivo é o que o client usa para `auth`, `llm` e `server.addr`.
196: 
197: Implementação: `crate::user_config` com `fn load() -> EffectiveUserConfig` que lê
198: global, lê local (se existir), e `fn merge(a, b)`. Substitui `Config::load` (`config.rs`) e
199: `ClientConfig::load` (`client.rs`).
200: 
201: ### Cliente puro gRPC (consequência de D3 — sem modo offline)
202: 
203: Com o modo offline removido, o `arlm-cli` deixa de ser um data plane local. **Tudo** passa pelo
204: `arlm-server` (gRPC/TLS), exceto a síntese/summarize que usa o **LLM do próprio usuário** localmente
205: (plan 017/020: `auth` + `llm` vêm do `~/.arlm/arlm.toml`).
206: 
207: - **Removidos do client**: `dispatch/local.rs` (branch local), `arlm_storage::Storage::open`
208:   local, `embedding.rs`/`build_embedder_from_config` (client não embeda), busca/contexto locais,
209:   vector store local, `data_dir()` como DB. O client **não** possui `knowledge.db` local.
210: - **Comandos sobreviventes viram chamadas gRPC puras** (server é a fonte de verdade):
211:   - `index` → `IndexProject` (client descobre arquivos no FS e envia **texto cru**; server chunka).
212:   - `search`/`query` → `Search`/`QueryWithCache` (server embeda a query e busca).
213:   - `memory` → `ListMemory`/`GetCache`/`InvalidateCache`/`TriggerMaintenance` (admin).
214:   - `persist` → `GetAnswerById` (server) + LLM do usuário local (summarize) + escrita do
215:     `wiki/...md` **local** (o `.arlm.toml`/`~/.arlm` do client só guarda config, não DB).
216:   - `history` → `GetHistory` (server, por `username`).
217:   - `init` → gera `.arlm.toml` + dispara `index`.
218: - O `--server`/endereço vem de `user_config` (`server.addr` global ou override local);
219:   `ARLM_SERVER_ADDR` ainda funciona como override de env (equivalente a setar `server.addr`).
220: 
221: ---
222: 
223: ## Decisões (confirmadas pelo usuário)
224: 
225: - **D1 — `server.toml` é arquivo do HOST, montado no container.** Não vive "dentro" do repo nem é
226:   gerado pelo client. O `docker compose`/`docker -v` mapeia `./server.toml` →
227:   `/etc/arlm/server.toml` (dentro do container; `ARLM_SERVER_CONFIG` sobrescreve o caminho
228:   interno). `ARLM_SERVER_ADDR`/`ARLM_DATA_DIR` continuam como overrides de env. O arquivo é
229:   disjunto do `~/.arlm/arlm.toml` do client.
230: - **D2 — Server faz o chunking.** O client transmite o conteúdo **cru** do arquivo
231:   (`IndexFile` com texto); o server fragmenta usando `[embedder].max_tokens/overlap_tokens`,
232:   embeda e armazena. O client **não controla** o server. *Muda o protocolo de index.*
233: - **D3 — Modo offline REMOVIDO.** Tudo depende do `arlm-server`. Quem quiser "offline" sobe o
234:   próprio container e cria seu server. O client é puro gRPC + LLM do usuário local (digest/
235:   summarize). `dispatch/local.rs` e todo branch local de `Storage`/embed/search/chunk do client
236:   são **eliminados**.
237: - **D4 — Sem transição.** Break total, sem retrocompatibilidade. O legado `~/.arlm/config.toml` /
238:   `.arlm/config.toml` é **ignorado** (não há fallback nem warning).
239: - **D5 — Auth global, vinculado ao server.** `[auth]` existe **só** em `~/.arlm/arlm.toml`
240:   (global). O `.arlm.toml` local não define `auth`; o merge o ignora se presente. Identidade é
241:   única e global.
242: 
243: ---
244: 
245: ## Configs que SURGEM da refatoração (019) — onde ficam
246: 
247: | Config nova | Escopo | Onde |
248: |---|---|---|
249: | `[maintenance] interval_secs` + `decay_score_floor` | servir/manter dados | **server.toml** (`[maintenance]`) |
250: | thresholds de `cleanup` (decay+consolidate) | manutenção | **server.toml** `[maintenance]` |
251: | `embedder.max_tokens` (chunk) / `overlap_tokens` / `dims` / `model` / `ollama_*` | processar dados | **server.toml** `[embedder]` (sai do client) |
252: | `search.tier/top_k/max_tokens` (defaults) | servir busca | **server.toml** `[search]` (sai do client) |
253: | `history` retention (opcional) | dados | **server.toml** (ex.: `[history] retention_days`) |
254: | `tls` / `mtls_ca` | segurança/servir | **server.toml** (`tls_cert`/`tls_key`/`mtls_ca`) |
255: | `[project].name` / `[project].ignore` | escopo do repo (não dado) | **`.arlm.toml` local** (client, só p/ descobrir arquivos) |
256: | `auth.username` / `refresh_token` | identidade user | **`~/.arlm/arlm.toml` global** |
257: | `llm.backends` (IA do user) | consumo de IA | **`~/.arlm/arlm.toml` global** (+ override local) |
258: | `server.addr` (client connect) | alvo do server | **user config** (global + override local) |
259: 
260: Removidas: `ServerConfig.llm` (server), `Config.agent` (`max_depth`/`max_nodes`), top-level
261: `backend`/`model` soltos do client (absorvidos por `llm.backends`), `Config.embedding` (vai p/
262: server).
263: 
264: ---
265: 
266: ## Where to Implement
267: 
268: | Componente | Crate | Arquivo(s) |
269: |---|---|---|
270: | `server.toml` schema + load (host mount) | `arlm-server` | `src/config.rs` (rework: remover `llm`, add `embedder`/`search`/`maintenance`/`tls.mtls_ca`; `load` de `ARLM_SERVER_CONFIG` default `/etc/arlm/server.toml`) |
271: | Remover `[llm]` server + `build_llm` (019) | `arlm-server` | `config.rs`, `lifecycle.rs`, `state.rs` |
272: | User config 2-escopos + merge granular (auth só global) | `arlm-cli` | `src/user_config.rs` (novo); rework `src/config.rs` (apenas auth/llm/server) |
273: | `arlm init` gera `.arlm.toml` + gitignore | `arlm-cli` | `src/commands/init.rs` (019) + `user_config` |
274: | Client puro gRPC: remove modo offline | `arlm-cli` | **remover** `dispatch/local.rs`; `dispatch/server.rs` vira o único dispatch; **remover** `arlm_storage::Storage::open` local, `embedding.rs`, busca/contexto locais, vector store local, `util::data_dir` como DB; `query.rs`/`search.rs` chamam só gRPC |
275: | Client lê `server.addr` do merge | `arlm-cli` | `src/client.rs`, `dispatch/server.rs`, `auth_client.rs` |
276: | Index protocolo: client manda **cru**, server chunka (D2) | `arlm-proto`+`arlm-server`+`arlm-cli` | `proto` (`IndexFile` texto cru), `grpc/index.rs` (server chunka/embeda), `commands/index.rs` (019) |
277: | Admin print path update | `arlm-server` | `src/admin.rs` (mensagem → `~/.arlm/arlm.toml`) |
278: | Break total: ignorar legacy `config.toml` | `arlm-cli` | `user_config::load` **não** lê `~/.arlm/config.toml`/`.arlm/config.toml` (sem fallback) |
279: 
280: ---
281: 
282: ## Implementation Steps
283: 
284: 1. **Server config rework**: `ServerConfig` recebe `embedder`/`search`/`maintenance`/`mtls_ca`;
285:    remove `llm` + `build_llm`; `load()` de `ARLM_SERVER_CONFIG` (default `/etc/arlm/server.toml`),
286:    mantendo `ARLM_SERVER_ADDR`/`ARLM_DATA_DIR`.
287: 2. **Client user_config**: novo `user_config.rs` com struct (auth/llm/server/project) toda
288:    `Option` + `merge(global, local)` recursivo; `load()` lê `~/.arlm/arlm.toml` e `.arlm.toml`.
289: 3. **Init**: gera `.arlm.toml` mínimo (`[project]`) e faz `append` de `.arlm.toml` ao `.gitignore`
290:    (idempotente); roda `index` (019).
291: 4. **Client despido de data-config + modo offline REMOVIDO**: remover `Config.embedding`/
292:    `search`/`agent`; **deletar `dispatch/local.rs`** e todo branch local; remover
293:    `arlm_storage::Storage::open` local, `embedding.rs`, busca/contexto locais e vector store
294:    local. `query`/`search`/`history`/`memory`/`persist`/`index` chamam **só** gRPC.
295: 5. **Index protocolo** (D2): client envia **texto cru**; `grpc/index.rs` (server) chunka com
296:    `[embedder].max_tokens/overlap_tokens` e embeda. Atualizar `proto`/`IndexFile`.
297: 6. **Wire**: `client.rs`/`auth_client.rs`/`dispatch/server.rs` consomem `user_config` (addr +
298:    auth + llm); `ARLM_SERVER_ADDR` continua como override de env.
299: 7. **Docs**: `install.sh`/`docker-compose`/`README` documentam `server.toml` (host mount),
300:    `~/.arlm/arlm.toml` e `.arlm.toml`; `arlm-server admin create-refresh` aponta para
301:    `~/.arlm/arlm.toml [auth]`. Sem nota de transição.
302: 8. **`cargo check --workspace` + clippy + fmt**.
303: 
304: ---
305: 
306: ## Testing
307: 
308: - `test_server_config_loads_from_arlm_server_config_env` (default `/etc/arlm/server.toml`).
309: - `test_server_config_has_no_llm_section` (parse de toml sem `[llm]` ok; `build_llm` ausente).
310: - `test_server_config_embedder_chunk_size_applied` (server usa `max_tokens` p/ chunk).
311: - `test_user_config_merge_local_overrides_global_granular` (campo local ganha; ausente cai no global).
312: - `test_user_config_nested_merge_recursive` (`[llm]` local funde com global campo a campo).
313: - `test_init_creates_local_arlm_toml_and_gitignores` (`.arlm.toml` em `.gitignore`).
314: - `test_init_does_not_write_auth_to_local` (refresh_token fica só no global).
315: - `test_client_uses_merged_server_addr`.
316: - `test_legacy_config_toml_ignored` (break total: `~/.arlm/config.toml`/`.arlm/config.toml`
317:   antigos são **ignorados**, não lidos).
318: - `test_auth_only_global` (merge ignora `[auth]` presente em `.arlm.toml` local).
319: - `test_server_and_user_config_files_disjoint` (server não lê `~/.arlm/arlm.toml`; client não lê
320:   `server.toml`).
321: - `test_client_no_local_storage_open` (nenhum comando sobrevivente abre `Storage` local; tudo é
322:   gRPC).
323: 
324: ---
325: 
326: ## Risks
327: 
328: | Risco | Mitigação |
329: |---|---|
330: | Colisão histórica `[server]` (addr vs listen_addr) | arquivos separados (`server.toml` vs `arlm.toml`); sem sobreposição |
331: | Break total sem transição | operadores devem reescrever configs (`server.toml` + `~/.arlm/arlm.toml`); documentar como *breaking change* no CHANGELOG; sem auto-migração |
332: | Remoção do modo offline exige reescrita do client | muitos comandos usam `data_dir()`/`Storage::open` local hoje; mover **todos** para gRPC (search/query/history/entities/persist); `dispatch/local.rs` deletado |
333: | Chunking no server muda tamanho de chunk vs indexações antigas | reindex necessário; `qa_cache` já invalida por hash de chunk (plan 017) |
334: | `server.toml` com secret em plaintext no docker | TLS keys são **paths** (montados); `data_dir` é volume; nada de secret em toml |
335: | Merge granular quebra em tabelas profundas | testar recursão; manter structs chatas (sem aninhamento > 2 níveis) |
336: | `.arlm.toml` commitado por engano | `arlm init` garante gitignore; documentar |
337: 
338: ---
339: 
340: ## Relação com 019/017/018
341: 
342: - **019 (remoção legado + CLI):** `arlm init` (B) e `arlm memory`/`persist` (C/D) consomem
343:   `user_config`; `maintenance` (C.1) é configurado aqui em `[maintenance]`. As referências a
344:   `~/.arlm/config.toml`/`.arlm/config.toml` no 019 são **supersedidas** por este plano
345:   (`~/.arlm/arlm.toml` global, `.arlm.toml` local, `server.toml` do server).
346: - **017 (QA-Cache):** `qa_cache` já é server-only; permanece em `server.toml [qa_cache]`.
347: - **018 (auth):** `auth.username`/`refresh_token` migram de `config.toml [auth]` para
348:   `~/.arlm/arlm.toml [auth]`; semântica de token inalterada.

137: ///
138: /// Returns an error if the address is invalid or the connection cannot be
139: /// established after the retry budget is exhausted.
140: pub async fn connect_channel(config: &ClientConfig) -> Result<Channel> {
141:     let raw = config.addr.trim();
142:     let (scheme, hostport) = if let Some(rest) = raw.strip_prefix("https://") {
143:         ("https", rest)
144:     } else if let Some(rest) = raw.strip_prefix("http://") {
145:         ("http", rest)
146:     } else {
147:         ("http", raw)
148:     };
149: 
150:     validate_addr(hostport).with_context(|| format!("invalid server address: {raw}"))?;
151: 
152:     let uri = if scheme == "https" {
153:         raw.to_string()
154:     } else {
155:         format!("http://{hostport}")
156:     };
157: 
158:     let endpoint =
159:         Channel::from_shared(uri.clone()).with_context(|| format!("invalid server URI: {uri}"))?;
160: 
161:     let endpoint: Endpoint = if scheme == "https" {
162:         let tls = ClientTlsConfig::new().with_native_roots();
163:         endpoint.tls_config(tls)?
164:     } else {
165:         endpoint
166:     };
167: 
168:     let max_attempts: u32 = 3;
169:     let mut attempt: u32 = 0;
170:     loop {
171:         attempt += 1;
172:         match endpoint.connect().await {
173:             Ok(channel) => {
174:                 info!(attempt, %raw, "connected to arlm-server");
175:                 return Ok(channel);
176:             }
177:             Err(e) => {
178:                 if attempt >= max_attempts {
179:                     return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(
180:                         "failed to connect to server at {raw} after {max_attempts} attempts: {e}"
181:                     ));
182:                 }
183:                 let backoff = Duration::from_millis(250 * 2u64.pow(attempt - 1));
184:                 warn!(
185:                     attempt,
186:                     max_attempts,
187:                     error = %e,
188:                     backoff_ms = backoff.as_millis() as u64,
189:                     "server connection failed, retrying with backoff"
190:                 );
191:                 tokio::time::sleep(backoff).await;
192:             }
193:         }
194:     }
195: }

2: //!
3: //! Wraps the generated gRPC client so every call automatically carries a
4: //! `Bearer` session token. The session token is obtained once from
5: //! `AuthRefresh` and proactively renewed on a background task (the refresh
6: //! token lives only in `config.toml`); the CLI user never manages it manually.

8: use std::str::FromStr;
9: use std::sync::Arc;
10: use std::time::Duration;
11: 
12: use anyhow::{Context, Result};

15: use tonic::metadata::MetadataValue;
16: use tonic::service::Interceptor;
17: use tonic::service::interceptor::InterceptedService;
18: use tonic::transport::Channel;
19: use tonic::{Request, Status};
20: 
21: use arlm_proto::proto::arlm_service_client::ArlmServiceClient;
22: use arlm_proto::proto::{AuthRefreshRequest, AuthRefreshResponse};
23: 
24: use crate::client::{self, ClientConfig};
25: 
26: /// Authenticated gRPC client type returned by [`connect`].
27: pub type ArlmClient = ArlmServiceClient<InterceptedService<Channel, BearerInterceptor>>;
28: 
29: /// Interceptor that attaches the current session token as a `Bearer` header.
30: #[derive(Clone)]
31: pub struct BearerInterceptor {
32:     token: Arc<Mutex<String>>,
33: }
34: 
35: impl Interceptor for BearerInterceptor {
36:     fn call(&mut self, mut req: Request<()>) -> Result<Request<()>, Status> {
37:         let token = self.token.lock().clone();
38:         if token.is_empty() {
39:             return Ok(req);
40:         }
41:         let value = MetadataValue::from_str(&format!("Bearer {token}"))
42:             .map_err(|_| Status::internal("invalid session token"))?;
43:         req.metadata_mut().insert("authorization", value);
44:         Ok(req)
45:     }
46: }
47: 
48: /// Connect to the server, performing `AuthRefresh` (if a refresh token is
49: /// configured) and returning a client that auto-attaches and renews the
50: /// session token.
51: ///
52: /// When no `refresh_token` is configured the returned client sends no auth
53: /// header (the server will reject privileged RPCs with `UNAUTHENTICATED`).
54: ///
55: /// # Errors
56: ///
57: /// Returns an error if the channel cannot be established or the initial
58: /// `AuthRefresh` fails.
59: pub fn connect(
60:     rt: &Runtime,
61:     client_config: &ClientConfig,
62:     auth: &crate::config::AuthConfig,
63: ) -> Result<ArlmClient> {
64:     let channel = rt
65:         .block_on(client::connect_channel(client_config))
66:         .context("failed to connect to arlm-server")?;
67: 
68:     let token = Arc::new(Mutex::new(String::new()));
69: 
70:     if let Some(refresh) = &auth.refresh_token {
71:         let refresh = refresh.clone();
72: 
73:         let mut refresh_client = ArlmServiceClient::new(channel.clone());
74:         let session: AuthRefreshResponse = rt
75:             .block_on(refresh_client.auth_refresh(AuthRefreshRequest {
76:                 refresh_token: refresh.clone(),
77:             }))
78:             .context("AuthRefresh failed")?
79:             .into_inner();
80:         *token.lock() = session.session_token;
81: 
82:         let renewal_token = token.clone();
83:         let mut renewal_client = ArlmServiceClient::new(channel.clone());
84:         let renewal_refresh = refresh.clone();
85:         rt.spawn(async move {
86:             let mut ticker = tokio::time::interval(Duration::from_secs(4 * 60));
87:             loop {
88:                 ticker.tick().await;
89:                 match renewal_client
90:                     .auth_refresh(AuthRefreshRequest {
91:                         refresh_token: renewal_refresh.clone(),
92:                     })
93:                     .await
94:                 {
95:                     Ok(resp) => {
96:                         *renewal_token.lock() = resp.into_inner().session_token;
97:                     }
98:                     Err(e) => {
99:                         tracing::warn!(error = %e, "auth session renewal failed; will retry");
100:                     }
101:                 }
102:             }
103:         });
104:     }
105: 
106:     let interceptor = BearerInterceptor { token };
107:     Ok(ArlmServiceClient::new(InterceptedService::new(
108:         channel,
109:         interceptor,
110:     )))
111: }

14: /// Resolve the effective output format from CLI flag and config file.
15: ///
16: /// `default` is used when neither the CLI flag nor the config file specify a
17: /// format. Content-retrieval commands (search/context/query) pass
18: /// `Format::Jsonl` so an AI consumes only the matched file content; all other
19: /// commands keep `Format::Path`. `allow_jsonl` coerces an explicit `jsonl`
20: /// selection to `Format::FullJson` for non-content commands, which have no
21: /// simplified JSONL rendering.
22: fn resolve_format(
23:     cli_format: Option<OutputFormatArg>,
24:     cfg_format: Option<&str>,
25:     default: Format,
26:     allow_jsonl: bool,
27: ) -> Format {
28:     let resolved = match cli_format {
29:         Some(OutputFormatArg::FullJson) => Format::FullJson,
30:         Some(OutputFormatArg::Path) => Format::Path,
31:         Some(OutputFormatArg::Markdown) => Format::Markdown,
32:         Some(OutputFormatArg::Text) => Format::Text,
33:         Some(OutputFormatArg::Jsonl) => Format::Jsonl,
34:         None => match cfg_format {
35:             Some("full_json") => Format::FullJson,
36:             Some("path") => Format::Path,
37:             Some("markdown") => Format::Markdown,
38:             Some("text") => Format::Text,
39:             Some("jsonl") => Format::Jsonl,
40:             _ => default,
41:         },
42:     };
43:     if !allow_jsonl && resolved == Format::Jsonl {
44:         Format::FullJson
45:     } else {
46:         resolved
47:     }
48: }
49: 
50: /// Entry point for command dispatch.
51: ///
52: /// Resolves configuration precedence (CLI overrides config overrides defaults)
53: /// and routes to either the local command implementation or a remote gRPC
54: /// server when `--server` is supplied.
55: pub fn dispatch(cli: Cli, cfg: Config, rt: &Runtime) -> Result<()> {
56:     let project = cli
57:         .project
58:         .clone()
59:         .or_else(|| cfg.project.clone())
60:         .unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from("."));
61:     let backend = cli.backend.clone().or_else(|| cfg.backend.clone());
62:     let model = cli.model.clone().or_else(|| cfg.model.clone());
63:     let agent_name = cli.agent.clone().or_else(|| cfg.agent.name.clone());
64:     let is_content = matches!(
65:         cli.command,
66:         Commands::Search { .. } | Commands::Context { .. } | Commands::Query { .. }
67:     );
68:     let default = if is_content {
69:         Format::Text
70:     } else {
71:         Format::Path
72:     };
73:     let format = resolve_format(cli.format, cfg.format.as_deref(), default, is_content);
74: 
75:     // Remote gRPC server mode. Precedence: `--server` flag > config file /
76:     // env (`~/.arlm/config.toml` `[server] addr` or `ARLM_SERVER_ADDR`) >
77:     // local execution. When neither is set we fall through to local mode.
78:     let server_addr = cli.server.clone().or_else(client::explicit_addr);
79:     if let Some(addr) = server_addr {
80:         return server::run_server(cli, addr, project, format, rt);
81:     }
82: 
83:     local::run_local(cli, cfg, project, backend, model, agent_name, format, rt)
84: }

526: /// Stream one disjoint group of files to the server as a single `IndexProject`
527: /// client-stream, returning the files/chunks counts reported by the server.
528: async fn stream_index_group(
529:     client: &mut ArlmClient,
530:     project: String,
531:     root: PathBuf,
532:     files: Vec<PathBuf>,
533:     progress: Arc<indicatif::ProgressBar>,
534: ) -> anyhow::Result<(i64, i64)> {
535:     let (tx, rx) = mpsc::channel::<IndexChunk>(32);
536:     let stream = ReceiverStream::new(rx);
537:     let response_fut = client.index_project(stream);
538: 
539:     let send_handle = tokio::spawn(async move {
540:         if tx
541:             .send(IndexChunk {
542:                 body: Some(index_chunk::Body::Init(IndexInit {
543:                     project,
544:                     root_path: root.to_string_lossy().to_string(),
545:                     force_include: vec![],
546:                     exclude_patterns: vec![],
547:                 })),
548:             })
549:             .await
550:             .is_err()
551:         {
552:             return;
553:         }
554: 
555:         for file in &files {
556:             let Ok(content) = std::fs::read_to_string(file) else {
557:                 progress.inc(1);
558:                 continue;
559:             };
560:             let rel_path = file
561:                 .strip_prefix(&root)
562:                 .unwrap_or(file)
563:                 .to_string_lossy()
564:                 .to_string();
565:             let compressed = arlm_embedding::pipeline::compress_text(&content);
566:             if tx
567:                 .send(IndexChunk {
568:                     body: Some(index_chunk::Body::File(IndexFile {
569:                         rel_path,
570:                         content: compressed,
571:                         compressed: true,
572:                         size_bytes: i64::try_from(content.len()).unwrap_or(i64::MAX),
573:                     })),
574:                 })
575:                 .await
576:                 .is_err()
577:             {
578:                 break;
579:             }
580:             progress.inc(1);
581:         }
582:     });
583: 
584:     let response = response_fut
585:         .await
586:         .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!("index stream failed: {e}"))?;
587:     send_handle
588:         .await
589:         .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!("upload task failed: {e}"))?;
590: 
591:     let inner: IndexResponse = response.into_inner();
592:     Ok((inner.files_indexed, inner.chunks_created))
593: }
594: 
595: /// Split `files` into `n` roughly equal, disjoint groups for parallel upload.
596: #[must_use]
597: fn partition_files(files: &[PathBuf], n: usize) -> Vec<Vec<PathBuf>> {
598:     let n = n.max(1).min(files.len().max(1));
599:     let mut groups: Vec<Vec<PathBuf>> = (0..n).map(|_| Vec::new()).collect();
600:     for (i, file) in files.iter().enumerate() {
601:         groups[i % n].push(file.clone());
602:     }
603:     groups.retain(|g| !g.is_empty());
604:     groups
605: }

1: //! Helpers to build the embedding backend and locate the per-buffer vector
2: //! store used for semantic (BGE-M3) search.
3: //!
4: //! Semantic filtering was previously never applied: indexing stored no vectors
5: //! and the query path was built with `semantic = None` + `query_vector = None`.
6: //! These helpers close that gap by constructing a real embedder (BGE-M3 when
7: //! weights are available, otherwise a deterministic lightweight fallback) and a
8: //! [`VectorStore`] directory scoped per project buffer.

34: /// Build an embedder from the resolved CLI [`Config`].
35: ///
36: /// `prefix` is the Nomic task prefix prepended to every input (e.g.
37: /// `"search_document: "` when indexing, `"search_query: "` when querying). It
38: /// is only applied by the Ollama backend; other backends ignore it.
39: ///
40: /// Resolution:
41: /// 1. `model = "ollama"` → remote Ollama embedder (`nomic-embed-text-v2-moe`
42: ///    by default, 768-dim). Laptop-friendly: runs on CPU with no weights.
43: /// 2. `model = "bge-m3"` (or unset with `model_dir` set) → local BGE-M3.
44: /// 3. Otherwise → deterministic `lightweight` hash embedder (no semantic value,
45: ///    only keeps the pipeline alive).
46: ///
47: /// If the selected backend fails to construct (e.g. Ollama unreachable), it
48: /// falls back to `lightweight` rather than aborting.
49: pub fn build_embedder_from_config(config: &Config, prefix: &str) -> Arc<dyn Embedder> {
50:     let emb = &config.embedding;
51:     let dims = emb.dims.unwrap_or(VECTOR_DIMS_BGE);
52: 
53:     if let Some("ollama") = emb.model.as_deref() {

56:             .clone()

58:         let omodel = emb
59:             .ollama_model

15: /// Resolve a backend by logical `name` (or the config default), falling back to
16: /// the legacy kind-based presets.
17: ///
18: /// `model_override` optionally forces the model for the request.
19: ///
20: /// # Errors
21: ///
22: /// Returns an error if no backend matches and the legacy kind cannot be parsed
23: /// or requires a missing API key.
24: pub fn resolve_backend(
25:     config: &Config,
26:     name: Option<&str>,
27:     model_override: Option<&str>,
28: ) -> Result<Arc<dyn LlmBackend>> {
29:     let name = name
30:         .map(ToString::to_string)

32: 
33:     // 1. Try a configured provider backend by name (or the first configured one).

35:         let chosen: Option<&BackendConfig> = match &name {
36:             Some(n) => config.llm.backends.iter().find(|b| {
37:                 b.name.as_deref() == Some(n)
38:                     || b.model.as_deref() == Some(n)
39:                     || n == b.family.as_str()
40:             }),
41:             None => config.llm.backends.first(),

syntax = "proto3";
package arlm.v1;

// ── Auth (plan 018) ──

// Client presents its refresh token; server mints a short-lived session token.
message AuthRefreshRequest {
  string refresh_token = 1;
}

message AuthRefreshResponse {
  // Opaque session token (UUIDv7); present this as `Authorization: Bearer`.
  string session_token = 1;
  // Session expiry, epoch milliseconds (UTC).
  int64 expires_at = 2;
  // Resolved role: "admin" | "non_admin".
  string role = 3;
  // Owning username (for audit).
  string username = 4;
}
syntax = "proto3";
package arlm.v1;

import "search.proto";

// ── Context Building ──

message ContextRequest {
  string project = 1;
  string task = 2;
  int32 max_tokens = 3;
  bool prefer_summaries = 4;  // default: true
}

message ContextResponse {
  string context = 1;
  repeated SearchResult sources = 2;
  ContextStats stats = 3;
}

message ContextStats {
  int32 total_tokens = 1;
  int32 raw_chunks_included = 2;
  int32 summary_chunks_included = 3;
  float summary_ratio = 4;  // 0.0 = all raw, 1.0 = all summaries
}
syntax = "proto3";
package arlm.v1;

// ── Indexing (client-streaming) ──
//
// The client discovers and reads files from its OWN filesystem, then streams
// each file's content to the server. The server never touches the client's
// filesystem — it only receives bytes over gRPC and indexes them. This removes
// any server-side path/FS knowledge (and the associated arbitrary-file-read
// footgun) and keeps the server a pure indexing engine.

message IndexChunk {
  oneof body {
    IndexInit init = 1;
    IndexFile file = 2;
  }
}

message IndexInit {
  string project = 1;
  string root_path = 2;
  repeated string force_include = 3;
  repeated string exclude_patterns = 4;
}

message IndexFile {
  string rel_path = 1;
  bytes content = 2;
  bool compressed = 3;
  int64 size_bytes = 4;
}

message IndexResponse {
  string run_id = 1;
  int64 files_indexed = 2;
  int64 chunks_created = 3;
  int64 summaries_generated = 4;
  double duration_ms = 5;
}
syntax = "proto3";
package arlm.v1;

import "google/protobuf/timestamp.proto";

// ── Project Management ──

message CreateProjectRequest {
  string name = 1;
  string root_path = 2;
}

message ProjectInfo {
  string id = 1;
  string name = 2;
  string root_path = 3;
  int64 chunk_count = 4;
  int64 file_count = 5;
  google.protobuf.Timestamp created_at = 6;
}

message ListProjectsResponse {
  repeated ProjectInfo projects = 1;
}
syntax = "proto3";
package arlm.v1;

import "search.proto";

// ── Query-Answer Cache (plan 017) ──

// Mode for manual invalidation of a single cached answer.
enum InvalidateMode {
  // Soft: mark stale (re-digest forced on next hit), keeps audit trail.
  STALE = 0;
  // Hard: remove the row and its question vector entirely.
  DELETE = 1;
}

// Admin-gated invalidation of cached query/result answers.
//
// Backward-compatible with plan 018: when `cache_id` is empty the legacy
// `result_cache` is purged by `project` (empty = all projects). When
// `cache_id` is set, the semantic `qa_cache` entry is invalidated (Stale/Delete)
// and, if `similarity_radius` is set, so are all nearby questions in the
// `question_vectors` space (the "error chain").
message InvalidateCacheRequest {
  // Project whose legacy cache to purge (plan 018 path). Empty = all projects.
  string project = 1;
  // Target `qa_cache` answer id (plan 017 path). Empty = use `project` path.
  string cache_id = 2;
  // Invalidation mode for the `qa_cache` path.
  InvalidateMode mode = 3;
  // If set, also invalidate `qa_cache` entries whose question is within this
  // cosine radius of the target (error-chain invalidation).
  float similarity_radius = 4;
}

message InvalidateCacheResponse {
  // Number of cache entries removed (qa_cache rows + question vectors).
  int64 invalidated = 1;
  // Username of the admin who triggered the invalidation (audit).
  string invalidated_by = 2;
}

// Query the semantic cache. The server is deterministic: it embeds, searches
// and decides hit/miss — it never runs an LLM. The client digests on a MISS.
message QueryWithCacheRequest {
  string project = 1;
  string question = 2;
  // Optional explicit buffer id (scoping). When 0 the server resolves by name.
  int64 buffer_id = 3;
}

message QueryWithCacheResponse {
  // Stable answer id (present on hit; on miss it is assigned on StoreAnswer).
  string cache_id = 1;
  // Whether a cached answer was served (no client LLM needed).
  bool hit = 2;
  // Resolved tier (0 = top, -1 = miss).
  int32 tier = 3;
  // Question cosine similarity of the best candidate.
  float similarity = 4;
  // Digested answer (hit only).
  string answer_text = 5;
  // Provenance chunks returned alongside a hit.
  repeated SearchResult provenance = 6;
  // Raw chunks to digest on a miss (client digests these).
  repeated SearchResult candidates = 7;
  // Number of chunks the client should digest.
  int32 digest_k = 8;
  // Number of provenance chunks to return with the answer.
  int32 provenance_k = 9;
}

// Store a digested answer (client-synthesized). Idempotent per
// (project, question_hash): concurrent identical stores reuse one cache_id.
message StoreAnswerRequest {
  string project = 1;
  string question = 2;
  string answer = 3;
  repeated string source_chunk_ids = 4;
  repeated string source_hashes = 5;
  string model = 6;
  int64 token_count = 7;
  int64 buffer_id = 8;
  // Reserved answer id from a prior QueryWithCache (optional; empty → server assigns).
  string cache_id = 9;
}

message StoreAnswerResponse {
  // Stable answer id (anti-drift, propagatable to sub-agents).
  string cache_id = 1;
}

// Direct, deterministic lookup of a previously served answer by its stable id
// (anti-drift: identical 1:1, no re-index/search/LLM).
message GetAnswerByIdRequest {
  string cache_id = 1;
  string project = 2;
}

message GetAnswerByIdResponse {
  bool found = 1;
  string cache_id = 2;
  string project = 3;
  string answer_text = 4;
  repeated string source_chunk_ids = 5;
  repeated string source_hashes = 6;
}
syntax = "proto3";
package arlm.v1;

// ── Search ──

message SearchRequest {
  string project = 1;
  string query = 2;
  int32 max_results = 3;
  SearchTier tier = 4;
  bool include_summaries = 5;  // default: true
  bool include_raw = 6;        // default: true
}

enum SearchTier {
  TIER_BM25 = 0;
  TIER_SEMANTIC = 1;
  TIER_HYBRID = 2;
  TIER_ENTITY = 3;
}

message SearchResult {
  int64 chunk_id = 1;
  string text = 2;
  float score = 3;
  string file_path = 4;
  int32 start_line = 5;
  int32 end_line = 6;
  bool is_summary = 7;
  SummaryInfo summary = 8;
}

message SummaryInfo {
  string summary_text = 1;
  int64 raw_chunk_count = 2;
  float confidence = 3;
}

message SearchResponse {
  repeated SearchResult results = 1;
  int32 total_count = 2;
  double duration_ms = 3;
}
syntax = "proto3";
package arlm.v1;

// ── Server Management ──

message ServerStatus {
  string version = 1;
  int32 uptime_seconds = 2;
  int32 active_runs = 3;
  int32 total_projects = 4;
  int64 total_chunks = 5;
  int64 total_summaries = 6;
  WriteQueueStats write_queue = 7;
  SummarizeStatus summarize = 8;
}

message WriteQueueStats {
  int32 pending_writes = 1;
  int32 batched_last_flush = 2;
  double avg_latency_ms = 3;
}

message SummarizeStatus {
  bool running = 1;
  string current_file = 2;
  int32 files_remaining = 3;
  double estimated_cost_usd = 4;
}
syntax = "proto3";
package arlm.v1;

import "google/protobuf/empty.proto";
import "google/protobuf/wrappers.proto";

import "project.proto";
import "index.proto";
import "search.proto";
import "context.proto";
import "session.proto";
import "server.proto";
import "auth.proto";
import "query_cache.proto";

// ── gRPC Service ──

service ArlmService {
  // Project management
  rpc CreateProject(CreateProjectRequest) returns (ProjectInfo);
  rpc ListProjects(google.protobuf.Empty) returns (ListProjectsResponse);
  rpc GetProject(google.protobuf.StringValue) returns (ProjectInfo);

  // Indexing (client-streaming: client streams file bytes to the server)
  rpc IndexProject(stream IndexChunk) returns (IndexResponse);

  // Search
  rpc Search(SearchRequest) returns (SearchResponse);
  rpc BuildContext(ContextRequest) returns (ContextResponse);

  // Sessions
  rpc CreateSession(CreateSessionRequest) returns (SessionInfo);
  rpc ListSessions(google.protobuf.StringValue) returns (ListSessionsResponse);
  rpc GetSession(google.protobuf.StringValue) returns (SessionInfo);
  rpc AddSessionTurn(AddSessionTurnRequest) returns (SessionTurn);

  // Server management
  rpc GetServerStatus(google.protobuf.Empty) returns (ServerStatus);

  // Auth (plan 018): exchange a refresh token for a 5-minute session token.
  rpc AuthRefresh(AuthRefreshRequest) returns (AuthRefreshResponse);

  // Cache (plan 017, admin-gated by plan 018): purge cached query/result
  // answers. Requires an authenticated admin session (non-admins get
  // PERMISSION_DENIED). Empty `project` purges all projects.
  rpc InvalidateCache(InvalidateCacheRequest) returns (InvalidateCacheResponse);

  // Query-Answer Cache (plan 017, client-side digest-once).
  rpc QueryWithCache(QueryWithCacheRequest) returns (QueryWithCacheResponse);
  rpc StoreAnswer(StoreAnswerRequest) returns (StoreAnswerResponse);
  rpc GetAnswerById(GetAnswerByIdRequest) returns (GetAnswerByIdResponse);

  // Memory admin (plan 019): list cached query/answer memory for a project.
  rpc ListMemory(ListMemoryRequest) returns (ListMemoryResponse);

  // Cache debug (plan 019): fetch a single cached answer by id.
  rpc GetCache(GetCacheRequest) returns (GetCacheResponse);

  // Maintenance (plan 019): run (or dry-run) cache cleanup/decay.
  rpc TriggerMaintenance(TriggerMaintenanceRequest) returns (MaintenanceReport);

  // History (plan 019): per-user query history (server scopes by user).
  rpc GetHistory(GetHistoryRequest) returns (GetHistoryResponse);
}

// ── Memory / Cache / Maintenance / History (plan 019) ──

message ListMemoryRequest {
  string project = 1;
  int64 limit = 2;
  bool include_entities = 3;
}

message MemoryEntry {
  string cache_id = 1;
  string project = 2;
  string question = 3;
  string created_at = 4;
  double score = 5;
  repeated string entities = 6;
}

message ListMemoryResponse {
  repeated MemoryEntry entries = 1;
  string stats = 2;
}

message GetCacheRequest {
  string cache_id = 1;
}

message GetCacheResponse {
  string answer = 1;
  repeated string source_chunk_ids = 2;
  repeated string files = 3;
  string project = 4;
}

message TriggerMaintenanceRequest {
  string project = 1;
  bool dry_run = 2;
}

message MaintenanceReport {
  int64 duplicate_chunks_removed = 1;
  int64 low_confidence_patterns_removed = 2;
  int64 decayed_chunks = 3;
  int64 kept = 4;
}

message GetHistoryRequest {
  string user = 1;
  int64 limit = 2;
}

238: /// Embed every chunk of `buffer_id` into the per-buffer vector store, replacing
239: /// any previous vectors for that buffer.
240: ///
241: /// This is the missing piece that makes semantic (BGE-M3) filtering functional:
242: /// Embed a batch of `(chunk_id, text)` pairs and push the resulting
243: /// `VectorEntry`s. Uses a single batched request; on failure it falls back to
244: /// per-chunk embedding so one bad chunk never drops the whole batch.
245: fn embed_pending(
246:     entries: &mut Vec<VectorEntry>,
247:     embedder: &Arc<dyn Embedder>,
248:     pending: &[(u64, String)],
249:     buffer_u: u64,
250: ) {
251:     let texts: Vec<&str> = pending.iter().map(|(_, t)| t.as_str()).collect();
252:     match embedder.embed_batch(&texts) {
253:         Ok(vectors) => {
254:             for (meta, vector) in pending.iter().zip(vectors) {
255:                 entries.push(VectorEntry {
256:                     chunk_id: meta.0,
257:                     buffer_id: buffer_u,
258:                     vector,
259:                 });
260:             }
261:         }
262:         Err(e) => {
263:             warn!(error = %e, "batch embedding failed, falling back to per-chunk");
264:             for (chunk_u, text) in pending {
265:                 match embedder.embed(text) {
266:                     Ok(vector) => entries.push(VectorEntry {
267:                         chunk_id: *chunk_u,
268:                         buffer_id: buffer_u,
269:                         vector,
270:                     }),
271:                     Err(e2) => warn!(chunk_id = chunk_u, error = %e2, "chunk embedding failed"),
272:                 }
273:             }
274:         }
275:     }
276: }
277: 
278: /// the knowledge engine stores chunk text but never computes embeddings, so the
279: /// vector store was always empty. We rebuild this buffer's store from scratch
280: /// to avoid stale vectors from deleted chunks.
281: async fn embed_buffer(config: &Config, storage: &arlm_storage::Storage, buffer_id: i64) {
282:     let embedder = build_embedder_from_config(config, "search_document: ");
283: 
284:     // Rebuild from scratch: remove the old vector store directory for this buffer.
285:     let vdir = vector_dir(buffer_id);
286:     if vdir.exists() {
287:         if let Err(e) = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&vdir) {
288:             warn!(error = %e, "failed to clear old vector store, reusing existing");
289:         }
290:     }
291: 
292:     let vstore = match open_vector_store(buffer_id, embedder.dimensions()).await {
293:         Ok(s) => s,
294:         Err(e) => {
295:             warn!(error = %e, "failed to open vector store, skipping embeddings");
296:             return;
297:         }
298:     };
299: 
300:     let chunks = match storage.list_chunks(buffer_id) {
301:         Ok(c) => c,
302:         Err(e) => {
303:             warn!(error = %e, "failed to list chunks for embedding");
304:             return;
305:         }
306:     };
307: 
308:     let Ok(buffer_u) = u64::try_from(buffer_id) else {
309:         warn!(buffer_id, "negative buffer id, skipping embeddings");
310:         return;
311:     };
312: 
313:     let mut entries: Vec<VectorEntry> = Vec::with_capacity(chunks.len());
314:     let mut pending: Vec<(u64, String)> = Vec::with_capacity(EMBED_BATCH_SIZE);
315:     for c in &chunks {
316:         let Ok(chunk_u) = u64::try_from(c.id) else {
317:             warn!(chunk_id = c.id, "negative chunk id, skipping chunk");
318:             continue;
319:         };
320:         match storage.get_chunk_content(c.id) {
321:             Ok(Some(text)) => pending.push((chunk_u, text)),
322:             Ok(None) => {}
323:             Err(e) => warn!(chunk_id = c.id, error = %e, "chunk content read failed"),
324:         }
325:         if pending.len() >= EMBED_BATCH_SIZE {
326:             embed_pending(&mut entries, &embedder, &pending, buffer_u);
327:             pending.clear();
328:         }
329:     }
330:     if !pending.is_empty() {
331:         embed_pending(&mut entries, &embedder, &pending, buffer_u);
332:     }
333: 
334:     if entries.is_empty() {
335:         return;
336:     }
337: 
338:     match vstore.insert_vectors(&entries).await {
339:         Ok(()) => tracing::info!(count = entries.len(), "embedded chunks into vector store"),
340:         Err(e) => warn!(error = %e, "failed to insert vectors"),
341:     }
342: }

177:                 "cache_id": cache_id,
178:                 "hit": !miss,
179:                 "answer": answer,
180:                 "provenance": prov,
181:             });
182:             println!("{}", serde_json::to_string(&json).unwrap_or_default());
183:         }
184:         Format::Jsonl => {
185:             println!(
186:                 "{}",
187:                 crate::output::jsonl::render_content_jsonl("cache_id", cache_id, &prov)
188:             );
189:         }
190:         Format::Markdown => {
191:             println!("## {cache_id}\n\n{answer}");
192:         }
193:         _ => {
194:             println!("{answer}");
195:         }
196:     }
197: }

//! Backend configuration for the generic, provider-agnostic LLM backend.
//!
//! A single [`BackendConfig`] fully describes how to talk to an LLM provider:
//! which wire [`BackendFamily`] to use for request/response mapping, the base
//! URL, the authentication scheme, and the endpoint paths. This replaces the
//! previous per-provider implementations (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama,
//! DeepSeek, MiMo), which are now *presets* over this config.
//!

/// Protocol family controlling how a [`CompletionRequest`] is mapped to/from
/// the provider wire format.
///
/// DeepSeek and MiMo speak the OpenAI protocol, so they use [`Self::OpenAi`].
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum BackendFamily {
    OpenAi,
    Anthropic,
    Gemini,
    Ollama,

impl BackendFamily {
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::OpenAi => "openai",
            Self::Anthropic => "anthropic",
            Self::Gemini => "gemini",
            Self::Ollama => "ollama",
        }
    }
}

impl fmt::Display for BackendFamily {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        f.write_str(self.as_str())
    }
}

    #[default]
    Bearer,
    /// Custom header, e.g. `x-api-key: <key>` (Anthropic).
    Header,
    /// Query parameter, e.g. `?key=<key>` (Gemini).
    Query,
    /// No authentication (Ollama).
    None,
}

/// This struct is the single source of truth that drives [`GenericBackend`].

///
/// # Example (TOML)
///
/// ```toml
/// [[backends]]

/// model = "gpt-4o"

/// health_method = "get"
///
/// [[backends]]
/// name = "my-anthropic"

/// api_key = "..."
/// auth = "header"
/// auth_header = "x-api-key"
/// extra_headers = [["anthropic-version", "2023-06-01"]]

/// health_method = "post"

pub struct BackendConfig {

    pub auth_prefix: String,
    /// Query parameter name used for [`AuthScheme::Query`] authentication.

    /// Extra static headers sent with every request (e.g. API version pins).

}

/// Scoped timing helper.
///
/// Logs the elapsed time of a code region on drop, with a structured
/// `timer` field so it can be filtered/aggregated in logs.
pub(crate) struct Timer {
    name: &'static str,
    start: std::time::Instant,
}

impl Timer {
    #[must_use]
    pub(crate) fn new(name: &'static str) -> Self {
        Self {
            name,
            start: std::time::Instant::now(),
        }
    }
}

impl Drop for Timer {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        let elapsed_ms = self.start.elapsed().as_millis();
        tracing::info!(timer = %self.name, elapsed_ms = elapsed_ms, "timing");
    }
}

use std::fs;
use std::path::Path;

/// Top-level LLM configuration file.
///
/// Holds an ordered list of [`BackendConfig`] entries. This is the structure
/// that `config.toml` (typically at `~/.arlm/config.toml`) deserializes into.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct LlmConfig {
    #[serde(default)]
    pub backends: Vec<BackendConfig>,
}

impl std::str::FromStr for LlmConfig {
    type Err = LlmError;

    fn from_str(s: &str) -> Result<Self, Self::Err> {
        toml::from_str(s).map_err(|e| LlmError::Serialization(e.to_string()))
    }
}

impl LlmConfig {
    /// Load configuration from a TOML file.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Returns [`LlmError::Backend`] if the file cannot be read, or
    /// [`LlmError::Serialization`] if its contents are invalid.
    pub fn from_file(path: &Path) -> Result<Self, LlmError> {
        let content = fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|e| {
            LlmError::Backend(format!("cannot read config {}: {e}", path.display()))
        })?;
        content.parse()
    }

    /// The configured backends, in file order.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn backends(&self) -> &[BackendConfig] {
        &self.backends
    }
}

}

pub struct ServerSection {
    pub addr: Option<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Deserialize)]
pub struct ProjectSection {
    pub name: Option<String>,

}

struct GlobalConfig {
    auth: Option<AuthConfig>,

    project: Option<ProjectSection>,
}

    auth: Option<AuthConfig>, // ignored

    server: Option<ServerSection>,
    project: Option<ProjectSection>,
}

    pub auth: Option<AuthConfig>,
    pub llm: Option<LlmConfig>,
    pub server: ServerSection,
    pub project: ProjectSection,
}

#[allow(dead_code)]
pub struct McpState {
    pub project: PathBuf,
    pub project_name: String,
    pub verbose: bool,
}

/// Handle a JSON-RPC 2.0 request for the MCP protocol.
#[tracing::instrument(skip_all, fields(method = %req.method))]
pub fn handle_jsonrpc(req: &JsonRpcRequest, state: &McpState) -> JsonRpcResponse {
    tracing::debug!(method = %req.method, "dispatch jsonrpc request");
    match req.method.as_str() {
        "initialize" => handle_initialize(req),
        "notifications/initialized" | "ping" => JsonRpcResponse::ok(req.id.clone(), json!({})),
        "tools/list" => handle_tools_list(req),
        "tools/call" => handle_tools_call(req, state),
        _ => JsonRpcResponse::err(
            req.id.clone(),
            -32601,
            format!("Method not found: {}", req.method),
        ),
    }

fn discover_files(root: &Path, ignore: &[String], force_include: &[String]) -> Result<Vec<PathBuf>> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut stack = vec![root.to_path_buf()];
    while let Some(dir) = stack.pop() {
        let entries = std::fs::read_dir(&dir).map_err(...)?;
        for entry in entries {
            let entry = entry.map_err(...)?;
            let path = entry.path();
            let rel = path.strip_prefix(root).unwrap_or(&path);
            let rel_s = rel.to_string_lossy();
            let is_dir = path.is_dir();
            if is_dir {
                if is_hidden_or_default_ignored(&rel_s) || matches_any(rel_s, ignore) && !matches_any(rel_s, force_include) {
                    // skip dir (don't recurse) unless force-included
                    if !matches_any(rel_s, force_include) {
                        continue;
                    }
                }
                stack.push(path);
                continue;
            }
            if matches_any(rel_s, force_include) || (!is_hidden_or_default_ignored(&rel_s) && !matches_any(rel_s, ignore)) {
                out.push(path);
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(out)
}
```

fn matches_pattern(rel_s: &str, pat: &str) -> bool {
    if pat.ends_with('/') {
        let dir = &pat[..pat.len()-1];
        return rel_s == dir || rel_s.starts_with(&format!("{dir}/")) || rel_s.contains(&format!("/{dir}/"));
    }
    if pat.starts_with("*.") {
        let ext = &pat[1..]; // ".rs"
        return rel_s.ends_with(ext);
    }
    if pat.contains('*') {
        // simple glob: convert to substring check after removing stars? Keep simple: check if pattern without stars is substring
        let simple = pat.replace('*', "");
        return rel_s.contains(&simple);
    }
    // exact substring
    rel_s == pat || rel_s.ends_with(&format!("/{pat}")) || rel_s.contains(&format!("/{pat}/"))
}

```
fn matches_pattern(rel: &str, pat: &str) -> bool {
    if let Some(dir) = pat.strip_suffix('/') {
        return rel == dir || rel.starts_with(&format!("{dir}/")) || rel.contains(&format!("/{dir}/"));
    }
    if let Some(ext) = pat.strip_prefix("*.") {
        return rel.to_ascii_lowercase().ends_with(ext);
    }
    if pat.contains('*') {
        let simple = pat.replace('*', "");
        return !simple.is_empty() && rel.to_ascii_lowercase().contains(&simple);
    }
    rel == pat || rel.ends_with(&format!("/{pat}")) || rel.contains(&format!("/{pat}/"))
}
```

//!
//! These tests assert the contract emitted by `build.rs` from the `.proto`

#![allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic)]

use arlm_proto::proto::*;

#[test]
fn test_run_result_fields_and_cost() {
    let stats = RunStats {
        nodes_visited: 7,
        max_depth_reached: 3,
        total_tokens: 1_024,
        total_cost_usd: 0.42,
        duration_ms: 1_250.0,
    };

    let run = RunResult {
        run_id: "run-1".into(),
        status: RunStatus::StatusCompleted as i32,
        answer: "done".into(),
        stats: Some(stats),
        total_cost: 0.42,
    };

    assert_eq!(run.run_id, "run-1");
    assert_eq!(run.status, RunStatus::StatusCompleted as i32);
    assert_eq!(run.stats.as_ref().unwrap().total_tokens, 1_024);
    assert!((run.total_cost - 0.42).abs() < f64::EPSILON);
}

#[test]
fn test_search_request_with_hybrid_tier() {
    let req = SearchRequest {
        project: "p".into(),
        query: "find auth".into(),
        max_results: 10,
        tier: SearchTier::TierHybrid as i32,
        include_summaries: true,
        include_raw: true,
    };

    assert_eq!(req.tier, SearchTier::TierHybrid as i32);
    assert_eq!(req.max_results, 10);
}

#[test]
fn test_session_info_fields() {
    let session = SessionInfo {
        session_id: "s-1".into(),
        project: "p".into(),
        title: "t".into(),
        created_at: None,
        turn_count: 2,
    };

    assert_eq!(session.session_id, "s-1");
    assert_eq!(session.turn_count, 2);
    assert!(session.created_at.is_none());
}

#[test]
fn test_add_session_turn_request_fields() {
    let req = AddSessionTurnRequest {
        session_id: "s-1".into(),
        query: "how?".into(),
        response: "answer".into(),
    };

    assert_eq!(req.session_id, "s-1");
    assert_eq!(req.query, "how?");
    assert_eq!(req.response, "answer");
}

#[test]
fn test_enum_variants_present() {
    assert_eq!(SearchTier::TierBm25 as i32, 0);
    assert_eq!(SearchTier::TierSemantic as i32, 1);
    assert_eq!(SearchTier::TierHybrid as i32, 2);
    assert_eq!(SearchTier::TierEntity as i32, 3);

    assert_eq!(RunStatus::StatusPending as i32, 0);
    assert_eq!(RunStatus::StatusRunning as i32, 1);
    assert_eq!(RunStatus::StatusCompleted as i32, 2);
    assert_eq!(RunStatus::StatusFailed as i32, 3);
    assert_eq!(RunStatus::StatusCancelled as i32, 4);

    assert_eq!(SummaryScope::ScopeFile as i32, 0);
    assert_eq!(SummaryScope::ScopeModule as i32, 1);
    assert_eq!(SummaryScope::ScopeProject as i32, 2);
}

    let client_type =

}

You are updating **documentation only** for the `arlm` (Agnostic RLM) Rust workspace at `/projects/my/ai-guides/TMP/agnostic-rlm-rs`, after a large refactor (plans 017/018/019/020). You must NOT modify any `.rs` source, `Cargo.toml`, `.seeds/`, or run git commits. Only edit Markdown / doc files.

## SHARED CONTEXT (read before starting — mandatory)
- `/projects/my/ai-guides/TMP/agnostic-rlm-rs/AGENTS.md` — architecture, crate responsibilities, conventions.
- `/projects/my/ai-guides/TMP/agnostic-rlm-rs/plan/019-cli-consolidation.md` — the CLI/legacy-removal plan (especially the "Superfície de CLI alvo" table, sections B/C/D/E, and F justifications).
- `/projects/my/ai-guides/TMP/agnostic-rlm-rs/plan/020-config-consolidation.md` — config consolidation (server.toml, user 2-scope config, pure gRPC client).

## WHAT CHANGED (the new reality to document)
**Philosophy:** on-demand, agent-agnostic, server-side processing. No recursive RLM loop, no server LLM. The server is a pure data plane (index/search/query/memory/history) reached over gRPC; the client is a pure gRPC client that only uses the USER's local LLM for digest (query `-qa`) and summarize (persist).

**New CLI surface:**
- `arlm init [--index] [--no-index]` — scaffolds `<project>/.arlm.toml` (gitignored) + runs index.
- `arlm index` — streams raw file text to the server (server chunks + embeds).
- `arlm search` — hybrid BM25+semantic (server-side).
- `arlm query` — on-demand QA; `-qa` digests via user LLM; `--cache-id` does a deterministic 1:1 lookup. Emits a `cache_id`.
- `arlm memory` (admin) — `list`/`get`/`invalidate`/`cleanup` (maps to ListMemory/GetCache/InvalidateCache/TriggerMaintenance; admin-gated on server).
- `arlm persist <response_id>` — writes `wiki/<yyyymmddhhmm>_<title>.md` (fixed structure: Response ID/Generated/Model/Project/Provenance + Summary/Key Findings/Related) using the user's LLM.
- `arlm history [--limit] [--user]` — per-user query history (server-scoped by refresh token).
- `arlm server` — hosts the gRPC/MCP data-plane server (no `/run` endpoint).
- **REMOVED commands:** `run`, `context`, `session`, `status`, `cost`, `cancel`, `checkpoints`, `restore-page`, `wiki`, `consolidate` (CLI), `decay` (CLI), `entities` (CLI). The server-side maintenance (consolidate/decay) is now cron + admin RPC `TriggerMaintenance` (and `arlm-server admin consolidate`).

**Config (plan 020):**
- `server.toml` is a HOST file mounted into the container (e.g. `./server.toml:/etc/arlm/server.toml`); read from `ARLM_SERVER_CONFIG` or default `/etc/arlm/server.toml`. It owns ALL data-plane config: `listen_addr`, `data_dir`, `tls_cert`/`tls_key`, `[embedder]` (chunk `max_tokens`/`overlap_tokens`), `[qa_cache]`, `[maintenance] { interval_secs, decay_score_floor }`. **No `[llm]`** (server is LLM-free).
- User config is 2-scope: global `~/.arlm/arlm.toml` (`[auth]` global-only with username+refresh_token, `[llm]` user AI, `[server] addr`) and local `.arlm.toml` (project overrides + `[project]`). Granular per-field merge (local > global). `[auth]` is global-only and ignored if present locally. Break-total: legacy `~/.arlm/config.toml` / `.arlm/config.toml` are NOT read.

## YOUR TASK — F9: update docs to reflect the above

Find all doc files that reference removed concepts and update them: search the repo (use `rg`/glob) for `summarizer`, `arlm run`, `Run`, `recursive RLM`, `recursive language model`, `context` (as a command), `consolidate`/`decay`/`entities` as CLI commands, server `[llm]`, legacy `config.toml`, `session`, `checkpoints`, `status`/`cost`/`cancel` commands. 3. Do NOT invent new architecture — only reflect what the code now does. If a doc describes a feature that still exists (hybrid search, QA-Cache, auth refresh tokens, admin role), keep it.

<content>
1: # arlm — Agnostic RLM
2: 
3: Recursive Language Model CLI/HTTP para processamento massivo de codebases. Indexa arquivos, armazena embeddings e realiza busca híbrida (BM25 + semântica) para fornecer contexto a agentes LLM.
4: 
5: **Agent-agnostic:** qualquer agente (OPencode, Cursor, Aider, Pi) pode consumir sua saída.
6: 
7: ## Arquitetura (server-first)
8: 
9: O `arlm` é **server-first** (ver `plan/016-server-first-architecture.md`): o
10: `arlm-server` é o processo primário e de longa duração, e o `arlm-cli` é um
11: cliente gRPC fino que se comunica com ele.
12: 
13: ```
14: ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
15: │                  arlm-server  (long-running)           │
16: │  SQLite (pool r2d2) + LanceDB (vetorial) + summarizer  │
17: │  expõe API gRPC (tonic + prost, via arlm-proto)       │
18: └───────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────┘
19:                               │ gRPC (protobuf, TLS opcional)
20: ┌───────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────┐
21: │  arlm-cli  (thin gRPC client)  ── index/search/run…   │
22: └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
23: ```
24: 
25: - **9 crates**: `arlm-cli`, `arlm-core`, `arlm-storage`, `arlm-search`,
26:   `arlm-embedding`, `arlm-memory`, `arlm-llm`, `arlm-proto`, `arlm-server`.
27: - Conexão tipada por `arlm-proto` (trait `ArlmService`, 24 RPCs).
28: - **Sem LLM no servidor para o QA-Cache (plan 017):** o servidor faz só
29:   embedding + SQLite + usearch e devolve respostas digeridas; a síntese LLM roda
30:   no **client** (LLM do usuário). Inclui cache semântico com `cache_id` estável
31:   (anti-drift), stale por hash de chunk e invalidação manual (Stale/Delete + raio).
32: - **Auth (plan 018):** refresh-tokens + sessões de curta duração com roles
33:   `Admin`/`NonAdmin`; RPCs mutantes exigem `Bearer` válido.
34: - **Sem LLM para index/search/context/query** (embeddings usam
35:   *fallback hash* determinístico e offline por padrão; BGE-M3 via `candle`
36:   é opcional). LLM é *opt-in* (`--llm`) apenas para `run`/summarize.
37: - O CLI também roda **localmente** (sem `--server`), operando diretamente
38:   sobre `~/.arlm` (retrocompatibilidade).
39: 
40: ## Instalação
41: 
42: ```bash
43: # Binários (server + client)
44: cargo build --release            # → ./target/release/arlm e ./target/release/arlm-server
45: 
46: # Ou via script de instalação
47: ./install.sh                     # instala arlm e cria ~/.arlm/config.toml
48: ```
49: 
50: ### Requisitos
51: 
52: - Rust 1.85+ (edition 2024)
53: - `protoc` (protobuf-compiler) para gRPC/`arlm-proto`
54: - `protobuf-devel` para includes do protobuf
55: 
56: ## Uso Rápido
57: 
58: ```bash
59: # Indexar um projeto
60: arlm index ./meu-projeto
61: 
62: # Indexar com ignore patterns
63: arlm index ./meu-projeto --ignore "dist/" --ignore "*.log"
64: 
65: # Indexar com watch mode (reindexa automaticamente)
66: arlm index ./meu-projeto --watch
67: 
68: # Buscar no projeto
69: arlm search "auth middleware"
70: 
71: # Buscar em todos os projetos indexados
72: arlm search "config handling" --all
73: 
74: # Buscar com tier específico
75: arlm search "error handling" --tier entity
76: 
77: # Buscar com limite de tokens
78: arlm search "database schema" --max-tokens 4000
79: 
80: # Construir contexto para um agente
81: arlm context "fix login bug" --all --tier auto --max-tokens 8000
82: 
83: # Ver status dos projetos
84: arlm status
85: 
86: # Servidor HTTP (legacy/local, opcional)
87: arlm serve --port 8080
88: ```
89: 
90: ## Modo Servidor (gRPC)
91: 
92: O modelo recomendado é separar servidor e cliente:
93: 
94: ```bash
95: # 1) Inicia o servidor (long-running) — dono do estado
96: arlm-server up                                   # escuta 127.0.0.1:50051
97: docker compose -f docker-compose.server.yml up -d   # ou via Docker
98: 
99: # 2) O cliente CLI conecta por gRPC
100: arlm --server 127.0.0.1:50051 index ./meu-projeto
101: arlm --server 127.0.0.1:50051 search "auth middleware"
102: arlm --server 127.0.0.1:50051 context "fix login bug"
103: arlm --server 127.0.0.1:50051 status
104: ```
105: 
106: Sem `--server`, o CLI opera localmente sobre `~/.arlm`. O endereço do servidor
107: também é resolvido por `~/.arlm/config.toml` (`[server].addr`) ou
108: `ARLM_SERVER_ADDR`.
109: 
110: ## Comandos CLI
111: 
112: | Comando | Descrição |
113: |---------|-----------|
114: | `arlm index <dir>` | Indexa um diretório (chunking + metadados) |
115: | `arlm search <query>` | Busca híbrida BM25 + semântica |
116: | `arlm context <task>` | Monta contexto para agente LLM |
117: | `arlm run <task>` | Executa RLM recursivo (requer `--llm`) |
118: | `arlm query <question>` | Pergunta com análise LLM (`--qa` usa o QA-Cache, `--cache-id <id>` lookup direto) |
119: | `arlm cache invalidate --cache-id <id>` | Invalida entrada do QA-Cache (Stale/Delete + raio) |
120: | `arlm status` | Lista projetos indexados |
121: | `arlm history` | Histórico de consultas |
122: | `arlm session create/list` | Sessões multi-turn |
123: | `arlm consolidate` | Dedup e cleanup de memória |
124: | `arlm persist` | Salva resultados como wiki pages |
125: | `arlm decay` | Salience decay em chunks antigos |
126: | `arlm serve` | Servidor HTTP/MCP |
127: 
128: ## Flags Principais
129: 
130: ### `arlm index`
131: 
132: | Flag | Descrição | Default |
133: |------|-----------|---------|
134: | `--chunk-size <N>` | Tamanho máximo por chunk (tokens) | 512 |
135: | `--ignore <pattern>` | Padrões de ignore (glob, múltiplos) | `.env`, `.env.*`, `*.pem`, `*.key` |
136: | `--watch` / `-w` | Reindexa automaticamente a cada mudança | off |
137: 
138: ### `arlm search`
139: 
140: | Flag | Descrição | Default |
141: |------|-----------|---------|
142: | `--top-k <N>` | Número de resultados | 10 |
143: | `--all` / `-a` | Busca em todos os projetos indexados | off |
144: | `--tier <tier>` | `fts`, `entity`, `vector`, `auto` | auto |
145: | `--max-tokens <N>` | Limite de tokens na saída (0=ilimitado) | 8000 |
146: | `--file-pattern <pat>` | Filtro por nome de arquivo | — |
147: | `--min-score <f>` | Score mínimo | — |
148: 
149: ### `arlm context`
150: 
151: | Flag | Descrição | Default |
152: |------|-----------|---------|
153: | `--top-k <N>` | Número de resultados | 10 |
154: | `--all` / `-a` | Busca em todos os projetos | off |
155: | `--tier <tier>` | `fts`, `entity`, `vector`, `auto` | auto |
156: | `--max-tokens <N>` | Limite de tokens na saída (0=ilimitado) | 8000 |
157: 
158: ### `arlm run`
159: 
160: | Flag | Descrição | Default |
161: |------|-----------|---------|
162: | `--llm` | Habilita modo LLM (obrigatório) | — |
163: | `--backend <name>` | Backend: openai, anthropic, ollama, gemini, deepseek, mimo | ollama |
164: | `--model <name>` | Modelo a usar | — |
165: | `--depth <N>` | Profundidade máxima de recursão | 3 |
166: | `--max-nodes <N>` | Número máximo de nós | 50 |
167: | `--concurrency <N>` | Limite de concorrência | 4 |
168: | `--max-budget <USD>` | Orçamento máximo em USD | 1.0 |
169: | `--live` | Renderiza árvore RLM em tempo real | off |
170: 
171: ## Formatos de Saída
172: 
173: Todos os comandos suportam 4 formatos:
174: 
175: ```bash
176: arlm search "query" --format json      # JSON estruturado
177: arlm search "query" --format tree      # Tabela colorida (default)
178: arlm search "query" --format markdown  # Markdown formatado
179: arlm search "query" --format prompt    # Prompt para LLM
180: ```
181: 
182: ## Arquitetura de Dados
183: 
184: ### Single Database
185: 
186: Todos os projetos compartilham `~/.arlm/knowledge.db`:
187: 
188: ```
189: ~/.arlm/
190: ├── knowledge.db          # SQLite (WAL, FTS5, metadados)
191: ├── knowledge.db-wal      # WAL journal
192: └── vectors.lance/        # LanceDB (HNSW vetorial, 1024-dim BGE-M3)
193: ```
194: 
195: Cada projeto é um `buffer` na tabela `buffers` com UUIDv7 único. Isolamento por `buffer_id` em todas as tabelas.
196: 
197: ### Busca Híbrida (Tiers)
198: 
199: | Tier | Componentes | Requisitos |
200: |------|-------------|------------|
201: | `fts` | BM25 (FTS5) | Nenhum |
202: | `entity` | BM25 + regex entities | Nenhum |
203: | `vector` | BM25 + entity + embeddings | Modelo BGE-M3 |
204: | `llm_rerank` | Tier 2 + LLM reranker | Backend LLM |
205: 
206: ### Token Budget
207: 
208: `--max-tokens` controla o tamanho da saída. chunks são mantidos/truncados por score decrescente até caber no budget:
209: 
210: ```bash
211: # Contexto enxuto (4k tokens)
212: arlm context "auth" --max-tokens 4000
213: 
214: # Contexto completo (ilimitado)
215: arlm context "auth" --max-tokens 0
216: ```
217: 
218: ## HTTP API (legacy/local)
219: 
220: > O servidor canônico é o `arlm-server` sobre **gRPC** (ver Modo Servidor acima).
221: > `arlm serve` é um servidor HTTP/MCP **local/opcional** mantido para
222: > retrocompatibilidade e integração MCP.
223: 
224: ```bash
225: arlm serve --port 8080
226: ```
227: 
228: | Endpoint | Método | Descrição |
229: |----------|--------|-----------|
230: | `GET /health` | GET | Health check |
231: | `GET /metrics` | GET | Métricas Prometheus |
232: | `POST /search` | POST | Busca no projeto |
233: | `POST /context` | POST | Monta contexto |
234: | `POST /run` | POST | Executa RLM recursivo |
235: | `POST /index` | POST | Indexa diretório |
236: | `GET /status` | GET | Lista projetos |
237: | `POST /mcp` | POST | Endpoint MCP (opcional) |
238: 
239: ## MCP (Model Context Protocol)
240: 
241: ```bash
242: arlm serve --mcp  # Habilita endpoint /mcp
243: ```
244: 
245: Ferramentas disponíveis:
246: - `rlm_context` — Busca contexto para uma tarefa
247: - `rlm_search` — Busca código com BM25 híbrido
248: 
249: ## Docker (server-first)
250: 
251: A imagem canônica é o `arlm-server` (gRPC):
252: 
253: ```bash
254: # Build da imagem do servidor
255: docker build -t arlm-server:latest -f Dockerfile.server .
256: 
257: # Subir o servidor (porta 50051, volume de dados persistido)
258: docker compose -f docker-compose.server.yml up -d
259: 
260: # CLI (no host) conecta por gRPC
261: arlm --server 127.0.0.1:50051 index /workspace
262: arlm --server 127.0.0.1:50051 search "query"
263: ```
264: 
265: O `docker-compose.server.yml` monta o volume `arlm-server-data` em `/data`
266: (configure `ARLM_DATA_DIR=/data`) e expõe `50051` (bind `0.0.0.0` via
267: `ARLM_SERVER_ADDR`). O healthcheck usa `arlm-server status`.
268: 
269: > **Indexação em Docker (client-streaming):** o servidor **não** lê o filesystem
270: > do cliente. A CLI descobre e lê os arquivos localmente e faz *stream* dos bytes
271: > para o servidor via gRPC (`IndexProject` é client-streaming). Portanto **não é
272: > necessário montar o projeto no container** — basta apontar a CLI para o caminho
273: > local:
274: >
275: > ```bash
276: > arlm --server 127.0.0.1:50051 index /caminho/do/projeto
277: > ```
278: >
279: > Por padrão, caminhos sensíveis/ignorados (`.env`, `.vscode`, `.github`,
280: > `.gitlab`, `.zed`, vendors, …) **não** são enviados. Use `--force-include=`
281: > para enviá-los explicitamente.
282: 
283: ## Desenvolvimento
284: 
285: ```bash
286: # Build dev
287: cargo build
288: 
289: # Rodar testes
290: cargo test --workspace
291: 
292: # Lint e format
293: cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings
294: cargo fmt -- --check
295: 
296: # Benchmarks
297: cargo bench
298: ```
299: 
300: ## Configuração de Build
301: 
302: `.cargo/config.toml` (incluído no repositório):
303: 
304: ```toml
305: [build]
306: jobs = 8
307: rustflags = ["-C", "target-cpu=native"]
308: 
309: [env]
310: PROTOC = "/usr/bin/protoc"
311: ```
312: 
313: ## Licença
314: 
315: MIT OR Apache-2.0

(End of file - total 315 lines)
</content>

1: # AGENTS.md — arlm (Agnostic RLM)
2: 
3: ## Project Overview
4: 
5: `arlm` is a Rust CLI tool implementing RLM (Recursive Language Model) for processing massive codebases. It indexes files, stores embeddings, and performs hybrid search (BM25 + semantic) to provide context for LLM-based agents. The CLI is agent-agnostic — any AI agent (OPencode, Cursor, Pi, Aider) can consume its output.
6: 
7: **Architecture:** 7-crate Cargo workspace with unidirectional data flow:
8: ```
9: arlm-cli → arlm-core → arlm-llm, arlm-search, arlm-memory
10:                            ↓
11: arlm-search → arlm-storage (SQLite + LanceDB), arlm-embedding
12:                            ↓
13: arlm-storage → rusqlite (FTS5/BM25), lancedb (HNSW vectors)
14: arlm-embedding → candle (BGE-M3), memmap2, rayon
15: ```
16: 
17: **Tech Stack:**
18: - Rust 2024 (edition = "2024", rust-version = "1.85")
19: - SQLite via rusqlite (bundled, WAL, FTS5 for BM25)
20: - LanceDB for vector storage (HNSW index)
21: - candle-core + candle-transformers for BGE-M3 embeddings (INT8 quantized)
22: - memmap2 for zero-copy file I/O
23: - Rayon for parallel chunking
24: - zstd for text compression
25: - clap (derive) for CLI
26: - tokio for async (LLM calls), Rayon for CPU-bound work
27: - mimalloc as global allocator
28: 
29: ## Code Conventions
30: 
31: ### Rust Style
32: - **Lints:** `clippy::pedantic = "warn"`, `clippy::unwrap_used = "deny"`, `clippy::expect_used = "deny"`, `clippy::panic = "deny"`, `unsafe_code = "forbid"` (only explicit `unsafe` blocks with justification)
33: - **Error handling:** `anyhow` for application code, `thiserror` for library types. NEVER use `.unwrap()` or `.expect()` in production code. Use `?` operator and `Result<T, E>`.
34: - **Naming:** snake_case for functions/variables, PascalCase for types, SCREAMING_SNAKE for constants
35: - **Imports:** Use explicit imports, avoid `use foo::*`
36: - **Patterns:** Builder for complex config, Newtype for domain types, Repository pattern for data access via traits
37: - **Async:** tokio runtime for LLM calls; `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` for CPU/DB-bound work (never block async workers with sync I/O)
38: - **Concurrency:** `AtomicU32`/`AtomicU64` for counters (no Mutex for simple state), `futures::stream::buffer_unordered` for fan-out with real concurrency limits, `parking_lot` for Mutex/RwLock when needed
39: - **Memory:** `Cow<'a, str>` for zero-copy chunking, `Arc<str>` for shared immutable IDs (cheap clone in broadcast channels), pre-allocate with `Vec::with_capacity`
40: - **Tip optimization:** `CompletionRequest.system` as `Option<Cow<'static, str>>` (zero-alloc for static prompts)
41: 
42: ### File Organization
43: ```
44: src/
45: ├── lib.rs           # Public API
46: ├── error.rs         # Error types (thiserror)
47: ├── types.rs         # Domain types
48: └── <module>.rs       # Feature modules
49: 
50: tests/
51: └── integration/     # Cross-crate integration tests
52: 
53: benches/
54: └── *.rs             # Criterion benchmarks (ingestion, search, rlm_loop)
55: ```
56: 
57: ### Crate Responsibilities
58: | Crate | Role |
59: |-------|------|
60: | `arlm-cli` | Binary entry point, clap parsing, output formatting |
61: | `arlm-core` | RLM engine (planner/solver/synthesizer), guardrails, budget |
62: | `arlm-storage` | SQLite (metadata, FTS5) + LanceDB (vectors), dual transactions |
63: | `arlm-embedding` | Chunking strategies (code/text/markdown), candle BGE-M3 embeddings |
64: | `arlm-search` | Hybrid search (BM25 + semantic + RRF fusion) |
65: | `arlm-memory` | Multi-project memory, knowledge base, sessions, trajectories |
66: | `arlm-llm` | LLM backend abstraction (OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, Gemini) |
67: 
68: ## Testing Strategy
69: 
70: ### Test Types and Commands
71: ```bash

73: cargo test
74: 
75: # Integration tests only
76: cargo test --test integration_test
77:

80:

83: 
84: # Benchmarks (Criterion)
85: cargo bench
86: 
87: # Lint and format (MUST run before committing)
88: cargo fmt -- --check
89: cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings
90: 
91: # Code coverage
92: cargo install cargo-tarpaulin
93: cargo tarpaulin --workspace
94: ```
95: 
96: ### Test Organization
97: - **Unit tests:** Inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in same file as code
98: - **Integration tests:** `tests/integration/` directory, test public API only
99: - **Benchmarks:** `benches/` with Criterion (ingestion.rs, search.rs, rlm_loop.rs)
100: - **Doc tests:** `/// # Examples` on public functions
101: 
102: ### Test Guidelines
103: 1. Every public function MUST have at least one test
104: 2. Use `tempfile` for filesystem/DB tests (auto-cleanup)
105: 3. Use `proptest` for property-based testing (chunking, search scoring)
106: 4. Mock external dependencies via trait objects (no network in unit tests)
107: 5. Test error paths with `#[should_panic]` or `Result<(), E>` pattern
108: 6. Benchmarks for hot paths: chunking, embedding, search, RRF fusion
109: 7. Name tests descriptively: `test_bm25_search_empty_index` not `test1`
110: 8. Use `#[ignore = "expensive"]` for slow tests (large file ingestion, full model load)
111: 
112: ### CI Requirements
113: Every PR must pass:
114: - `cargo fmt -- --check`
115: - `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings`
116: - `cargo test --workspace`
117: - `cargo test --doc`
118: - `cargo audit` (security)
119: 
120: ## Performance Guidelines
121: 
122: ### Key Decisions
123: | Component | Choice | Why |
124: |-----------|--------|-----|
125: | File I/O | memmap2 | Zero-copy, OS-managed paging |
126: | CPU parallelism | Rayon (par_iter) | 100% core utilization for chunking/embedding |
127: | Search | SQLite FTS5 (BM25) + LanceDB HNSW (semantic) | Each specialist, fused via RRF |
128: | State | SQLite WAL | Transactional, crash-safe, concurrent readers |
129: | Embedding | Candle BGE-M3 INT8 | Local inference, no Python/API dependency |
130: | Concurrency | Sync + channels + Rayon | Zero async overhead for CLI operations |
131: | Build | lto=true, codegen-units=1 | Minimum binary, maximum machine code optimization |
132: | Allocator | mimalloc | Less fragmentation than glibc for ingestion workloads |
133: 
134: ### SQLite Optimizations (applied on connection open)
135: ```sql
136: PRAGMA page_size=8192;            -- BEFORE any write
137: PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;
138: PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL;
139: PRAGMA mmap_size=268435456;       -- 256MB
140: PRAGMA cache_size=-65536;         -- 64MB
141: PRAGMA temp_store=MEMORY;
142: PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000;
143: PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint=2000;
144: PRAGMA journal_size_limit=33554432; -- 32MB cap
145: PRAGMA hard_heap_limit=104857600;   -- 100MB limit
146: PRAGMA optimize;
147: ```
148: 
149: ### Performance Targets
150: - Search latency: < 100ms (typical ~21ms)
151: - Ingestion: ~30s for 10k files (~100MB)
152: - Memory: bounded by `hard_heap_limit` (100MB)
153: 
154: ## Security Guidelines
155: 
156: 1. **No secrets in code:** Never hardcode API keys, tokens, or passwords. Use env vars or config files excluded from git.
157: 2. **SQL injection:** Always use parameterized queries (`?1`, `?2` or named params). Never format SQL strings.
158: 3. **Input validation:** Validate all external inputs (file paths, user queries, LLM responses).
159: 4. **unsafe code:** `forbid` at workspace level. Each `unsafe` block must have a `// SAFETY:` comment justifying the invariant.
160: 5. **Dependency audit:** `cargo audit` in CI. No known vulnerabilities allowed.
161: 6. **File permissions:** DB files and config should be owner-only (0600).
162: 7. **FTS5 injection:** Sanitize user queries before passing to FTS5 MATCH. Escape special FTS5 characters.
163:

4:Pipeline de chunking e geração de embeddings para o `arlm`: divide arquivos em chunks (code/text/markdown/recursive) e os converte em vetores densos para busca semântica.
